author: Ariadna Wdowiak
title: El Servicio Penitenciario Federal es responsable directo de las condiciones inhumanas
content:
11 de febrero de 2026: El hombre que ríe acaba de arrastrar más de cincuenta metros a un fotoperiodista enceguecido por el gas pimienta en spray a quemarropas que le echó Gendarmería desde el otro lado de las vallas sobre la cara


Milton Tolomeo y Eneas Gallo no son protagonistas de una zaga de aventuras ni de una serie policial. No son héroes mitológicos. Son dos trabajadores precarizados que militaron y participaron de la cosa pública siempre que pudieron y lo sintieron de esa manera. Pero hoy siguen en prisión preventiva en el penal federal de Marcos Paz por su participación en las protestas del 11 de febrero contra la reforma laboral, frente al Congreso. Tolomeo fue detenido el 15 de febrero. Y Gallo, el 18 de marzo. El Ministerio de Seguridad denunció de terrorismo a los responsables de los incidentes, y el fiscal Carlos Stornelli pidió aplicar el artículo 41 quinquies, que duplica las penas, pero el juez Gonzalo Rúa rechazó ese agravante al dictar la preventiva. Hoy, ambos esperan un juicio oral sin fecha. Desde el 8 de noviembre, Tolomeo hace huelga de hambre en reclamo de su libertad, de agua potable y alimentos, y de mejoras en las condiciones de detención. CORREPI y la Gremial de Abogadas y Abogados piden el cierre de la causa, mientras el Gobierno sostiene que hubo una acción organizada para desestabilizar el orden institucional.


Texto y fotos Andrés Manrique (

ANRed).


 


23 de septiembre de 2026: un Carlston.


El miércoles 11 de febrero, mientras el Senado aprobaba la reforma laboral, una multitud se movilizó frente al Congreso en una marcha convocada por la CGT y distintos sectores sociales y políticos.

El operativo de seguridad, según el Gobierno, terminó con 71 detenidos

. 51 detenciones estuvieron a cargo de fuerzas federales, y 20 las ejecutó la Policía de la Ciudad. La fiscalía fue liberando a la mayoría de los y las detenidas los días siguientes. Entre otros, se detuvieron a personas en situación de calle, a kilómetros de los hechos, sin la más mínima prueba y a más  de un mes de la movilización. Pero quedaron algunos casos por definir. Milton Tolomeo y Eneas Gallo, no fueron apresados ese día, ni cerca del Congreso.


11 de febrero de 2026: reforma laboral


El 11 de febrero, mientras Senadores aprobaba una flexibilización nueva para el trabajo y una forma más radicalizada de precarizarlo, afuera del Congreso

 las fuerzas represivas estuvieron durante más de tres horas

 disparándole a manifestantes, a familias, a vecinos y a fotorreporteros con postas de goma, escopetas Byrna a gas comprimido, dos hidrantes, gas pimienta y granadas de gas lacrimógeno. En ese escenario bélico sostenido por

decisión unilateral del ejecutivo

, unos manifestantes arrojaron unas molotovs del otro lado de las vallas.


Los derechos no se consiguieron pidiendo por favor


La causa


Milton Tolomeo


Milton fue detenido el 15 de febrero en su trabajo

, donde era operario de maestranza. Además, es masajista deportivo, oficio que ejercía por las tardes. Dicho en sus propias palabras, es una «persona que no soporta las injusticias y que siempre creyó que es posible cambiarlas, que siempre hay que involucrarse cuando éstas suceden y no resignarse ni mirar para otro lado», lo que lo llevó a movilizarse contra la reforma laboral el 11 de febrero de 2026.


Entre el 12 y el 13 de febrero, Alejandra Monteoliva -Ministra de Seguridad-, anunció que su cartera denunciaría por terrorismo a los responsables de los incidentes. Dijo que habían realizado una acción organizada para desestabilizar el orden institucional. En esa campaña, el Ministerio difundió un video con cuatro sospechosos y una lista de 17 implicados: Milton Tolomeo no figuraba en el video nu en la lista.

A Monteoliva se la denunció penalmente junto a jefes del operativo por incumplimiento de deberes

. Tolomeo fue detenido a mediados de febrero y el Gobierno lo estigmatizó, difundiendo su cara, con el rótulo de “anarquista de la Molotov”. El domingo 15 de febrero, la ministra salió a celebrar por redes: “Dijimos que lo íbamos a encontrar y lo encontramos” No tenía pruebas suficientes.


9 de septiembre de 2026


La Coordinadora Contra la Represión Policial e Institucional (CORREPI), quienes asumieron su defensa, explican que se lo acusa por los delitos de resistencia a la autoridad, intimidación pública y tenencia de material incendiario. Los primeros dos delitos son los habituales aplicados a manifestantes, como parte de la criminalización de la …

author: Martha Teodoro
title: Faith groups stand with detained protesters
content:
Police arrest protesters, including members of alternative media and student publications, in Sucat, Muntinlupa City, on November 15, 2026. The protesters are part of a delegation who are set to join a protest in Manila against Pax Silica and US President Donald Trump's visit. Photo from Bayan Laguna

“What we are fighting for is engagement and trade grounded in equality, respect for sovereignty, and mutual benefit.”

Ecumenical councils, Christian youth, and Catholic bishops denounce the US-led critical minerals deal and state crackdown ahead of the 49th ASEAN Summit.

More than 300 protesters were detained at Camp Bagong Diwa of the Philippine National Police in Taguig City following aggressive police dispersals on November 15. Police dispersed the Southern Tagalog Lakbayan protest caravan in Sucat, Parañaque and Muntinlupa while separate clashes happened at Liwasang Bonifacio in Manila.

The protests targeted the proposed signing of the Pax Silica framework during US President Donald Trump’s visit to Manila. Meanwhile, Protestant, ecumenical, and Roman Catholic leaders warned that they will sacrifice Philippine sovereignty, ancestral lands, and public utilities to US geopolitical and corporate interests.

In a pastoral statement issued Nov. 12, 2026, the National Council of Churches in the Philippines (NCCP) condemned both the economic terms of Pax Silica and the Marcos Jr. administration’s suppression of constitutionally guaranteed freedoms. “In a display of servility to the US, the government of Pres. Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is rolling out the red carpet, spending billions of pesos on lavish preparations while ordinary Filipinos struggle with poverty, rising prices, and economic hardship. In true ‘Imeldific’ fashion, authorities are clearing Manila’s streets of vendors and urban poor communities to conceal poverty from visiting dignitaries. Worse, they have imposed a ban on protests, suppressing constitutionally guaranteed freedoms.”

Signed by NCCP Chairperson The Most Rev. Brent Harry W. Alawas and General Secretary Minnie Anne Mata-Calub, the statement warned that Pax Silica’s push for critical minerals, semiconductor supply chains and artificial intelligence data centers places the country squarely in the crosshairs of superpower conflict. “More alarming is the prospect of signing the lopsided Pax Silica agreement during Trump’s visit. Designed to secure US access to critical technology supply chains, including artificial intelligence and critical minerals, the agreement places Philippine resources and sovereignty at the service of US strategic interests amid its rivalry with China. Pax Silica threatens to intensify large-scale mining, resource extraction, and data center development, resulting in environmental destruction and the displacement of Indigenous Peoples and farmers.”

Meanwhile, youth leaders from the United Church of Christ in the Philippines—Middle Luzon Jurisdictional Area Christian Youth Fellowship (UCCP MLJA-CYF) echoed this call in a manifesto titled “Kapayapaang Para sa Sangnilikha, Hindi Para sa Imperyalistang Bansa!” and warned that communities in Central Luzon will bear the brunt of the project’s ecological and social costs. “While we recognize the importance of technological and economic development, such progress must never come at the expense of Philippine sovereignty, the welfare of the people, the protection of creation, the rights of Indigenous Peoples on the margins, and peace not only in Luzon but across the entire Philippines… What we are fighting for is engagement and trade grounded in equality, respect for sovereignty, and mutual benefit—not the domination of a few and entanglement in conflicts that should never become the burden of the Filipino people.”

Caritas Philippines president and San Carlos Bishop Gerardo Alminaza said in August that the proposed Tarlac development zone directly threatens Indigenous communities and vital local resources. “The site is not empty land. It is home to Aeta Indigenous families, farmers, and rural communities whose rights and livelihoods must come before corporate and geopolitical interests. Pax Silica must not become another pretext for land conversion, displacement, destructive mining, or the diversion of electricity and water away from public needs.”

title: Demo 1×1 Flyer für Gen-Z Proteste
content:
Wir haben zu oft gesehen wie Menschen sich filmen, unvermummt Pyro zünden oder ohne Handschuhe Steine auflesen. Daher haben wir einen kleinen Demo 1×1 Flyer geschrieben.


Druckt den Flyer vor den Protesten und verteilt ihn auf den Demos. Ihr könnt auch Einweghandschuhe auf der Demo verteilen (am besten sollten Menschen 2 Paare übereinander ziehen). Animiert und zeigt Menschen auch wie man sich mit einem Tshirts vermummt, wenn es Action gibt.


Wichtig: Ergänzt die lokale Nummer des Ermittlungsausschuss vor dem Drucken. Schreibt denen auch und fragt, ob sie an dem Tag aktiv sind.


Druckt nur in linken Läden und sagt den Menschen vorher, dass ihr solche brisanten Sachen drucken wollt. Am besten Face-to-Face, notfalls mit verschlüsselter Mail anschreiben. Normale Drucker speichern die Text, die mit ihnen gedruckt wurden.


Druckt nur DNA frei. Das bedeutet habt recht frisch gewaschene lange Klamotten an. Kauft neues Papier und neue Tüten zum Transport der Flyer. Vorher nochmal alle Arbeitsutensilien und Unterlagen mit Chlor reinigen. Beim Drucken nicht in Gesicht, Haare oder auf eure Klamotten fassen und Einmalhandschuhe tragen.


Am besten helfen mehrere Menschen beim verteilen auf der Demo. Wenn am Anfang noch nicht alle schwarz angezogen sind, in bunt aber recht unkenntlich die Flyer verteilen. Nur mit Handschuhen verteilen. Möglicherweise auch weitergeben lassen.


Demo 1×1


Redet nur mit Personen über Aktionen, die mitmachen. Ihr wisst nie wer mithört oder sich im schlimmsten Fall verplappert. Redet nur face-to-face ohne Handys.


Seid am besten zu zweit auf der Demo, organisiert euch evtl. in einer größeren Gruppe. Redet vorher über alle möglichen Aktionen und ob ihr die Konsequenzen, wie Knast, ertragen könnt.


Überlegt euch ein Handzeichen und ein Wort (z.B. „Backofen“) das ihr ruft, wenn ihr euch auf der Demo verliert. Ruft auf keinen Fall eure echten Namen.


Nehmt keine Handys oder Smart-Watch mit und macht keine Fotos oder Videos (potenzielle Beweismittel). Solltet ihr euer Handy dabeihaben, schaltet es jetzt aus!


Keine Gespräche über Politik, die Demo oder Straftaten bei An- und Abreise.


Bei Vorkontrollen, nett sagen, dass ihr einkaufen geht. Ansonsten nur angeben: Name, Adresse, Familienstand, Staatsangehörigkeit und Berufsbezeichnung. Keine Arbeitsstelle oder Name eurer Schule oder Uni.


Keine Straftaten ohne Handschuhe und Vermummung, sowie in Klamotten die ihr im Alltag anhabt. Fingerabdrücke, Kleidung und DNA sind Beweismaterial.


Vermummung ist strafbar. Wechselt euer Outfit (nicht nur die Vermummung) nur für die Zeit, in der ihr unerkenntlich sein wollt. Zieht euch nur in Menschenmassen, oder Gebüschen um, wenn ihr nicht gefilmt werdet und geht dann weg.


Cops versuchen während und nach der Demo Menschen festzunehmen. Auch Zivicops ohne Uniform folgen Menschen in der Demo. Wenn euch Menschen folgen, sagt ihnen nett & bestimmt, dass sie gehen sollen.


Cops beklagen, dass (brennende) Barrikaden auf den Straßen ihnen erschweren Menschen mit Autos zu verfolgen und wenn einzelne Streifen von mehreren Menschen angegriffen werden, sie erst mehr Kräfte zusammenzuziehen müssen.


Bei Festnahme: Keine Aussage oder Unterschrift! Du hast das Recht auf einen Anruf – ruf den EA an! Keine Mitarbeitspflicht; also nicht laufen, reden oder vermummen für Videos/Bilder. Grimassen schneiden bei Fotos. Bei DNA-Abnahme Beschluss von Richter*in verlangen. Nach Verhaftung zu Sprechstunde der Roten Hilfe gehen.


Redet niemals über vergangene Straftaten, erst recht nicht mit Handys oder online.


Cops versuchen oft Personen in vermeintlichen Smalltalk zu verwickeln. Am besten einfach ignorieren und nichts sagen, dann könnt ihr euch nicht verplappern.


Nehmt euch Zeit für eine emotionale Nachbesprechung und meldet euch, wenn nötig, bei „Out Of Action“.


Packliste


Personalausweis, Schlüssel, Bahnkarte, Bargeld, Wasserflasche (still)


Telefonnummer des EA (Ermittlungsausschuss) mit Edding auf den Arm schreiben, dieser kontaktiert solidarische Anwält*innen bei Verhaftungen


Nummer des EA:


Cops filmen; versucht euch so anonym wie möglich zu kleiden (keine Rückschlüsse auf Geschlecht, Tattoos, Körperbau, Körperbehaarung…)


blaue Jeans und billige/alte Schuhe


schwarze Überziehjacke ohne Logos (gibt es günstig z.B. bei Decathlon)


schwarzes Shirt fürs Gesicht (legal bei Anreise, illegal beim Tragen)


neue Arbeitshandschuhe in einer Tüte (DNA-frei)

author: Charlotte England
title: Mamdani Abolishes Violent Police Protest Unit
content:
Zohran Mamdani is set to disband a controversial New York City police unit known for using excessive force against protesters.


The New York City mayor laid out plans on Monday to scrap the Strategic Response Group (SRG) in favour of a “civilian-led approach” to policing protest that will put “communication, de-escalation” and “coordination” front and centre.


In a joint statement with the city’s police commissioner, Jessica Tisch, Mamdani said his plan would involve replacing 600 SRG officers with a civilian team and a small specialised police unit to handle protests.


Abolishing the SRG – a highly militarised police unit that became notorious for its violent and racist policing of Black Lives Matter protests – was one of Mamdani’s core 2025 campaign pledges.


Under Mamdani’s reforms, the use of tear gas, rifles, painfully loud noises above 90 decibels and kettling – the surrounding and trapping of protesters, usually before mass arrest – will all be banned.


The mayor also endorsed a council bill that would ban the New York Police Department (NYPD) from ever reviving the SRG or its tactics.


The SRG has been subject to countless misconduct claims over the years. In 2020, Human Rights Watch accused the unit – which handles both protests and counter terrorism – of “serious violations of international human rights law” after officers trapped around 300 peaceful protesters in the Bronx neighbourhood of Mott Haven, then beat and arrested them for breaking a curfew they had been prevented from obeying.


More recently, the SRG has been accused of using excessive force against pro-Palestine and anti-ICE protesters, including punching people who are already pinned to the floor, heavy use of tear gas and mass arrests.


In October, Mamdani ordered the NYPD to conduct its first comprehensive review into use of force in more than a decade, and appointed a new chair of the Civilian Complaint Review Board to increase police accountability.


“New Yorkers exercising their constitutional right to protest should not be met with the same police response as a terrorism threat,” Mamdani said in a statement on Monday. “Protecting New Yorkers’ rights and keeping our communities safe go hand in hand.”


In March, Mamdani created the Mayor’s Office of Community Safety, which he said would strengthen violence prevention, change how the city responds to mental health crises and tackle the root causes of crime. Under the new plans, an unarmed civilian unit within the office, with no powers of arrest, will take the lead in engaging with protesters from 2028.


Within the NYPD, meanwhile, a new First Amendment Support Team (FAST) will respond to protests. Named after the constitutional amendment that protects freedom of speech and the right to peaceful assembly, the team of 30 armed officers will be trained to de-escalate tensions and communicate with demonstrators. They will be backed by a new Patrol Support Division, trained in crowd management, which will either accompany them to protests or be stationed nearby.


Under the new structure, the SRG’s counterterrorism functions will be separated from protest policing and instead consolidated within the NYPD’s Intelligence and Counterterrorism Bureau.

author: Isaac Nellist
title: Protesters condemn state government attacks on Palestine solidarity, free speech
content:
Rallies were held across the country on November 15 to express solidarity with the people of Palestine and oppose repression of speech and protest by all levels of government.

The national day of action against repressive laws was called by Justice for Palestine Magan-djin (JFP) as part of its campaign to repeal the Queensland Liberal National Party government’s laws which criminalise Palestine solidarity slogans including “From the river to the sea” and “Globalise the intifada [uprising]”.

Chris Minns’ NSW Labor government is supporting the Queensland LNP government in the High Court challenge brought by JFP to overturn the laws. Victorian Liberals leader Jess Wilson has vowed to ban the phrase “Globalise the intifada” if elected on November 28.

JFP spokesperson Remah Naji said repression is “uniting our political class” and “thousands of us are united in defending our right to protest genocide”.

“The crimes remain the crime of genocide, the crime of occupation and the crime of apartheid. There is no amount of repression that will distract us from Israel’s crimes or absolve our government from its complicity in them.”

Michael Bradley, from MARQUE Lawyers, which is representing JFP in the High Court Case, said: “Queensland is currently leading the way with its ridiculous law that criminalises mere words, but other states are watching and keen to follow suit.

“It is more critical than ever that a stand is taken — in the courts and on the street — to demand our basic rights: to assemble, to protest and to speak.”

The crack down comes as Israel continues to kill Palestinians in Gaza and the Occupied West Bank, despite the so-called ceasefire. Its strike on the Nasser Hospital on November 12 — the only functioning hospital in Gaza — which killed six people, including surgeon Dr Rizq Shaira and a teenage patient, was condemned by 18 countries for violating international law.

As winter floods, storms and cold descend, many are still left sheltering in tents because of Israel’s restriction of supplies into Gaza. A nine-month-old baby died from hypothermia in Khan Younis in Southern Gaza on November 12 due to exposure to extreme cold.

Israel has killed at least 1610 Palestinians since the so-called ceasefire took effect.

Jonathan Strauss reports that 500 people marched in Magan-djin/Brisbane behind a large banner featuring the banned slogan “From the river to the sea”, a frequent chant of the Palestine solidarity movement.

The other banned slogan, “Globalise the intifada”, was not commonly used at Palestine rallies in Magan-djin, but expresses a desire for international support for the Palestinian people.

Anti-Zionist Jewish activist Stephen Heydt told the crowd that “kifah” means “fight” in Arabic. At the end of his speech he and others revealed t-shirts with the “globalise” slogan.

Police soon forcefully intervened, arresting seven people throughout the rally, including Heydt and two women who had carried the lead banner.

Naji said genocide was the real crime, not protesting the complicty of the Queensland and federal government.

The seven arrests add to the 31 previously made under the anti-free speech laws. Some, like Heydt, have now been arrested twice.

JFP is pursuing a High Court challenge to strike down the anti-free speech laws. It is asking for financial support for this and is organising a fundraising event on December 11.

The rally also featured music from a local punk band and a Riff Raff brass contingent.

Pip Hinman reports from Gadigal Country/Sydney that hundreds took to the streets again for Gaza on November 15. They demanded that NSW and federal Labor take action for Palestine, and stop trying to suppress free speech — particularly those speaking up against genocide.

The protest was called to show solidarity with pro-Palestine supporters in Queensland, who are being criminalised for standing up against genocide, and called for the scrapping of bans on phrases which call for rights, dignity, peace and justice for those living between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.

Minns wants to bring in similar laws, but is waiting on the outcome of the High Court challenge.

Speakers at the protest included Dr Shamikh Badra, who is from Gaza. He called on the federal government to act for Palestine, and not allow the weapons trade to continue.

Badra condemned the strike on Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza. He said people were still being denied food, medical assistance and other aid, and …

title: Women in Arzoxlî protest against delivery of solar panels
content:
The dispute over the construction of two solar power plants is escalating in the village of Arzoxlî (Turkish: Kervanpınar), in the Sur district of Amed (Diyarbakır). Although an administrative court has temporarily suspended the implementation of the Zenkar-2 project, preparations for the neighboring Zenkar-1 project are continuing. On the 23rd day of a protest vigil against the construction work, trucks delivered solar panels intended for the project to the site.


In response to the delivery, women from Arzoxlî gathered in the village square and marched together toward the construction site. Chanting slogans such as “Excavator operators, get off our grazing land,” “Axa me ava me hebûna me ye” (Our land and water are our existence), “Resistance leads to victory” and “No to companies in Arzoxlî,” they protested against the continuation of the project.


Soldiers block access to construction site


On their way to the project site, the villagers were stopped by Turkish gendarmerie. The soldiers blocked their access and prevented them from proceeding any further. The protesters expressed their anger at the soldiers’ actions.


Residents of Arzoxlî are demanding that construction work on the Zenkar-1 solar power plant also be halted. While a court order has already suspended construction of Zenkar-2, the villagers continue their resistance against the second project through a permanent protest camp.


Women in Arzoxlî continue resistance against solar power project

title: Evin Zapsu's lawyer: Evin is in severe pain and needs treatment
content:
The health condition of seriously ill prisoner Evin Zapsu, who is held at Kayseri Bünyan Women's Closed Prison and was diagnosed with cancer on 16 November, remains critical. Biopsy results and other medical examinations revealed stage four uterine cancer that has spread to other parts of her body. Despite repeated calls for her release, Evin Zapsu remains imprisoned.


Relatives of ill prisoners have called for their release outside the Ministry of Justice, while Evin Zapsu's lawyer, Berivan Çelik, spoke to ANF about her client's health and the latest developments.


'Evin is suffering from severe pain'


Berivan Çelik said that Evin Zapsu remained in good spirits despite trying to conceal the pain, swelling and physical changes. Çelik said that doctors had informed Evin Zapsu, who was diagnosed with stage four uterine cancer with metastases, that she urgently needed surgery. She warned that further delays in treatment could leave her client dependent on others for care.


The lawyer said that she met Evin Zapsu face to face at the prison last Tuesday and witnessed her deteriorating health firsthand.


Despite taking two strong painkillers, Evin Zapsu was visibly suffering from severe pain and had significant abdominal swelling and other physical changes. Çelik said that her client remained in good spirits but was trying to conceal her suffering.


Berivan Çelik said: "Although she had taken two strong painkillers before coming to our meeting, it was very clear that she was in pain, even though she tried not to show it. Nevertheless, her spirits were high and she was smiling. She believed that even if her test results were bad, she would be able to overcome the illness without too much difficulty."


Report concludes that she can remain in prison


Berivan Çelik said that an earlier medical assessment had concluded that her client could remain in prison. Three days after they submitted a request for the postponement of her sentence and her release, Evin Zapsu was taken to Kayseri City Hospital, where a medical board prepared a report.


Çelik said that the report concluded that Evin Zapsu was fit to remain in prison, while subsequent biopsy results revealed the severity of her illness.


Çelik also said: "Three days after we first requested the postponement of her sentence and her release, Evin was taken to Kayseri City Hospital. A medical board report was prepared at the hospital, and the report issued last Monday concluded that she could remain in prison. However, the biopsy results revealed stage four uterine cancer with metastases.


We therefore submitted another application today. We have not yet received a written response to our previous request. No decision approving or rejecting our application has been communicated to us."


'The masses have spread to her chest and armpits'


Berivan Çelik also referred to radiological imaging and CT scan results, saying that her client's health had deteriorated since the first scans were carried out in August.


Çelik said that masses initially detected in the abdominal area had spread over time and that new masses had developed.


Çelik also said: "The initial radiological scans showed masses only in her abdomen. She told us that these masses had gradually spread upwards towards her chest and that new masses had begun to appear in her armpits. We have the radiological images, CT scans, their reports and the biopsy results.


When we compare the reports from August with her current condition, we can see that the masses have increased considerably and are causing much more pain."


Berivan Çelik said that the doctor who examined her client had told her that she urgently needed surgery to remove the masses. She explained that following the initial pathology results, she and Evin Zapsu's family had consulted an oncology specialist on the basis of the scans taken in August.


Although the specialist provided a verbal opinion, they were unable to obtain a written assessment. Following the biopsy results, they submitted a new application.


Çelik said that they attached the biopsy results to their second petition and stressed that treatment must begin immediately.


'Treatment is not possible under prison conditions'


Berivan Çelik also described the health problems her client faces in prison, saying that the cold conditions force her to sleep with hot-water bottles and that she spends most of her time in bed because of the pain.

author: anred
title: Cabaret Voltaire, un puente al revisionismo de derecha
content:
Desde hace tiempo, el canal de stream rosarino viene llevando a cabo un cruzada en favor de la derecha peronista a la que no reconoce como tal pero que minimiza en lo que hace al rol de la represión paraestatal previa a la última dictadura militar. En esta oportunidad se despacharon con todo junto a un invitado de lujo: Rodrigo de la Serna.

Por Nicolás Salas.   


El ascenso de la ultraderecha en Argentina abrió un escenario de balances en la militancia en general y dentro del peronismo en particular. El derrotero que implicó el gobierno de

Alberto Fernández

 empoderó a algunos sectores que no sólo habían cuestionado su candidatura sino que además pronosticaron de antemano el fracaso del frente “Todos”. En los últimos años, figuras como

Guillermo Moreno

 supieron legitimarse en esos planteos y ampliar la escena política para la intervención de una tendencia que se mantuvo marginal o minoritaria dentro de lo que fue el auge de la lucha por los derechos humanos a principios del siglo XXI. 


Actualmente nos encontramos con periodistas, comunicadores o divulgadores que recuperaron esas banderas que, a principios del kirchnerismo,

Gerónimo “el momo” Venegas

 y

Hugo Moyano

 supieron agitar casi en soledad cuando nadie prestaba el oído a la exigencia por la reapertura de la causa por el asesinato del secretario general de la CGT,

José Ignacio Rucci

. “

Cabaret Voltaire

” es una versión actualizada, en modo stream, de esta disputa que viene saliendo a la superficie después de años en el subsuelo de la agenda política.  


El 8 de noviembre de 2026, el canal rosarino emitió un programa que contó con la participación del actor y músico Rodrigo de la Serna. La excusa del encuentro fue la presentación de la serie “

Gordon

”, policial basado en la historia de

Aníbal Gordon

, un mercenario de la represión paraestatal, de los servicios de inteligencia y de los centros clandestinos de detención entre las décadas de los 60′ y los 80′. La interacción del artista con Mauricio Vera y Tomás Trapé, conductores del programa, dio lugar a varios debates que trascendieron el abordaje mismo de la producción cinematográfica y pusieron sobre la mesa varias tesis (ponele) sobre la historia argentina moderna. Todas ellas sumergidas en

un revisionismo que pareciera perseguir un único objetivo que es el de deslindar responsabilidades políticas a quienes protagonizaron la represión paraestatal durante el último gobierno de Juan Domingo Perón y de Isabel Martínez de Perón

. Todo parece moverse con muy poca rigurosidad histórica y agitada sobre un balance crítico (y por derecha) de las últimas experiencias progresistas de gobierno.   


Tesis I : A partir de la figura de Rucci, hay que reconciliar a las partes en disputas dentro del peronismo de los 60’/70′


Como lo ha hecho en innumerables programas, Tomás Trapé volvió a referirse a Rucci y se animó a cuestionar una máxima de los organismos de

DD.HH

: “n

uestra responsabilidad histórica no es elegir, porque uno no tiene un muerto en ninguno de los dos bandos, sino que es construir la síntesis y el perdón, y para el perdón se necesita un gesto. Nosotros hemos hecho varios programas sobre Rucci, y lo de Rucci es un gesto para la reconciliación”. 


En la reconstrucción histórica,

organismos como las Madres e Hijos han marcado un hilo conductor entre la represión previa a 1976 y la ejercida posteriormente en la dictadura

. En algunos casos, las consideraciones sobre el personaje en cuestión y su rol con las patotas de ese entonces son muy claras: “

Rucci fue un asesino que mató a montones de pibes y a otros los mandó a la muerte porque los denunció. Que lo hayan matado de ninguna manera es un crímen de lesa humanidad. El crimen de lesa humanidad es cuando interviene el Estado

. La familia de Rucci ahora sale porque la derecha está saliendo», supo denunciar públicamente

Hebe de Bonafini

.


 


Para ir a una órbita ideológica más afín a los mencionados streamers, podemos citar a

Juan Manuel Abal Medina

 en su libro “

Conocer a Perón

” (1). Si bien sus 478 páginas orbitan en una reivindicación constante a la figura de Perón y José Ignacio Rucci, eso no impide que

el autor reconozca y exponga diálogos que corroboran la participación directa del exsecretario general de la CGT en la masacre de Ezeiza (junio de 1973)

, inicio de la contienda entre las diferentes tendencias dentro del peronismo que escalará (sin retorno) con el asesinato del mismo Rucci en septiembre de 1973 …

title: 3 UN experts press the Philippines over mass detentions of ASEAN summit protesters
content:
Three United Nations Special Rapporteurs have publicly called out the Philippine government over the reported detention of more than 300 people during protests at the opening of the ASEAN 2026 summit, warning that the arrests point to a broader squeeze on dissent.

The mass arrest happened last November 15, 2026 when demonstrations broke out across Metro Manila to coincide with the regional summit to oppose the U.S.-led Pax technology and mining initiative and the presence of U.S. President Donald Trump. They were released on the night of November 18, following a decision of the Muntinlupa prosecutor.

Read: Police violently disperse, arrest hundreds in Muntinlupa protest

Among the arrested are mostly members of the Southern Tagalog group Lakbayan in Muntinlupa City, alongside media workers including student journalists, and progressive groups at Liwasang Bonifacio in Manila, and Bulacan.

Andrea Bolaños Vargas, Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights defenders, said she is concerned by reports of police violence against peaceful protesters and is monitoring the safety and protection of human rights defenders.

“I have received worrying information about the situation and am closely monitoring developments, including regarding the safety and protection of human rights defenders,” Vargas said.

Gina Romero, UN Special Rapporteur on the rights to freedom of peaceful assembly and of association, wrote she received reports that security officials earlier in the week urged groups to hold off on protests until after the summit, reportedly to avoid a bad image before foreign visitors.

#Philipines today's police behaviour mirror a wider crackdown on dissent in the country. I have been receiving worrisome information about sedition subpoenas for anti-corruption protests, authorities tagging student leaders as "wanted", military home visits & campus lockdowns 3/

“Peaceful protests are not a PR question, they are a (human rights) issue,”

Romero added that this goes beyond the image of the ASEAN Summit taking place in the country. “(The) Philippines prior protests on related issues such as the pax silica have also been harassed,” she wrote.

Astrid Riano, Special Rapporteur on the right to a clean, safe and healthy environment, also said she is closely following the situation in Manila and in demonstrations elsewhere in the country.

Read: ‘Make Pax Silica deal public’

Riano also emphasized that ASEAN’s efforts should be aligned on its declaration to the right of a safe, clean, healthy, and sustainable environment at the 47th ASEAN Summit in Kuala Lumpur on October 26, 2025. This declaration aimed to address climate change, biodiversity loss, and environmental pollution.

“The right to a #healthyenvironment includes access to information and public participation, which includes peaceful demonstrations,” Riano said.

The same police brutality during Anti-Pax Silica protests are also prevalent across the regions of the country.

In Cebu City, rights group Karapatan Central Visayas has recorded reports of at least 10 attempted arrests and about 20 people injured in the police dispersal, with one protester reportedly rushed to the emergency room.

On November 18, 2026, the arrested protesters were released after three days in detention. Global civil society alliance CIVICUS is urging the Philippine government to investigate police restrictions and excessive force against protesters during the ASEAN Summit in Manila. (RVO)

author: Mitch Perry
title: Florida Will Break Its Own Death Penalty Record With 20th Execution on Thursday
content:
Thomas M. Overton’s attorneys and Floridians for Alternatives to the Death Penalty say Overton is innocent of murder.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Death row prisoner Thomas M. Overton is scheduled to be executed at 6 p.m. Thursday at Florida State Prison. His would be the 20th conducted by the state this year, breaking the record 19 that took place in 2025.

More are coming: Gov. Ron DeSantis has signed death warrants for Ricardo Gonzalez and that execution is set Dec. 1, and for Willie Seth Crain Jr. for Dec. 10.

Overton was sentenced in 1999 for the 1991 murders of a Monroe County couple and their unborn child. At the time of her death, the woman was eight months pregnant, and Overton was also convicted in the death of their unborn son.

Overton has always maintained that he is innocent.

“Executing Overton would violate his right to Due Process and be a manifest injustice because there remains a great deal of untested evidence and inconclusive evidence that must be retested,” his attorneys claimed in a motion to vacate his conviction and death sentence filed in the circuit court in Monroe County on Oct. 28. “Further, there remains information that was never disclosed to Overton regarding potential third-party guilt. This evidence would independently support Overton’s actual innocence claim.”

The group Floridians for Alternatives to the Death Penalty says the new motion documents “extraordinary failures” in the original investigation of the murders.

“Thomas Overton’s case sounds outrageous, but the reality is that Florida routinely sends people to death row based on unreliable evidence and deeply flawed investigation,’ said Grace Hanna, executive director of the organization.

Overton’s attorneys have also filed for a stay of execution with the U.S. Supreme Court. They contend DeSantis’ refusal to grant clemency to anyone convicted of murder violates the due process rights of those on death row seeking a final act of mercy.

More than half of all the public executions in the United States have taken place in Florida this year. If Overton’s execution takes place as scheduled, it would be the 38th in the country in 2026. It would also be the 39th execution to take place in Florida in the past two years.

The death penalty is legal in 27 states, but only 14 states have executed anyone since the start of 2019, according to the State Court Report.

Donations are down for Truthout at a time when media is under immense pressure. Google’s AI search has driven our traffic down by 15 percent, Trump is arresting journalists, and many independent media organizations face heartbreaking cutbacks and closures.

At the same time, movement media is vital in the fight against Trump’s authoritarian reign. Our mandate to tell the truth, share strategies for resistance, and speak against fascism is ever more urgent in this deluge of political censorship and misinformation. Yet, we are struggling to meet our publishing costs when our work is so urgently needed.

We are fundraising right now for those basic operating expenses — we need $19,000 in the next 24 hours. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference.

title: Polonya'da görevinden uzaklaştırılan Anayasa Mahkemesi Başkanı'nın dokunulmazlığı kaldırıldı
content:
Polonya'da Anayasa Mahkemesi Genel Kurulu, 30 Ekim'de görevinden uzaklaştırılan Mahkeme Başkanı Bogdan Swieczkowski'nin dokunulmazlığının kaldırılmasına ve hakkında cezai kovuşturma yürütülmesine izin verdi.

Anayasa Mahkemesi Genel Kurulu, Swieczkowski ve Anayasa Mahkemesi Başkan Yardımcısı Bartlomiej Sochanski'nin 30 Ekim'de görevlerinden uzaklaştırılmalarıyla ülkede patlak veren ve Başbakan Donald Tusk liderliğindeki hükümet ile Cumhurbaşkanı Karol Nawrocki ve muhalefet arasında siyasi ve hukuki tartışmaya dönüşen krizin ardından 3. kez toplandı.

Mahkemeden yapılan yazılı açıklamaya göre, Genel Kurul, 17 Kasım'da aldığı kararla Swieczkowski hakkında çeşitli suçlamalar kapsamında cezai kovuşturma izni verirken, Swieczkowski'nin gözaltına alınması ve tutuklanması talebini reddetti.

Swieczkowski, "Savcılıkta üst düzey görevlerde bulunduğu dönemde yetkilerini kötüye kullanmakla, savcıların çalışma haklarını ihlal etmekle, avukatlık sırlarını ifşa etmekle, Anayasa Mahkemesi Başkanı olarak görevini yerine getirmemekle ve başka bir yargıcın fiziksel dokunulmazlığını ihlal etmekle" suçlanıyor.

Genel Kurul, Swieczkowski'nin görevlerini yerine getirmesini askıya alırken, maaşının yüzde 50 azaltılmasına karar verdi.

Aynı toplantıda, 30 Ekim'de görevinden uzaklaştırılan Başkan Yardımcısı Sochanski hakkında da cezai kovuşturma izni verildi. Sochanski'nin de görevinden uzaklaştırılmasına ve maaşının yüzde 25 azaltılmasına karar verildi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Israel Extends Arbitrary Detention of Leading Palestinian Doctor
content:
An Israeli court has extended the arbitrary detention of a leading Palestinian doctor, despite international outcry over reports of his torture in custody and his deteriorating health. 


Dr Hussam Abu Safiya, a paediatrician and director of Gaza’s Kamal Adwan Hospital, has been imprisoned by Israel without charge or trial since 27 December 2024. 


An Israeli court in the southern city of Be’er Sheva decided to extend Dr Abu Safiya’s detention by another six months on Wednesday, rejecting his lawyer’s request to release him and ruling that he “poses a threat to the state of Israel”,

according to Israeli news outlet Haaretz

.


This is despite ongoing reports that Dr Abu Safiya, a leading voice in Gaza’s systematically decimated healthcare system, has been subjected to beatings and torture in Israeli detention. 


Lawyer Nasser Odeh

reported in July

 that his client was barely recognisable since being transferred to Rakevet, a notorious underground wing of the Ramla prison complex in central Israel, where

Palestinian prisoners are reportedly

 deprived of sunlight and subject to extreme violence. 


Odeh said Dr Abu Safiya was weak, on the verge of losing consciousness and bearing fresh bruises and torture marks on his head and body. He added that the doctor told him: “This is the last time you’ll see me… they brought me here to kill me.”


Former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn condemned Israel’s “abominable” treatment of the paediatrician, telling Novara Media: “Dr Abu Safiya is one of thousands of health workers who have been detained or killed by Israel. This grotesque attack on healthcare personnel is an assault on the healthcare system itself – which is part and parcel of Israel’s genocide against the Palestinian people.


“What will it take for Britain to speak up, end all military cooperation, and impose real sanctions on Israel?”


Amnesty International UK slammed the extension of Dr Abu Safiya’s detention as “shameful” and challenged the UK government to “publicly demand” his immediate and unconditional release.


Karla McLaren, the charity’s government and political relations manager, told Novara Media: “A doctor who spent his career saving lives is now fighting for his own. More than 800 UK doctors and healthcare workers have already called on the foreign secretary to take urgent action. Dr Abu Safiya must be released immediately and unconditionally, and the UK government must publicly demand this and press Israel to give him independent medical care now.


“Every day he remains in detention without the UK government publicly demanding his release, it is accepting that doctors can be locked up for doing their jobs.”


Ahead of his detention, despite a near-total military siege, intensifying Israeli attacks on his hospital and the surrounding area, and the killing of his son and many of his colleagues, Dr Abu Safiya insisted on staying to keep Kamal Adwan Hospital running. It was the last functioning hospital in northern Gaza. 


In October 2024, the IDF raided the medical facility, arresting Dr Abu Safiya and freeing him shortly afterwards. The Israeli military killed

 his 15-year-old son Ibrahim

in the same operation.  


Dr Abu Safiya was arrested again while on duty at the hospital in December 2024. An

iconic photograph

 shows the doctor in his white coat facing Israeli tanks through the rubble.


Israel claims Dr Abu Safiya is a senior Hamas operative, an allegation he denies. He is being held under Israel’s

“unlawful combatants” law

, which is used to indefinitely imprison Palestinians without charge or trial in what Amnesty International describes as a “flagrant violation of international law”.

author: EDRi
title: One year later, a broad coalition tells EU lawmakers: do not simplify away people’s rights with the Digital Omnibus
content:
On 19 November 2025, the European Commission presented the Digital Omnibus as an exercise in simplification. One year later, 100 organisations and individuals from across civil society are warning that simplification is turning into deregulation, with consequences far beyond the usual digital-rights debate.

A new open letter calls on EU lawmakers to protect data protection, privacy and other fundamental rights, rather than weakening them in the name of empty promises of competitiveness and the AI hype.

There are plenty of things about EU digital regulation that could genuinely be simpler: people should not have to fight through endless cookie banners, regulators should cooperate better, businesses should not operate in good faith knowing other companies won’t be held accountable when disrespecting the law…

But cutting red tape and cutting rights are not the same thing. The Digital Omnibus proposed, amongst other, significant changes to the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and ePrivacy framework. These affect when information about us is protected, how companies may reuse personal data for AI, safeguards around automated decision-making, access and transparency rights, and protection against unwanted access to our devices.

All of this is happening in a much wider political context. Across different EU policy areas, protections for people, workers, consumers and the environment are increasingly being reopened and deregulated under the language of ‘simplification’ and competitiveness.

One of the clearest examples is AI. Companies developing AI systems want enormous amounts of data. The Digital Omnibus on Data would create a specific route under the GDPR for AI development, training and operation to rely on the so-called legitimate interest legal basis. The existing legal tests would not disappear, but the risk is that large-scale reuse of personal data for AI becomes increasingly normalised, while people are left to find out what happened to their data and try to object afterwards.

This is particularly concerning in a market already dominated by big tech companies with huge advantages in data, infrastructure and capital, which can undermine companies that have invested in more privacy-protective and rights-respecting products and want clear rules and a genuine level playing field.

AI is only one piece of the proposal. Other changes touch sensitive and biometric data, automated decisions, transparency and access rights, and the confidentiality of our devices and communications.

These changes matter differently to different communities. They matter to workers subject to automated management and surveillance, worried about losing their jobs or their tasks becoming even more alienating; patients whose sensitive information needs strong protection; people facing discrimination who rely on transparency and access rights to challenge unfair systems; journalists and human rights defenders who depend on confidential communications; children and young people exposed to commercial tracking; and consumers confronted with companies holding vastly more information and power than they do.

That is why this cannot be treated as a niche dispute, even less when we remember the GDPR is the cornerstone of the EU’s digital rulebook.

To mark the first, and hopefully last, anniversary of the proposal, 100 organisations, academics, researchers, individuals and responsible businesses are coming together around a simple message: the EU can simplify its rules without simplifying away people’s rights.

The open letter calls on the European Parliament and Member States to reject provisions that weaken rights and substantive protections, and to ensure that any evidence-backed genuine problems in the GDPR, ePrivacy or other legislation are addressed through proper democratic processes, backed by evidence, consultation and scrutiny.

Fundamental rights are not red tape, and if we are speaking about simplification, the question should rather be ‘simplification for whom?’

author: Rory Mir
title: Outage Chaos: When Tech is too Big to Fail
content:
Outages happen, but we deserve a resilient internet where no one outage at one company can put people at risk and disrupt the global economy. We can only get there by addressing an over-reliance on a few cloud monopolists through effective antitrust laws and interoperability requirements.

Service outages, like we’ve seen recently at Microsoft, Apple*, banks, courts, airlines, and elsewhere, can be more than an annoying hurdle. Losing a vital service due to an error can cause the same impacts as a government-ordered internet shutdown—people losing access to vital information and lines of communication. As usual, the greatest harms are faced by people on the margins globally.

There’s not much hope in companies out-nerding these issues either. Technical errors will always exist, whether it’s a bug, negligence from an administrator, or a malicious attack. The problem is an over-reliance on any one company or system when these inevitable outages occur. It’s a matter of public safety and economic stability that policymakers mitigate the impact of these disruptions before they occur.

In order to do so, we must ensure antitrust prevents providers of key technical systems from becoming too big to fail.

The harms inflicted by tech monopolies go beyond monetary costs to the end user. In fact, monopolists can often offer lower prices, or even offer free services, thanks to their greater scale and incentive to shut out competitors using free-flowing investment capital. The problem is this puts a few tech companies in a position of incredible influence. The true cost is a loss of control when our private data, access to knowledge, and free expression all become mediated by tools owned by a handful of billionaires.

Losing diversity in our digital infrastructure creates a less stable and less resilient internet for everyone.

This isn’t just a bad deal for us as individuals. Losing diversity in our digital infrastructure creates a less stable and less resilient internet for everyone. When everything from daily tasks to national security is reliant on a few digital monocultures, one mistake or exploit can cascade into an explosive impact. The risks multiply in the current investment climate, where financial markets reward companies that strip-mine redundancy and resiliency from critical systems. Even if you see the problem coming, an outage that hits clients, suppliers, collaborators or loved ones proves just as disruptive. We need to remove these chokepoints for good, which means a digital sovereignty movement that makes the web more free by design—not just importing existing levers of control into another nation's borders.

Central to this effort must be undercutting platform control by fostering interoperability, i.e. when tools are made to be compatible among competitors. When this is done carefully, it’s not only easier to switch to better alternatives, we wind up with more alternatives as it becomes more viable to compete or offer complementary tools alongside existing systems.

This is what made systems like email great. You could choose your own apps and services, even using several simultaneously, and never lose touch with a contact. Early architects of the internet did not take reliable hosting for granted. Services were often on a machine a few rooms over, and needed to be prepared for the occasional interruption of service.

But in the age of hyperscalers and massive data centers, the infrastructure underlying the web isn’t owned by many scattered IT departments, it’s rented from a handful of “cloud” providers. These providers managed to scale up quickly and replace interoperability with walled gardens, enticing customers with lower costs while making it costly to leave and tightly controlling how services behave. Once in control, these platforms have every incentive to enshittify their services and devalue their workers, delivering an increasingly shoddy and restrictive service.

This context makes building interoperability an act of defiance—often coming from the sweat of open source developers. These projects may be tolerated by monopolists in the short term, but can be one boardroom decision away from being broken entirely. A better internet means championing these creators through funding, liability protections, and requiring big players to cooperate. Here is what lawmakers should do:

Federal and state legislators should—

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Giorgio Agamben: The death of the word?
content:
Michelangelo,

Cumaean Sibyl

 (c. 1511), Sistine Chapel, Vatican City


This short article was originally published under the title “Morte della parola?” in the Italian newspaper

Paese Sera

 on 8 February 1968. It has been republished in the latest issue of the French magazine

Entétement

, although the original version can be found on the

La Voce di Fiore

 archive website. A Spanish translation of the same can be found at th magazine

Ficción de la razón

.


A book has recently been published in Paris,

Of Grammatology

 (1967), a work destined to cause a stir not only in the field of linguistic studies. Jacques Derrida, one of the most original figures in the new wave of French philosophical criticism, begins with the observation that, today, “through a movement whose necessity we can barely glimpse, everything that, for at least twenty centuries, has tended to be defined under the name of language, is beginning to be summarised under the name of writing”. It does indeed seem that writing—which, according to Rousseau, was nothing more than a complement to speech—is gradually freeing itself from its subordination to the phonetic medium, to the point of reversing its traditional relationship with language: writing would therefore not be a technique in the service of language, but rather, on the contrary, it is language that can be considered a specific case, an aspect, of writing.


To better understand the phenomenon to which Derrida refers when he speaks of writing dissociated from the phonetic element, one need only consider the example of mathematics, whose symbolic notation does not refer to any spoken language. If we consider that today we are witnessing a process of mathematisation across all the sciences, the “liberation” of writing described by Derrida becomes an extremely concrete phenomenon (readers who have followed recent news regarding the

in vitro

 synthesis of living matter, carried out by certain American scientists, will recall having heard talk of writing and “programmes” even in relation to the most elementary processes of the living cell). The “liberation” of writing described by Derrida becomes an extremely concrete phenomenon.


On the basis of these premises, Derrida deduces the need for a pure science of writing, which considers writing prior to speech and independently of it: this science is, precisely, “grammatology”; and, to define its aims, it suffices to substitute this term for “semiology”, the term Saussure uses to outline the programme of his famous

Course in General Linguistics

: “We shall call it grammatology… and, as it does not yet exist, we cannot say what it will be; but it has a right to exist, and its place is determined in advance”. The age of speech, which began under the creative power of the verb, is drawing to a close before our very eyes; the character of this new age might be summed up in the following formula: “In the beginning was the written word’’.


Whilst it is true that, from this perspective, linguistics must become a mere branch of grammatology, Derrida seems, however, to overlook the fact that a science already exists which considers language not as speech, but as code and writing; consequently, grammatology itself should necessarily be understood as a sub-branch or a section of that science. This is cybernetics, which, from its beginnings in Wiener’s theories, defined its world as a universe of writing and coding. The very idea of grammatology is already fully contained within the notion of “programme”, one of the key concepts of cybernetics. Etymologically, “programme” —pro-grammer— means “to put the letter (that is,

writing

) first”, whilst “prophecy” means, by contrast, “to put the word first”. Indeed, in the programme assigned to an electronic brain, everything that constitutes the living, phonetic element of language is erased to make way for a system of absolute writing that can be deciphered but not pronounced. It is fair to say that, up to now, our civilisation has known two types of language that have gradually diverged: the language of science is, essentially, written language —code, writing—, whilst the language of poetry and philosophical thought is spoken language —breath, word—. Nevertheless, these two domains—which, for convenience’s sake, we might call the “sphere of the programme” and the “sphere of prophecy”—are drawing ever closer together today thanks to cybernetics; through the mathematisation of human phenomena, cybernetics …

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Harassment won’t stop a son’s search for his missing father
content:
Marklen Lariosa, son of missing Kilusang Mayo Uno (KMU) labor organizer William Lariosa, speaks during a rally in Davao City on the first anniversary of his father’s disappearance on April 10, 2025. Photo by Kath Cortez/Davao Today

“Family members searching for their disappeared loved ones have to endure threats and harassment from state forces on top of the terrible uncertainty and emotional turmoil they are already going through.”

Is it a mistake for a son to demand justice and accountability?

Marklen, son of disappeared labor organizer William Lariosa, raised this question following the recent incident of harassment and surveillance he experienced. Members of his family were alarmed after two unidentified individuals were looking for his residence on the night of October 25.

He told Bulatlat that this was the first time such an event had happened since his father, a labor organizer under Kilusang Mayo Uno (KMU) Southern Mindanao, was abducted in Quezon, Bukidnon, on April 10, 2024.

Marklen could not think of other possible reasons, suspecting that the incident may have something to do with his continuing involvement in campaigns and mobilizations that demand the surfacing of Lariosa. “Is it a mistake for a son to search for his missing father?” he further asked.

Read: After 2 years, son laments continuing disappearance of Mindanao labor organizer

Neighbors of the Lariosa family in their hometown in Davao de Oro province were the ones who encountered the two individuals. They reportedly wore helmets and were on board a black motorcycle, introducing themselves as “collectors” when they were asked.

For Marklen, the response and presence of the two raised suspicions. Aside from the fact that they visited the community around 7 p.m., which is outside the regular working hours, Marklen said that he did not apply for any financial loan.

After the incident, he was concerned for the safety of his family, prompting them to lodge a blotter report with the barangay. However, he stood firm that it won’t stop him from continuing his cause.

Desaparecidos, an organization of families and friends of enforced disappearance victims, denounced the incident, urging the government to put an end to this kind of harassment.

“Family members searching for their disappeared loved ones have to endure threats and harassment from state forces on top of the terrible uncertainty and emotional turmoil they are already going through,” JL Burgos, Desaparecidos chairperson, said in a statement.

Rights groups Karapatan and the Center for Trade Union and Human Rights (CTUHR) also expressed strong condemnations about what happened.

Marklen, a member of the National Board of Desaparecidos, has raised a possibility that the two individuals who recently visited their neighborhood might be connected to those who visited their house several times prior to the disappearance of his father.

He said they were visited by individuals who allegedly introduced themselves as state agents once in 2022 and three times in 2023, accusing Lariosa of being involved in communist insurgency. There were warnings, he added, that they would get dragged into it if they would not cooperate.

The series of visits was reportedly the primary reason why Lariosa was forced to take refuge in Bukidnon. Marklen affirmed that his father, who remains missing, had been a labor organizer.

On July 8, the Supreme Court required certain commanders and elements of Philippine Army units to comment on the petition for review on certiorari filed by the family.

Read: Military ordered to reply to missing Mindanao labor organizer’s case

Since 2024, KMU Southern Mindanao has documented 57 cases of human rights violations against its members and organizers.

The labor group released a statement on October 24, presenting the faces of some individuals, including former high-ranking New People’s Army (NPA) member Roberto Rosete Jr., who allegedly harassed KMU’s leaders and members.

Read: Groups decry surveillance of KMU office in Southern Mindanao

Marklen called for an end to any form of harassment and intimidation against families of the disappeared, pointing out that achieving justice is their only goal. (RVO)

author: Shan Kenshin Ecaldre
title: Peasant organizer persists despite surveillance
content:
Jesus Monasterial. (Photo from Photo from Tanggol Magsasaka-TK)

Repeated surveillance restricted his movements and caused anxiety over his family’s safety.

When he was a university student, he questioned the purpose of agricultural education. Now he is organizing landless farmers and fisherfolk.

Jesus Monasterial has spent more than two years working with rural communities in Southern Tagalog. However, his work resulted in repeated surveillance by state forces, peasant groups said.

On October 31, Tanggol Magsasaka–Timog Katagalugan reported that a police intelligence operative identified as “Bruno” had been asking about Monasterial’s whereabouts in Lian, Batangas. The operative was reportedly previously assigned in Nasugbu.

At the time, Monasterial was assisting a protest camp in Barangay San Diego, where farmers, fisherfolk, and residents opposed the possible demolition of several houses.

“I was on my way back to the people’s protest camp in San Diego when news reached us that someone had been asking about my personal information,” he said.

The camp was established by Samahang Mangangawil 1979 and the San Diego Homeowners’ Association, with support from the Katipunan ng mga Samahang Magbubukid sa Timog Katagalugan (KASAMA-TK) and Pambansang Lakas ng Kilusang Mamamalakaya ng Pilipinas–Timog Katagalugan (PAMALAKAYA-TK).

The incident prompted fellow organizers to discuss security measures. They also plan to file a complaint before the Commission on Human Rights (CHR).

Monasterial’s involvement in peasant organizing began at the University of the Philippines Los Baños (UPLB) where he was enrolled in BS Agricultural Biotechnology.

Coming from a family of farmers in Bicol, where his grandparents worked as agricultural tenants, he became increasingly critical of an agricultural education system that he said served the interests of transnational corporations rather than addressing farmers’ lack of land and government support.

Through the League of Filipino Students–UPLB, he became involved in social issues action and joined community immersions with farmers in Tartaria, Silang, Cavite, as well as Mangyan communities in Mindoro and Dumagat communities in Rizal.

These experiences led him to leave his studies and become a full-time organizer. He now serves as deputy secretary-general of KASAMA-TK.

His work involves staying in communities, conducting consultations and political education, and helping establish local farmers and fisherfolk associations.

“Being a full-time organizer means devoting my entire time to the communities and being far from my loved ones,” he said, adding that he had to set aside his plan to finish college.

The October 31 incident was not the first reported surveillance involving Monasterial.

On July 19, 2026, soldiers from the 16th Infantry Battalion of the Philippine Army reportedly sought to identify the organizers of KASAMA-TK’s Regional Peasant Consultation in Barangay Malinis, Lemery, Batangas.

On September 21, a man introducing himself as “Del” Dela Cruz reportedly approached a member of Sugarfolks’ Unity for Genuine Agricultural Reform (SUGAR-Batangas), attempting to persuade the member to leave the organization and provide information about its activities.

According to Tanggol Magsasaka–Timog Katagalugan, the man showed footage of a protest outside the Department of Agriculture regional office led by the Alyansa ng Magsasaka para sa Kumpensasyon (AMK), SUGAR-Batangas, KAISAHAN, and KASAMA-TK. He allegedly warned the member against working with Monasterial, claiming that the organizer was “already drawing attention.”

The protest resulted in a dialogue with government representatives to demand agricultural inputs and implements for farmers and farmworkers affected by successive calamities.

The groups also cited previous incidents in Barangay Casile, Laguna; Lupang Ramos and Tartaria, Cavite; and Coron, Palawan.

Monasterial said that the repeated surveillance restricted his movements and caused anxiety over his family’s safety. “Repeated surveillance limits my movements as an organizer and makes me fear returning home to my family because they might also be targeted by the state due to my advocacy.”

Despite the threats, Monasterial said that his work remains rooted in the struggles of farmers and farmworkers.

In Batangas, he witnessed sugarcane cutters and loaders receiving only P350 to P400 for every ton of cane harvested and loaded onto trucks. Their wages are paid at the …

author: dev
title: Habiter au corps d'un âne mort ou le chemin de Nietzsche
content:
Dans la continuité des très nombreux articles que nous avons publiés afin de déchiffrer l'Intelligence artificielle, le monde qu'elle avale, celui qu'elle charrie et celui qu'elle produit, nous partageons cette semaine l'épatante découverte d'Olivier Chiran et Pierre Muzin. La première occurrence de l'expression IA reviendrait au célèbre philosophe Friedrich Nietzsche dans le tout aussi célèbre

Ainsi parlait Zarathoustra

, un tiret séparait néanmoins les deux voyelles :

« Braire à tout propos I-A, c'est ce qu'apprennent les ânes et ceux qui en ont l'esprit. »


« Donnez-moi du travail, de la fatigue,


de la douleur et de l'enthousiasme. »


George Sand


1.


Pour savoir précisément où nous en sommes, mais aussi faire face à ce qui nous arrive, alors que l'intelligence artificielle étend son emprise sur le monde et les vies, nous avons besoin d'un sémaphore.


2.


On dit que l'expression « intelligence artificielle » a été lancée par John McCarthy, en 1956, lors de la conférence de Dartmouth, coup d'envoi du programme de recherche consacré à la reproduction algorithmique de la pensée humaine. Soixante-douze ans plus tôt, en 1884, Friedrich Nietzsche, le célèbre philosophe allemand, rédige son grand poème philosophique :

Ainsi parlait Zarathoustra

. Dans la troisième partie de cet ouvrage (trouvée « sous le ciel alcyonien de Nice », dira-t-il), il écrit : « Braire à tout propos I-A, c'est ce qu'apprennent les ânes et ceux qui en ont l'esprit

 [

1

]

. » Première apparition de ces deux lettres, longtemps avant Dartmouth. Évidence de leur rapprochement – en même temps que, d'un simple tiret, de leur mise à distance. On pourrait s'étonner que les traducteurs français (Henri Albert en 1903, Geneviève Bianquis en 1969) aient fait le choix, au lieu du « hi-han » conventionnel, de les conserver telles quelles. Mais le texte allemand dit bien : «

Immer I-A sagen – das lernte allein der Esel, und wer seines Geistes ist

 ! » – Nietzche ayant délibérément fait tomber le

h

 de «

iah

 », braiment de l'âne dans la langue de Goethe. Nous dirons donc, quant à nous, que l'histoire de l'I-A commence à la fin du xixe siècle, lorsqu'un philosophe visionnaire, cheminant à flanc de montagne, a compris qu'on pouvait arracher au cri de l'âne sa puissance d'exclamation intempestive – et qu'il y avait là, pour nous, un grand danger

 [

2

]

.


3.


C'est qu'il y a deux ânes. Gilles Deleuze, commentant les propos de Nietzsche : « On aurait pu croire que l'âne, l'animal qui dit I-A, était l'animal dionysiaque par excellence. En fait, il n'en est rien ; son apparence est dionysiaque, mais toute sa réalité est chrétienne

 [

3

]

. » Le braiment sans son ou ses

h

, c'est cette manière qu'a l'âne de dire toujours oui – mais un faux oui, une fausse affirmation qui ne sait pas dire non, qui ne sait qu'acquiescer face à ce qui est. Bêtise. Démission de la pensée. Obscurantisme. Post-vérité. Positivisme logique. (Margaret Thatcher : «

There is no alternative

 » → TINA : « I-A ! I-A ! ») Toutes choses contre lesquelles, justement, la philosophie s'évertue à lutter. « Le réel tel qu'il est, conclut Deleuze, c'est une idée d'âne. »


4.


Il arrive aussi, on le sait, que l'âne se cabre. L'I-A approbatif que dénoncent les philosophes est la forme mutilée de ce « hi-han ! » qui est à la fois refus catégorique et cri pour l'autonomie et la liberté. Entre les deux, il y a toute la différence entre l'âne vivant (dionysiaque) et l'âne mort (chrétien) – entre l'appel à la révolte et le bourdon béat de la fanfare. (« Si l'âne contribue peu à l'harmonie durant sa vie, écrivait-on au milieu du xixe siècle, il la sert généreusement après sa mort, lui fournissant les meilleures peaux qui existent pour les grosses caisses et les meilleurs tibias pour fabriquer des clarinettes

 [

4

]

. »)


5.


Dans

L'Âne

, de Lucius de Patras, le narrateur voit une magicienne se transformer en oiseau après s'être frotté le corps avec un onguent

 [

5

]

. Ayant voulu l'imiter, il se retrouve, quant à lui, métamorphosé en âne. Séquestré par une bande de brigands, il tente de leur échapper en emportant avec lui, dans sa fuite, une jeune prisonnière. Par malchance, les brigands retrouvent les fuyard

·

e

·

s, les renvoient à leur geôle et imaginent comment les punir avec toute la sévérité requise. « Écoutez une rare et nouvelle invention, qui vous plaira, ou je me trompe fort, dit l'un d'eux à ses comparses ; l'âne doit mourir, c'est la justice …

title: Lieblingsstreberin: Paula Saunders
content:
In der Apple-TV-Serie „Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed“ gerät Tatiana Maslany als geschiedene Mutter in einen Scam aus Cybersex, Erpressung und Verschwörung.

Geschiedene Soccer Mom, gewissenhafte Fact-Checkerin, falsch Verdächtigte? Paula Saunders (Tatiana Maslany), Protagonistin der Apple-TV-Serie „Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed“, lässt sich auf kein Label festlegen. Sie jongliert mit einem Sorgerechtsstreit und einem schlecht bezahlten Medien-Vollzeitjob – worüber sie sich beim Online-Sexarbeiter Trevor ausheult, der ihr empathisch zuhört, solange sie ihn bezahlt. Bis Trevor plötzlich bei ihrer Camsex-Session entführt wird. Kurze Zeit später kriegt sie einen Anruf, dass sie 15.000 Dollar zahlen soll, um ihn freizukaufen. Von der Polizei wird sie mit dem Hinweis, dass das sicher Betrug ist, abgewimmelt. Als sie nicht zahlt, wird sie mit Cybersex-Aufnahmen erpresst. Da das Sorgerecht für ihre Tochter auf dem Spiel steht, nimmt sie die Sache selbst in die Hand und spürt anhand von ein paar wackeligen Screenshots und einer Überweisung die Erpresser*innen auf. Sie beherrscht alle Techniken der Open-Source-Recherche, ist kreativ und fokussiert, wenn es darum geht, die Fakten herauszufinden. Bis die Frage aufkommt: Wer sind eigentlich die Scammer hinter Trevor? Während die Darstellung von Online-Sexarbeiter*innen als „Scammer“ klischeehaft ausfällt, finden sich alle menschlichen Ambivalenzen in Paulas Charakter wieder, was sicher auch Tatiana Maslanys schauspielerischem Können zu verdanken ist. Paula wird von einer Mischung aus Erpressung, Gewalt und Tatendrang weiter in den Scam hineingezogen, bis sie der ziemlich nutzlosen Polizei immer verdächtiger erscheint. Dabei will Paula nach eigenen Angaben nur eine gute Mutter sein und legt sich dafür regelmäßig mit ihrem Ex-Mann Karl (Jake Johnson) an. Neben all dem coacht sie die Fußballmannschaft ihrer Tochter bis zum Gewinn und scheint immer kurz vor einer Beförderung zu stehen. Wenn sie nur ihre Unschuld beweisen und die große Verschwörung aufdecken könnte, die sie in die Situation gebracht hat … Die Serie „Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed“ ist auf Apple TV verfügbar, eine zweite Staffel ist geplant.
