author: Unknown
title: Lilia Folt - On Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness
content:
Author

: Lilia Folt

Title

: On Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness

Date

: September 27

th

, 2026

Notes

: Originally published in

Dissonant Times

, a grassroots journalism and counter-info project from the Willamette Valley of Oregon.

Source

: Dissonant Times, Retrieved on 11/5/2026 from https://dissonanttimes.org/anarchic-reflections-on-anti-surveillance-mindfulness/


 Surveillance has become a ubiquitous feature of everyday life in America. Cameras watch us from businesses and homes, from bus stops, from cars, from traffic lights. Bluetooth trackers ping our smartphones as we pass by, mapping our movements. The phones themselves illuminate our paths through society by continuously pinging cell towers, providing our cell providers our location data, information that is only a subpoena away, if that. In countless ways, we’ve been made to both passively accept and actively participate in our own surveillance. This vast complex of surveillance doesn’t just gather information about us, it also shapes our behaviors, temperaments, and ways of moving through the world. Surveillance molds us down to the level of subjective, sensory, embodied experience. At that same level we can begin to shake off its hold on us and reclaim ourselves. For that, I am offering a practice I’m calling “anti-surveillance mindfulness,” a form of walking meditation that builds mindful awareness of surveillance cameras. This practice, if taken up consistently, opens onto a broader project of transforming our relationship to the places we live in, a project that itself naturally blossoms into materially transforming public space, as self expands to world in the moment-by-moment practice of mindfulness.


Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness


 Readers may or may not be familiar with the Panopticon. Designed by 18

th

 century English liberal Jeremy Bentham, the Panopticon was a model for an institutional building designed so that a single prison guard can watch all the inmates from a central watch tower. The inmates, meanwhile, cannot tell whether or not they are being watched, and therefore could be watched at any moment. To quote Bentham:


 The more constantly the persons to be inspected are under the eyes of the persons who should inspect them, the more perfectly will the purpose of the establishment have been attained. (...) This being impossible, the next thing to be wished for is, that, at every instant, seeing reason to believe as much, and not being able to satisfy himself to the contrary, he should

conceive

 himself to be so.


 A lot has changed since the 1700’s, but the disciplinary paradigm of surveillance has remained the same. If anything, it has expanded beyond specific institutions to encompass much of society.


 There are cameras everywhere, and we are being watched, and while we are aware of this, we tend to see it as normal and unremarkable, an inevitability we must resign ourselves to. Consciousness of being surveilled fades into the background, becoming a constant assumption of being watched that we internalize. This surveillance consciousness is running us all the more effectively because it is not distinct, because it is

un

conscious. That is why the first step in anti-surveillance mindfulness is becoming conscious of surveillance.


 Mindfulness is at the same time a means and an end, the seed and the fruit. When we practice mindfulness in order to build up concentration, mindfulness is a seed. But mindfulness itself is the life of awareness: the presence of mindfulness means the presence of life, and therefore mindfulness is also the fruit. — Thích Nhất Hạnh,

The Miracle of Mindfulness


 “Mindfulness” is a practice originating in various sects of Buddhism. The mindfulness practices and concepts I’m familiar with have largely been within the school of Zen Buddhism

[1]

.


 The classic mindfulness practice is watching the breath, and that is a great starting point. Take a breath in, the air entering through your nose, your stomach and chest softly expanding as you inhale. Then exhale through the mouth, the stomach and chest settling back down, gently exhaling for a little longer than your inhale. Repeat this several times, deepening your breaths slightly. From there, start to check in with your body. Notice how it feels to be sitting down, or to be standing if you are standing; notice how it feels to be holding this piece of paper, holding your phone, or looking at your computer, however it is that you are reading …

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: Air Creebec hit by administrative data breach affecting employees and passengers
content:
Air Creebec, a regional Quebec airline owned by the Cree Nation of Eeyou Istchee, reported a data breach Wednesday affecting both customers and staff.

In a press release, the company announced “an unauthorized intrusion targeting some of its administrative systems.”

The release stresses that the breach did not compromise any systems associated with aircraft, flight operations or flight safety, noting the company’s administrative systems were not connected with aircraft and flight systems, which it said operate independently.

“Initial findings indicate that administrative files were exfiltrated,” states the release. “These files may contain personal information relating mainly to current and former employees, as well as passengers. Others may also contain operational, administrative or financial information related to customers and partners. The review is ongoing.”

Based in the airport of Val d’Or in the Abitibi-Témiscamingue region of western Quebec, roughly 520 kilometres northwest of Ottawa, Air Creebec offers flights to 16 destinations in Quebec and Ontario. The company’s fleet consists of 21 Dash-8 turboprop regional airliners, along with one ATR 72 turboprop air-freighter for cargo, and carries 200,000 passengers per year.

Cybersecurity experts assessing damage

Air Creebec director for Marketing and Business Development Edward Trahan said the breach was identified in October after which company officials immediately brought in cybersecurity experts to analyze the situation.

“They’re currently evaluating what’s going on and what the breach actually contained,” Trahant told APTN News. “The experts are still conducting their review, so there’s no numbers [of victims] at this time that we can give.”

He added that for security reasons, he was not presently willing to name the cybersecurity team currently helping with post-breach recovery.

He said because the attack was designed to go undetected it was hard to determine the date upon which it began, and for how long attackers were able to access Air Creebec’s systems prior to being discovered.

“What I can assure you of is that as soon as [we were] made aware of [it], we acted immediately and did not wait.”

At the moment, Trahant said the attack appeared to have stolen information “related to our employees, past employees too, and maybe even our passengers.”

“But it’s hard to confirm at the moment.”

Company will contact affected parties

He added that a priority for Air Creebec is contacting every one of their staff or customers whose information has been compromised, which cybersecurity experts would undertake to carry out as soon as possible.

“A part of what the cybersecurity experts are doing for us is gathering information to [determine] what kind of protection packages we can provide to people that had their information involved,” said Trahan.

“Those people will be directly contacted in probably the next few days — [but] probably more like [the next] day — about what package they will receive, what protection they’re going to have and how long it’s going to last.”

Trahan said the cybersecurity team was currently in the process of securing all possible intrusion points, but he said the nature of cybersecurity is that 100 per cent protection is impossible.

“It’s just the way of the world,” he said, “but they are closing every possible way to get in and they are getting to the very end of that. As for how they got in initially, we don’t know yet and I don’t want to speculate while the review is still underway.”

Trahan said he and Air Creebec are taking the situation very seriously and are committed to supporting all those affected, and the company said it would be in touch with affected people to offer “appropriate protective measures,” including the possibility of credit-monitoring and identity-protection services.

“Those services will be based on the nature of the information exposed and the risks that were identified,” he said. “So individuals that are eligible to receive this protection will be informed directly and will be given a list of steps to follow in the very near future.”

Jesse joined APTN as a producer after 16 years as a print and web journalist. During seven of those years, he covered the Cree Nation of Eeyou Istchee for community newsmagazine The Nation. Jesse’s writing on Indigenous issues has also appeared in Canadian Geographic, the Toronto Star, the Rover, The Eastern Door, Metro, and the Huffington Post.

author: Scott Timcke
title: The Stories Shaping Africa’s AI Future
content:
In the boardrooms of Addis Ababa and the tech hubs of Nairobi, a new worldmaking project is underway. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become one of the central arenas where African states negotiate their position in an unequal global order. To speak of “AI in Africa” is not simply to describe the arrival of a technology, but to encounter a set of competing discursive frames through which political desires, developmental ambitions, ethical claims, and governance priorities are translated into technical agendas. As national strategies and regional protocols are rolled out, what comes into view is a struggle over how Africa is imagined within this machine age, and what kinds of futures that imagination makes thinkable.


These frames are not simply different ways of describing a new technology. They are competing scripts for what Africa is, what AI is for, and who ought to shape its future. Some cast the continent as a site of leapfrogging and renewal; others as a zone of exposure, extraction, sovereignty, moral repair, or improvised adaptation. Each brings some actors and possibilities into focus while pushing others to the margins. That is why the issue is not only what AI means for Africa, but what pictures of Africa are being called into view through AI discourse.


The first terrain is shaped by promise and protection. One of the most pervasive registers is promissory. In the African renaissance 2.0 frame, visible in the

AU Continental AI Strategy

, AI appears as a

leapfrogging

 device through which Africa can bypass the chokepoint of traditional industrialization and enter prosperity through technical modernization. Here, the ethical subject is the developmental state or planner charged with delivering growth, inclusion, and renewal. What comes into view is capacity, competitiveness, and beneficial transformation. What recedes from view are the historical and political-economic conditions that make acceleration so attractive in the first place: debt, infrastructural dependence, uneven ownership, and the possibility that AI may deepen rather than overcome inherited asymmetries.


Running alongside this is a protective register. In this vulnerability frame, Africa is not late but exposed to surveillance, bias, exclusion, and systems introduced into settings where safeguards are weak and redress is limited. As the

CIVICUS report on AI surveillance in Africa

 suggests, the issue is not only future risk but already existing forms of technologically mediated harm. The ethical subject here is the harm-bearing population—the data subject, precarious worker, surveilled citizen, and linguistically marginal user most likely to absorb the costs of badly governed AI. This frame is ethically indispensable because it foregrounds rights, harm, and institutional fragility, including the uneven but growing architecture of data protection on the continent. Its limit, however, is that it can cast Africa chiefly as a site to be protected rather than one from which technological futures are actively contested and shaped.


A second terrain is shaped by structure and sovereignty. Alongside these promissory and protective registers sits a more structural critique. In the

anti-colonial frame

, AI appears as a socio-technical order built through unequal material relations: not only data extraction, but also mineral supply chains, outsourced labor, environmental degradation, foreign-owned infrastructures, and asymmetrical control over the institutions that govern digital life. From this perspective, Africa is not outside the AI order looking in; it is already deeply inserted into it, though often on subordinated terms. The ethical subject is the dispossessed worker, community, or polity whose labor, resources, and data are drawn into AI systems while ownership and value are captured elsewhere. What becomes visible is the political economy of AI—an approach that makes it harder to sustain the comforting idea that Africa’s main problem is simply one of readiness or delayed entry. But the frame has limits. In foregrounding dispossession, it can flatten internal differentiation, externalize agency too completely, and become so totalizing that the uneven realities of negotiation and strategic inhabitation recede from view.


The sovereignty frame shifts the question from extraction to control: AI is cast as a problem of authority over infrastructure, procurement, standards, and rulemaking, a concern visible in South Africa’s

National …

title: Dr. Korkmaz: Turkey may pay a heavy price for military alliances
content:
Tensions between Iran and Israel, the new political landscape in Syria, escalating conflicts in Yemen and the Mecca Defence Pact are reshaping the balance of power in the Middle East. Relations between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Egypt and the Gulf states, the position of the Kurds in regional developments and the future of the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey are also among the major issues on the regional agenda.


Dr. Toros Korkmaz spoke to ANF about developments in the Middle East, regional power relations and the future of the peace process in Turkey.


'Power struggles in the Middle East bring both risks and opportunities'


Korkmaz said that the Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey began at a time of continuing wars and power struggles in the Middle East, and that it could not be considered independently of the uncertainties created by these developments.


Korkmaz said: "Opportunities and risks do not emerge in isolation. This is actually a dialectical process. If we look at the peace process, a very serious perception of a security threat emerged in Israel following Hamas's attack on Israel on 7 October 2023. This prompted Israel to put its plan to reshape the Middle East into action. Following this plan, we witnessed the fragmentation of Syria, then the Israel-Iran war backed by the United States, and the direct involvement of the US in that war. The peace process came onto the agenda after all these developments. Frankly, I do not think such a peace process could have begun under the present circumstances if this environment of war had not emerged and if the Turkish government and state had not been aware of Israel's plan to reshape the Middle East. That is why I believe the 7 October attack was very important."


'A possible war with Iran will affect the process in Turkey'


Korkmaz said that the direction of the Kurdish question could change amid the ongoing armed conflicts in the Middle East, particularly the threat of war involving Iran. He warned of the risks arising from Turkey's reluctance to move the process forward.


Korkmaz also said: "Consider what would happen if Iran were severely weakened by the Iran-Israel war and entered a process of fragmentation. In that case, the possibility of Kurds in Eastern Kurdistan (Rojhilat) gaining increasing autonomy would emerge. This would put pressure on Turkey. Under such circumstances, Turkey might decide to continue the peace process. However, a different picture could emerge if the current stalemate continues and the Turkish state concludes that Israel has reached the limits of its power and no longer has the capacity to advance further or reshape the Middle East. If such a perception develops within the Turkish state, there may be a tendency to freeze or slow down the peace process, or to limit reforms as much as possible.


Therefore, how the war ends, who emerges victorious and what kind of regional situation develops afterwards are extremely important. Will Iran fragment or remain intact? What are the limits of Israel's power? All these questions will be decisive."


'National consciousness and aspirations are growing among Kurds'


Korkmaz said that the war concerned not only Turkey and the Turkish state but also the development of Kurdish national consciousness throughout the conflict.


Korkmaz said: "National consciousness is growing among Kurds across all four parts of Kurdistan, in Syria, Iraq, Iran and Turkey. Kurds recognise that the Middle East has become a region engulfed in conflict and that they can survive this period only by strengthening unity and solidarity among themselves. I believe this is an important development.


The Kurdish dynamic must be taken into account. It cannot be ignored. Kurds are becoming increasingly aware of their national identity and are organising across all four parts of Kurdistan. What have we witnessed during this process? For example, for the first time, all Kurdish parties in Iran came together. Organisations that previously seemed incapable of coming together found common ground. In Turkey, particularly in Northern Kurdistan, there has also been a significant increase in national consciousness. At times when Kurdish rights were violated in Rojava and the region was under threat, Kurds mobilised not only in Turkey but also across Europe.


War creates existential conditions, and such circumstances can contribute positively to the development of national consciousness among …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Jeffries, Who’s Pledged to End Trump’s War on Iran, Says “No” on Defunding It
content:
Jeffries instead advocated for a war powers resolution that Trump would likely completely ignore.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Despite his numerous pledges to work “aggressively” to end the war on Iran, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-New York) suggested this week that he opposes efforts to defund the war, as some progressives and moderate Democrats have called for.

A small but vocal group of Senate and House Democrats have said that they wish to move to end the Iran war immediately, starting with barring funding for war efforts in the government funding package due by December 11. This, experts have said, is one of the strongest tools that Democrats have at their disposal to end the war; in fact, they say, it may be the only way to force the lawless Trump administration to withdraw troops.

On Tuesday, Jeffries said he’s a “no” for that effort.

In an interview at The Atlantic Summit, Jeffries said that Democrats must “move aggressively to end the reckless and costly war of choice in Iran right out of the gate” when they take the majority in January, dismissing by omission the chance to act before then, despite Democrats’ leverage to do so.

Jeffries criticized President Donald Trump’s conduct of the war, saying that there is “no plan” or “strategy” for the war, and that Democrats must “aggressively” pass a war powers resolution. That would “take the fight around ending the war to the Oval Office,” Jeffries said.

“What does ending the war mean? Not funding their operations in the Gulf?” asked interviewer Jeffrey Goldberg, editor-in-chief of The Atlantic.

“Well, no,” said Jeffries. “It means a cessation of hostilities…. So that’s what a war powers resolution is able to do, right?”

When asked what the strategy is if Trump vetoes the resolution, Jeffries simply said that his plan is to make it so that vetoing such a resolution — or a bill to reenter the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) — would be embarrassing for Trump.

Jeffries, who House Democrats elected to lead the caucus as speaker in the new Congress on Wednesday, did not once acknowledge that Iran also has a major say in ending the war, despite Goldberg asking him about Iran’s role multiple times.

Indeed, for months, Iranian leaders have been consistently asking that the U.S. follow the memorandum of understanding that the U.S. and Iran struck in June. That agreement, which Trump unilaterally broke, stipulated an end to the U.S.’s strikes, naval blockade, and sanctions, in exchange for Iran ending its retaliatory strikes, renewing its pledge to not develop nuclear weapons, and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

Jeffries also did not acknowledge that the Trump administration, which experts say has already broken numerous laws to wage this war, is likely to completely ignore any stipulations on the war placed by a war powers resolution.

The presumptive speaker-elect also suggested on Tuesday that he’ll help grant funding for the war through year’s end.

According to Punchbowl, Jeffries said that he’s in “active conversation” with congressional leaders “to arrive at either a government funding agreement in advance of Dec. 11 that meets the needs of the American people in terms of their health, their safety, their national security, and their economic well-being, or we have to move toward a continuing resolution of funding that would put us into some point next year with Democrats holding the gavels in both the House and the Senate.”

The statement suggests that he isn’t in favor of efforts by figures like Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Maryland) to use the December funding deadline to defund the war.

The remarks are an about-face from Jeffries. For months, he has pledged to work to end Trump’s Iran war. In a press conference last Thursday, he even acknowledged that Democrats are opposed to funding it.

“House Democrats have uniformly opposed providing any additional money to Donald Trump’s war machine, to Pete Hegseth’s war machine over in the Middle East,” he said.

At the same time, however, he is not endorsing any of the legislative efforts to actually force an end to the war, only advocating for efforts to will that outcome into existence through an abstract pressure campaign.

“Jeffries’ Iran position is Trump needs to ‘end the war’ but he absolutely cannot do so without Iran agreeing to humiliating terms, zero …

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Man Charged With Destroying £45m US Warplane Using Axe and Ball Bearings
content:
An Irish man “effectively destroyed” a £45m ($60m) US military aircraft using an axe and ball bearings, prosecutors have alleged. 


Daithí Ó Corráin, 48, is accused of sneaking onto the tarmac at Shannon Airport in County Clare, Ireland, and barricading himself inside a US Air National Guard C-130 Hercules aircraft, before causing extensive damage to the plane. 


Ó Corráin allegedly cut wires and hydraulic lines, smashed every gauge in the cockpit, damaged the aircraft’s exterior with an axe, and poured ball bearings into its fuel tank. 


Prosecutors in New York have charged Ó Corráin, also known as David Curran, with destruction of government property, which carries a maximum prison sentence of ten years. 


Ó Corráin is alleged to have researched and planned the April 2026 attack for months

according to court filings

 unsealed by prosecutors on Tuesday. 


“The damage inflicted rendered the aircraft inoperable,” the indictment states, “and based on the extent of the damage, the aircraft – worth approximately $60m – will not return to active flight status.” 


The aircraft was “en route to another country on US military assignment”, it adds.


Shannon Airport serves as a key hub for US troops and military equipment, and has been the site of frequent anti-war protests and

monthly peace vigils

 opposing American aggression in the Middle East.


The C-130 Hercules aircraft is a military transport plane described

by the US Air Force

 as “the prime transport for airdropping troops and equipment into hostile areas”. 


An

online fundraiser

 set up by people describing themselves as Ó Corráin’s friends and comrades says Ó Corráin is an “independent peace activist”. It suggests the alleged action was taken in protest of the US-Israel war on Iran and the US-funded genocide Israel is committing in Gaza.  


Ó Corráin was

arrested at the scene

 and charged by Ireland’s national police with causing criminal damage.


Protesters have repeatedly breached the perimeter at Shannon Airport in recent years, with US prosecutors noting that three people were

arrested for driving a van

 through the fence in May 2025 and three others allegedly spray-painted a US aircraft later the same month.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Birds of War": New Film Tells a Story of Love and Journalism from Syria to Lebanon
content:
We speak with Janay Boulos and Abd Alkader Habak, filmmakers and subjects of the new documentary

Birds of War

, which tells their epic love story through years of upheaval in the Middle East. Boulos, a London-based Lebanese journalist working for the

BBC

, and Habak, a Syrian activist and cameraman, first connected while covering the Syrian civil war and stayed in touch through years of war, revolution and exile, forming a relationship that is chronicled in the documentary by drawing on 13 years of their personal videos, voice notes and other correspondence.


The film also examines the unequal relationship between international news organizations and local journalists whose work they rely on, the fraught political history between Syria and Lebanon, and how Boulos and Habak’s personal connection overcame those divisions.


“Without our journalistic relationship, [we] would have never been together. I would have never opened my heart to somebody like him,” says Boulos. “We can be any race, any gender, any religion, any background, but at the same time we’re all humans.”


Birds of War

 premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, where it won the World Cinema Documentary Special Jury Award for Journalistic Impact.

title: Milli Savunma Bakanlığı bütçesinde silahlanmada yüzde 229 artış: Askeri sanayi şirketlerinde kârları patlatmaya devam
content:
Dicle Sezen Öz [email protected]

Milli Savunma Bakanlığının (MSB) 2027 bütçesine ilişkin görüşmeler bugün TBMM Plan ve Bütçe Komisyonunda başlıyor. MSB’nin yeni bütçesi, Ankara’da yapılan NATO zirvesinde alınan kararlar, Suudi Arabistan ve Pakistan ile 10 yıl süreyle bağlayıcı olacak şekilde imzalanan Mekke Anlaşması ve Türkiye’nin başta cihatçı HTŞ yönetimindeki Suriye olmak üzere Ortadoğu ve Afrika’da askeri varlığını büyüttüğü bir dönemde görüşülecek.

AKP iktidarı ve askeri sanayi şirketleri yeni siparişler için kapı kapı gezerken, bütçe teklifinde öne çıkan başlık ‘savunma’ ve güvenlik harcamalarındaki rekor artış oldu. Cumhurbaşkanı Yardımcısı Cevdet Yılmaz’ın da bütçe sunumunda belirttiği üzere silah ve mühimmat alımına ayrılan ödenek yüzde 229 oranında artırılıyor.

2026 yılında 822.9 milyar TL olan MSB bütçesi, 2027 teklifinde yüzde 86.2’lik artışla 1 trilyon 532.6 milyar liraya çıkarılıyor. Bu artışın 573.9 milyar lirası mal ve hizmet alımlarından kaynaklanıyor. Bu kalem yüzde 158.2 artışla 936.6 milyar liraya çıkıyor. Yani 2027 bütçesindeki her 100 liranın 61 lirası bu mal ve hizmetlere yani ‘silah ve mühimmata’ gidecek.

Savaş harcamalarındaki artış Savunma Sanayii Destekleme Fonu (SSDF) ve iç güvenlik birimlerini de kapsayan güvenlik bütçesinde de görülüyor. Söz konusu iki kalemin 2.15 trilyon liradan 3.45 trilyon liraya yükselerek merkezi yönetim bütçesinin yüzde 12.7’sine denk gelmesi bekleniyor. Bu toplam içinde doğrudan ‘savunmaya’ ayrılan pay ise yüzde 83.5 artışla 2.2 trilyon liraya çıkacak.

Aselsan, Roketsan, Tusaş, MKE ve Baykar gibi askeri sanayi şirketlerine akan para, genel bütçe dışında tutulan ve Merkez Bankası nezdinde yönetilen SSDF üzerinden sağlanıyor. Teklifin 10. maddesi, silah alımları ve NATO altyapı yatırımlarında bütçe ödenekleriyle birlikte SSDF kaynaklarının da kullanılmasına imkan tanıyor.

Halktan toplanan vergilerin nasıl şirket kasalarına aktığı Sayıştayın son denetim raporlarıyla da belgeleniyor. Sayıştay verilerine göre SSDF’nin geliri 2025’te yüzde 73.8 artışla 374.5 milyar liraya; bu paranın yüzde 99’unun harcandığı ve çoğunluğu silahlara giden mal ve hizmet alım gideri ise 275.2 milyar liraya çıktı.

Bütçenin diğer yüzünde ise iktidarla kol kola olan askeri sanayi şirketlerinin hızla büyüyen kârları var.

Aselsan’ın 2026 yılının ilk dokuz ayındaki net kârı, geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 75.1 artarak 15.1 milyar liradan 26.5 milyar liraya kadar yükseldi. Şirketin aynı dönemdeki 151.5 milyar liralık toplam gelirinin yüzde 42’sine denk gelen 63.9 milyar liralık kısmı doğrudan Savunma Sanayii Başkanlığına yapılan satışlardan elde edildi ve elindeki bekleyen sipariş tutarı 30.7 milyar dolara ulaştı.

Baykar 2025 için 2,5 milyar dolar gelir açıklarken, Tusaş’ın üretimden satışları 140.9 milyar lirayı buldu.

Bunlar yalnızca öne çıkan şirketlerin birkaçı. Savunma Sanayii Başkanı Haluk Görgün, geçtiğimiz ay Bursa’da katıldığı bir çalıştayda yıl başından bu yana askeri sanayide 15 milyar dolarlık yeni sözleşme imzalandığını söyledi. Görgün, Aselsan, Roketsan, Tusaş, Havelsan ve STM’nin yurt içindeki alt yüklenicilerine verdiği ve henüz tamamlanmamış siparişlerin tutarının da 13.4 milyar doları aştığını açıkladı.

MSB’ye bütçeden ayrılan bu payın bu denli büyümesinin bir sebebi hiç şüphesiz iktidarın yıl boyu altına imzasını attığı uluslararası anlaşmalar. Son bir yılda askeri sanayi hem yeni iç siparişlerle hem de yeni anlaşmalar ve dış satışlarla yeni pazarlara açıldı. Geçen yılki komisyon görüşmesiyle aynı gün imzalanan 6.5 milyar dolarlık hava savunma paketini, bu yıl ekim ayında Aselsan ile imzalanan 2,46 milyar avroluk hava savunma sözleşmeleri ve mayıs ayında Tusaş ile bağlanan yurt içi Kaan savaş uçağı tedarik anlaşması izledi.

Türkiye, ekim 2025’te Birleşik Krallık’tan 20 Eurofighter savaş uçağı almak için 8 milyar sterline varan bir anlaşmaya imza attı. Mart 2026’da imzalanan eğitim ve destek sözleşmesiyle de BAE Systems ve Rolls-Royce dahil Britanyalı şirketlere iş alanı açıldı. Öte yandan Katar’dan ikinci el Eurofighter alımı için görüşmelerini sürdüren MSB, ekimde Doha’dan satış sözleşmesi taslağını beklediğini bildirdi.

Türkiye’deki askeri sanayi patronlarının bir gözü de dışarıya satışlarda. Bu kapsamda Tusaş, İspanya’nın Airbus liderliğindeki eğitim programı için 30 adet Hürjet, Azerbaycan için ise 14 adet Hürkuş-II üretecek. title: Pisa, depositi di esplosivi: la città sempre più esposta ai rischi della guerra
content:
Due nuovi depositi di munizioni a San Giusto, un hangar da 40 milioni e un aeroporto che ogni anno accoglie quasi sei milioni di passeggeri. Chi garantisce la sicurezza della popolazione?


Un’interessante inchiesta condotta dal

Movimento No Base.


All’interno dell’aeroporto militare di Pisa vogliono realizzare due nuovi depositi destinati allo stoccaggio di esplosivi e munizionamento. Non si tratta di un’ipotesi o di un progetto ancora indefinito. A confermarlo è il capitolato speciale d’appalto dell’Aeronautica Militare, che descrive nel dettaglio le opere previste, le loro finalità e i costi.


Il progetto prevede la costruzione di due riservette di tipo igloo, strutture in cemento armato destinate alla conservazione di materiale esplosivo, accompagnate da bastionature di protezione, una tettoia per lo stoccaggio temporaneo degli esplosivi, una recinzione perimetrale con cancello carrabile elettrificato e un locale uffici. L’importo a base di gara è di oltre 5,5 milioni di euro. Il 28 ottobre 2026 l’appalto è stato aggiudicato per un impegno complessivo indicato in oltre 6,1 milioni di euro. Secondo la documentazione progettuale resa pubblica da Diritti in Comune, ciascuna delle due strutture sarebbe dimensionata per una capacità indicativa di dieci tonnellate di esplosivo netto equivalente, per un totale iniziale di venti tonnellate. La stessa documentazione segnala inoltre la possibilità di predisporre in futuro altre quattro riservette, che porterebbero la capacità complessiva potenziale a sessanta tonnellate.


Ma il dato che più dovrebbe richiamare l’attenzione della cittadinanza non è soltanto la quantità di materiale che potrà essere conservata. È la funzione che queste strutture sono chiamate a svolgere. Il capitolato spiega infatti che la necessità di stoccare munizionamento e materiali esplosivi, indicati con la denominazione 

HOT CARGO

, deriva da esigenze operative direttamente collegate all’attività di volo e alla presenza di un 

Air Terminal Operation Centre

 della JMOU Italia. Non siamo quindi davanti a un intervento edilizio generico all’interno di un’area militare: l’obiettivo dichiarato è dotare lo scalo di una nuova capacità di deposito e gestione di munizionamento ed esplosivi funzionale alle attività militari, anche a quelle connesse ai teatri di guerra.


È questo passaggio che rende il progetto particolarmente rilevante per Pisa. La città ospita la 46ª Brigata Aerea, uno dei principali reparti italiani per il trasporto militare di personale, mezzi e materiali. L’aeroporto militare costituisce una componente essenziale del sistema infrastrutturale della Difesa, ma si trova anche al centro di un contesto urbano densamente abitato e condivide lo spazio aeroportuale con lo scalo civile Galileo Galilei. La realizzazione dei depositi aggiunge dunque una funzione nuova e significativa a un’infrastruttura che già svolge un ruolo militare rilevante.


Un aeroporto, due funzioni, milioni di passeggeri


C’è un elemento che rende la vicenda pisana particolarmente delicata e che non può essere lasciato sullo sfondo: l’aeroporto militare non è un’infrastruttura separata dalla vita civile della città. La gestione dello scalo civile è affidata a Toscana Aeroporti, società il cui presidente è 

Marco Carrai

, che ricopre anche l’incarico di console onorario dello Stato di Israele per Toscana, Emilia-Romagna e Lombardia. Il sedime e le infrastrutture militari fanno invece capo all’Aeronautica Militare. Le due funzioni convivono nello stesso sistema aeroportuale.


Nel 2025 lo scalo ha registrato quasi sei milioni di passeggeri. A questi numeri si aggiungono le centinaia di lavoratrici e lavoratori che ogni giorno operano nei servizi aeroportuali, nella movimentazione delle merci, nella manutenzione, nella sicurezza e nelle attività connesse allo scalo. Intorno all’aeroporto si trovano inoltre quartieri abitati da decine di migliaia di persone, a partire da San Giusto e San Marco. 

Ma non ci sono soltanto le abitazioni e le infrastrutture aeroportuali: nelle vicinanze si sviluppano alcune delle principali arterie di comunicazione della città e dell’intera area pisana, come la via Aurelia e la superstrada Firenze-Pisa-Livorno (Fi-Pi-Li), percorse quotidianamente da un intenso traffico di automobili, mezzi pesanti e lavoratori pendolari. title: Revolutionary groups urge Filipinos to hold Trump accountable over war crimes
content:
The National Democratic Front of the Philippines (NDFP) said US President Donald Trump’s visit to the Philippines would deepen US involvement in the country and serve the foreign country’s interests in Philippine land, resources and labor.


NDFP secretary general Elias Dipasupil in a statement also described the US-led Pax Silica initiative as an escalation in US intervention and oppression in the Philippines.


“Trump, a certified warmonger, is an enemy of peace in the Philippines,” Dipasupil said, adding that the US only seeks to draw the country into conflict with China through increased US military aid and joint US-PH military activities that are also used to suppress the revolutionary movement in the


NDFP allied organizations — Compatriots, an organization of overseas Filipinos; KAGUMA, Alliance of Patriotic Teachers; and Christians for National Liberation (CNL) – said Ferdinand Marcos Jr. government’s subservience to US dictates would only result in economic hardship, resource plunder and violations to Philippine sovereignty.


Compatriots said US domination in the Philippines only worsened economic pressures that lead many Filipinos to seek work abroad. It cited “landlessness, lack of job opportunities, livelihood, low wages and high costs of living.”


KAGUMA criticized projects promoted as sources of jobs, renewable energy and participation in the global artificial-intelligence supply chain which, it said only serve the economic and military interests of the US. It warned that resource extraction could damage the environment, displace Indigenous communities, and intensify landgrabbing.


The group also urged educators to build and promote critical awareness. “Education is a key platform for fostering patriotic awareness,” the underground organization said.


CNL chairperson Renmin Malaya described Trump’s politics as marked by “chaos, militarism, imperial aggression” and called for an independent economy.


He said the Philippines should “develop its own productive capabilities, protect its patrimony, and firmly uphold its sovereignty.” Malaya said that liberation requires militant struggle and cited the international-law concept of

jus ad bellum

 (just war), “to end oppression and exploitation.”


CPP condemns mass arrests of anti-Trump patriots


The Communist Party of the Philippines (CPP), meanwhile, said it stands with Filipinos in absolute condemnation of the widespread mass arrests carried out by the Philippine National Police since Sunday that targeted workers, students, peasants, Indigenous peoples and other sectors who defy Trump and Pax Silica.


The CPP also condemned the arrest of scores of journalists covering the protest actions, as well as paralegals providing assistance.


“The mass arrests, purportedly carried out with so-called maximum tolerance, exposes the Marcos regime’s gross intolerance to protest actions that oppose his subservience to his American masters,” CPP chief information officer Marco Valbuena said.


“Police actions have been coordinated with US Secret Service agents who are in the country ahead of Trump. Marcosian political repression, along with artificial white walls erected to hide impoverished communities, are reminiscent of his father’s old dystopian dictatorship,” Valbuena added.


By ordering the police to forcibly clamp down on all protests, Marcos clearly aims to please his imperialist master Trump that may be a prelude to even more brutal acts of suppression that will drive away communities to pave the way for imperialist plunder of the country’s patrimony, CPP said.


“Contrary to Marcos’ aims, however, intensified fascist repression is certain to succeed only in fueling greater resistance of the Filipino people to US imperialism’s Pax Silica with its aims of expanding its economic and geopolitical interests in the Philippines,” Valbuena warned. #

title: Anti-Bases Movement Going Strong on Jeju Island
content:
By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, November 17, 2026


The photo above is an old one. The base protest has been happening on Jeju Island for years. Now the destruction has been done, the base been built, and the war ships come and go. On Tuesday, there were no U.S. Navy ships present, just Korean war ships, one of them likely to soon be sent to the war on Iran, as well as a submarine, and Chinese cruise ships arriving. There is also a new rocket-launching platform that is taken out miles off the coast to launch rockets. A week ago, someone

died

 in a rocket operation. Hanwha, the company involved, has many branch corporations. One of them is Hanwha Defense USA which builds U.S. warships in Philadelphia.


The massive base on Jeju Island was created in large part for the U.S. Navy, and the protests denounce the latest U.S. wars.


As part of a display along a road approaching the base is this image of the beloved Gureombi Rock, almost all of which was destroyed by the base construction.


A sign indicates the number of daily protests as of today: 7,124.


Every morning for 7,124 mornings, protesters have taken their message to the base.


Every late-morning for 7,124 late-mornings, a Catholic mass has been followed by a noon protest at the base.


Protesters suspect that this ship, docked at the base, may soon be sent to join Trump’s war on Iran, on behalf of the people of Korea who have zero interest in participating in such reckless, murderous crimes. To the left above is the rocket launcher. Top center is a world cup stadium.

title: Animal Rising Disrupts National Pig Awards in Central London Following Campaigner Arrests
content:
Animal Rising campaigners disrupted the National Pig Awards at the Royal Lancaster Hotel in central London this evening (16 November), while protesters outside blocked the main entrance. Police were called to the venue.

Despite enhanced security, six campaigners reached the event and were subsequently apprehended before being ejected from the hotel at approximately 7 pm. Around 70 protesters gathered outside as attendees arrived, holding placards reading “Free Luna” and “End Factory Farming”.

The group publicly declared its intention to shut down the awards last week, calling for Red Court, a pig factory farm in Suffolk, to release Luna, a mother pig whose life of confinement was filmed continuously for over a month by Animal Rising earlier this year. [1]

The investigation documented squalid conditions and illegal piglet thumping on the Red Tractor Assured farm. [2] Over 40,000 people have since signed a petition calling for Luna’s release to a sanctuary. [3]

The group filmed Luna confined in a narrow farrowing crate for five weeks, unable to turn around or take more than a step forward. A sanctuary has since offered her a home for the rest of her life. [4]

Red Court confirmed last week that Luna is once again in a farrowing crate. If the farm refuses to release her, she will remain there for approximately another month, confined with her newborn piglets, before she is removed and re-inseminated.

The farm has also rejected a proposed £5,000 donation to You Are Not Alone, an East Anglian charity supporting farmers’ mental health, in exchange for Luna’s release. [5]

Earlier today, Animal Rising announced that a third campaigner, Michelle Farnham, had been arrested on suspicion of burglary following the open rescue of three piglets (Leila, Nova and Maia) from Red Court.

Before the rescue, Animal Rising reported serious welfare concerns at the farm to the police, RSPCA and Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA).

APHA, the body responsible for enforcing farmed animal welfare, informed Animal Rising that the farm’s conditions, including the illegal thumping of a piglet, were normal.

Farnham attended Stoke Newington Police Station at 10 am this morning. Her fellow rescuers, Thomas Cusick and Liam Shaughnessy, had previously reported themselves to the police and been arrested. [6]

Farnham, 26, Animal Rising’s Campaign Lead, attracted national attention in September when she spent 21 days and nights locked in a farrowing crate in Trafalgar Square, highlighting Luna’s story and the suffering of animals in factory farms. High-profile visitors included Chris Packham and Green MP Adrian Ramsay. [7]

Animal Rising is campaigning for a government commitment to end UK factory farming by 2040.

author: Tobias Schalyo
title: PETA x Adventsome – vegane Adventskalender: Infos zur Verlosung und die Gründer:innen im Interview
content:
Werbung | Die

Weihnachtszeit

 rückt näher und mit ihr die Vorfreude auf kleine tägliche Überraschungen. Gemeinsam mit Adventsome verlosen wir von PETA Deutschland daher drei vegane Adventskalender voller

pflanzlicher Snacks

 und Infos zur Unterstützung gemeinnütziger Projekte. Der vegane Adventskalender zeigt, wie vielfältig, lecker und kreativ die Weihnachtszeit sein kann – mit vielen rein veganen Überraschungen. 


Über unsere Social-Media-Kanäle verlosen wir insgesamt drei vegane Adventskalender von Adventsome im Wert von jeweils 149 Euro. Mit etwas Glück können Sie sich oder Ihren Liebsten eine ganz besondere tierfreundliche Vorweihnachtszeit schenken. 


Teilnahmezeitraum: 13.11.2026 bis 16.11.2026

 


Inhaltsübersicht


									Interview mit Adventsome: Lea und Josias im Gespräch zum veganen Adventskalender


									Alle Infos zur PETA x Adventsome-Verlosung


									Lust auf noch mehr vegane Adventskalender?


Interview mit Adventsome: Lea und Josias im Gespräch zum veganen Adventskalender


Wir haben mit den Gründer:innen des Start-ups Adventsome – Lea und Josias – ein Interview geführt, um die Menschen hinter dem Projekt und den Gedanken hinter dem veganen Adventskalender vorzustellen: Welche Motivation treibt sie an, welche Rolle spielen Tiere bei Entscheidungen und wie kann ein Adventskalender über die Weihnachtszeit hinaus etwas bewegen? 


Lea und Josias – die Gründer:innen des Start-ups Adventsome.


PETA: Nehmt uns mit an den Anfang: Wie wurde aus eurer persönlichen Begeisterung für Adventskalender die Idee zu Adventsome?


Gab es einen bestimmten Moment, in dem ihr dachtet: „Genau so einen Kalender möchten wir selbst entwickeln“?

 


Adventsome:

 Die Idee kam uns, als wir uns 2017 gegenseitig Adventskalender schenken wollten, aber uns keiner wirklich begeistern konnte. Wir wünschten uns einen, der uns mit jedem Türchen aufs Neue überrascht, ganz viele unterschiedliche Produktkategorien vereint und in einer sinnvollen Verpackung kommt, die nicht nach 24 Tagen im Müll landet. Die zwei Kalender, die wir daraufhin selbst bastelten, haben uns im Dezember so viel Freude bereitet, dass wir beschlossen haben, diese auch mit anderen zu teilen. Ein Jahr später brachten wir unsere ersten 500 Adventskalender auf den Markt, die wir damals alle selbst neben der Uni verpackten – das waren ganze 12.000 einzelne Geschenke! 


PETA: Weihnachten verbinden viele Menschen mit Mitgefühl und Nächstenliebe. Welche Rolle spielen Tiere für euch dabei – und wie hat das eure Entscheidung für einen vollständig veganen Adventskalender geprägt?

  


Adventsome

: Wir lieben Tiere, haben selbst auch zwei

Katzen adoptiert

 und uns jahrelang im Tierschutz engagiert. Mit Adventsome möchten wir daher keine Produkte unterstützen, für die Tiere leiden müssen. Gleichzeitig finden wir es spannend, wie vielfältig das vegane Sortiment mittlerweile ist und wie viele innovative Alternativen es gibt. Genau den Brands, die diese Entwicklung weiter vorantreiben, möchten wir eine Bühne geben und ihnen helfen, bekannter zu werden. Unser Adventskalender soll Menschen dafür begeistern, Neues auszuprobieren und vielleicht auch die eine oder andere Gewohnheit zu hinterfragen! 


PETA: Euer Kalender verbindet 20 Produkte von Start-ups mit vier Spendentürchen. Was sollen Menschen beim Auspacken erleben – und was soll davon nach dem 24. Dezember bleiben?

 


Adventsome

: Wir wünschen uns, dass unsere Kund:innen jeden Morgen mit echter Vorfreude ein Türchen öffnen. Das schönste Feedback ist für uns, wenn uns jemand schreibt, dass er oder sie wieder kindliche Neugier verspürt. Richtige Überraschungen sind im Erwachsenenleben so selten geworden! 


Nach Weihnachten bleiben soll zunächst einmal unsere weiterverwendbare Design-Box, die wir jedes Jahr mit einer Künstlerin gemeinsam kreieren. Außerdem hoffentlich ganz viele neue Gedankenanstöße und Perspektiven und vielleicht auch das ein oder andere Lieblingsprodukt? 


Lea und Josias engagieren sich seit Jahren im Tierschutz und haben selbst zwei Katzen adoptiert.


PETA: Von Snacks über Pflege bis zu Alltagsprodukten: Wo findet ihr die Überraschungen, die es in euren Kalender schaffen?

  


Adventsome

: Die wichtigste Frage ist immer: Würden wir uns selbst darüber freuen, wenn wir morgens das Türchen öffnen? Das Produkt muss zudem vegan, unisex und alkoholfrei sein und auch darüber hinaus mit unseren Werten matchen!

author: Benji
title: Grossdemo gegen Tönnies
content:
Grossdemo gegen Tönnies

Wir demonstrieren am 21.11. in Kellinghusen

Ihr seid wütend auf Tönnies? Wir auch! Wir haben

dokumentiert

, was Schweine bei Tönnies wirklich erleiden müssen. Wir haben bei Tönnies in Rheda-Wiedenbrück protestiert. Doch Tönnies tötet weiter. Deshalb fahren wir jetzt nochmal groß auf und demonstrieren an dem Schlachthof, aus dem die Aufnahmen unserer Aufdeckung stammen: Kellinghusen.


Bist du dabei?


Samstag, 21.11.2026

14:00 – 17:00 Uhr

Unterer Marktplatz, 25548 Kellinghusen

Hintergrundinfos


Rideshare-Tool

Damit möglichst viele Menschen zur Demo gegen Tönnies kommen, wollen wir euch bei der Planung eurer Anreise unterstützen. Daher haben wir ein cleveres Rideshare-Tool entwickelt, mit dem ihr Fahrgemeinschaften bilden könnt. So wird die Anreise für euch günstiger, einfacher und spaßiger.


Jetzt einsteigen!

Warum demonstrieren wir?

Anlass für die Großdemo am 21. November ist unsere aktuelle Veröffentlichung „Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies“. Tönnies ist Deutschlands größter Schlachtkonzern und gilt als eines der mächtigsten Unternehmen der europäischen Fleischindustrie. Als Marktführer tötet Tönnies jedes Jahr 16 Millionen Schweine. Unsere Aufdeckung zeigt den grausamen Erstickungskampf der Tiere in der CO₂-Anlage. Die Schweine schreien vor Angst und versuchen zu fliehen.


Was wir bisher getan haben

Gewalt im Schlachthof aufgedeckt

Verstöße dokumentiert

Tönnies angezeigt

Eine große Welle an Presseberichten ausgelöst

Zahlreiche Interviews geführt

Eine politische und gesellschaftliche Debatte angestoßen

Bei der Tönnies-Zentrale in Rheda-Wiedenbrück protestiert

Hintergrundinfos

Und jetzt?

Die Gewalt im Schlachthaus geht unvermindert weiter! Wir sind wütend. Deshalb fahren wir jetzt nochmal ganz groß auf, bündeln unsere Kräfte an einem Termin und demonstrieren gemeinsam mit euch an genau dem Schlachthof, aus dem die Aufnahmen unserer Aufdeckung stammen:

Kellinghusen!


Unsere Forderung: Der Betrieb muss schließen!


Ablauf und Programm

14:00 Uhr: Auftakt


Wir starten mit einer Auftaktkundgebung mit Redebeiträgen auf dem Unteren Marktplatz.

Demozug


Als großer und lauter Demozug ziehen wir mit Schildern, Bannern und Fahnen durch Kellinghusen, skandieren lautstark und setzen ein starkes Zeichen.

Zwischenstopp am Schlachthof


Die Demoroute führt uns bis zum Schlachthof. Dort gibt es weitere Redebeiträge.

Abschlusskundgebung


Gemeinsam laufen wir zurück zum Unteren Marktplatz, wo die Demo nach einer Abschlusskundgebung endet.

So kannst du mithelfen

Du willst mithelfen, dass die Demo richtig groß wird? Dann unterstütze uns bei der Mobilisierung: Bring deine Freund*innen mit zur Demo, teile unseren

Content auf Social Media

 oder poste selbst unser Sharepic:


Demoregeln

Bitte beachtet unsere allgemeinen Demohinweise, damit sich alle wohlfühlen. Danke für euer Verständnis und eure Mithilfe!


1. Antispeziesistisch und abolitionistisch

Einen Ansatz, die Ausbeutung der Tiere zu reformieren und somit im Grundsatz beizubehalten, verfolgen wir nicht. Unsere Forderungen sind grundsätzlich antispeziesistisch und abolitionistisch. Wir bitten deshalb ausdrücklich darum, auf der Demo vermeintliche „Zwischenschritte“ oder „Reformen“ (z. B. Biofleischkonsum oder Verbesserung der Haltungsbedingungen) nicht als Ziel zu kommunizieren.

2. Kein Platz für Menschenfeindlichkeit

ARIWA lehnt alle Formen allgemeiner und gruppenbezogener Menschenfeindlichkeit (wie zum Beispiel Ableismus, Antisemitismus, Homo- und Trans*feindlichkeit, Rassismus oder Sexismus) sowie verschwörungsideologische Denkmuster ab. Personen mit solchen Hintergründen sind bei der Demo ausdrücklich nicht erwünscht. Mehr Infos:

ariwa.org/selbstverstaendnis

3. Keine Kleidung tierischen Ursprungs

Bitte tragt nach Möglichkeit keine Kleidung tierischen Ursprungs und achtet darauf, dass sie auch nicht so aussieht. Denn Produkte wie Kunstpelz oder Kunstleder können missverstanden werden und für Außenstehende einen falschen Eindruck erwecken.

4. Keine Partei- oder Religionswerbung

Parteiwerbung, Werbung für religiöse Gruppierungen sowie Holocaust-Vergleiche sind nicht erwünscht.

5. Bitte keine Tiere mitbringen

Aufgrund von Lärm, Hitze und Enge bitten wir euch, keine Tiere mit zur Demo zu bringen.

Grossdemo gegen Tönnies

title: Enquête élevage de cochons E.Leclerc
content:
L214 publie sa onzième enquête sur les conditions de vie désastreuses des cochons élevés pour E.Leclerc. Les images proviennent d’un élevage intensif de cochons situé sur la commune de Poullaouen, dans le Finistère (Bretagne). Elles témoignent des infractions répétées et des pratiques sources de souffrance pour les animaux : porcelets castrés à vif, coupe des queues de tous les porcelets et sans anesthésie, meulage des dents systématique...

L214 demande à E.Leclerc de s’engager à respecter la réglementation et à interdire les cages dans les élevages qui l'approvisionnent. L’association se mobilise devant les 16 centrales d'achats de E.Leclerc et porte plainte contre l’élevage et E.Leclerc pour sévices graves et mauvais traitements sur les animaux.

Depuis 2024, l’association L214 a rendu publiques des images issues de onze élevages de cochons approvisionnant les magasins E.Leclerc. Les pratiques qui y ont été constatées sont cruelles et, pour certaines, illégales :

Les truies passent la moitié de leur vie enfermées dans des cages où elles ne peuvent même pas se retourner ;

Les queues des porcelets sont coupées à vif de façon systématique ;

Les porcelets subissent d’autres mutilations, comme le meulage des dents et la castration, souvent sans anesthésie ;

Les cochons sont détenus sur caillebotis, au-dessus de leurs déjections, sans matériaux manipulables (paille, etc.) pour satisfaire leurs besoins essentiels.

En votre qualité de présidents de centrales d’achats (SCA), vous siégez au comité stratégique de E.Leclerc, ce qui vous confère un rôle important dans l’élaboration du consensus interne de l’enseigne. Vous avez la responsabilité de porter au sein de cette instance un engagement contre les pires pratiques d'élevage pour les cochons

Nous, signataires de cette pétition, demandons à E.Leclerc de mettre fin à l’enfermement des truies en cage et de respecter la réglementation, afin d’épargner aux cochons les souffrances les plus extrêmes.

author: hsa_oryx
title: A Licence to Hunt: “Cruel, Inhumane and Selfish” Lauderdale Huntswoman Sentenced: 300 Hours’ Unpaid Work and Ten-Year Dog Ban
content:
Scotland’s first conviction under the Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023 has resulted in a substantial community sentence for ex-huntswoman Claire Bellamy, following evidence gathered by Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs.


Claire Bellamy after breaching the licence.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs.


Former Lauderdale Hunt master and huntswoman Claire Bellamy has been sentenced to 300 hours of unpaid work and banned from owning or keeping most dogs for ten years after being convicted of deliberately hunting a fox with hounds. 


Bellamy appeared at Paisley Sheriff Court on Monday 9th November, where Sheriff Gill imposed the maximum 300 hours of unpaid work permitted under a Community Payback Order, to be completed within 12 months. 


The sentence follows

Bellamy’s conviction in October

, the first secured under Scotland’s Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023.


The prosecution was made possible thanks to footage captured by Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs, who have been documenting the ongoing illegal hunting in Scotland that has continued since the new licensing system became law. 


On the 4th January 2025 – almost 2 years after the new law came into force – Bellamy was hunting with approximately 17 hounds near Kirkton Woods, between Houston in Renfrewshire and Kilmacolm in Inverclyde.


The hunt had obtained a licence from NatureScot, the public body responsible for administering Scotland’s licensing scheme.


However, the licence did not give the hunt unrestricted permission to hunt foxes. It was also strictly restricted to a certain geographical area.


“The recording of the fox being chased by multiple hounds was particularly harrowing to watch.” Sheriff Gill


Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs.


Footage captured by sabs, showed hounds hunting a fox into an open field beyond the boundaries specified in the licence. The dogs were not under control – also a requirement of the licence.


During the trial Sheriff Gill described the footage as harrowing and rejected Bellamy’s claim that she had not deliberately hunted the fox. 


A member of the Glasgow Hunt Sabs filming the hunt as they breach the NatureScot issued license.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs. 


At sentencing the sheriff praised the evidence of the witnesses, singling out the hunt sab who recorded the pursuit.


In contrast, Sheriff Gill addressing Bellamy directly described her actions as “

cruel, inhumane and selfish

”.


“Cruel, inhumane and selfish” – words used by Sheriff Gill to describe Bellamy during her sentencing hearing.  Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs.


The court heard that Bellamy had taken part in approximately 1,500 hunts during her ‘career’ as a fox-killer. Despite this, she had shown no responsibility for what occurred that day.


A background report prepared by probation services for sentencing recorded that Bellamy believed she had done nothing wrong, showed no empathy towards the hunted fox, and considered herself to be the victim of an example being made.


The hounds chasing the fox.


“What you don’t understand is that the law is the law, and you are bound by the law.” Sheriff Gill.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs.


She also complained that Scotland’s legislation made hunting foxes more difficult, to which Sheriff Gill’s response was an astonished

“Ms Bellamy, that is the purpose of the legislation

”.


The court also made it clear that Bellamy was bound by the law regardless of whether she personally agreed with it.


The belief among the hunting community that their traditional animal cruelty should take precedence over legislation designed to protect wildlife was shattered in Paisley Sheriff courts.


Bellamy escaped a custodial sentence, although Sheriff Gill made it clear that prison was a genuine possibility.


Claire Bellamy hunting the fox in breach of the licence.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs.


The Community Payback Order requiring 300 hours of unpaid work was imposed as a direct alternative to imprisonment. Bellamy was further warned that failing to comply with the order could result in her returning to court and potentially receiving a custodial sentence. 


Bellamy was also disqualified from keeping dogs for 10 years, though there is an exemption which allowed her to retain her pet terrier (it would be a terrier wouldn’t it), and the collies she uses in her shepherding work.


Whilst Bellamy is no longer master of the Lauderdale Hunt, this didn’t stop the Lauderdale recently advertising a

‘Newcomers to Trail Hunting Week’

, which was quickly removed …

title: Animal Rights Radicals Destroy Several Hunting Hides in Italy amid Controversy over Hunting Law Reform
content:
Several hunting hides in Veneto have been wrecked and covered in anti-hunting graffiti. Images released by four hunting organisations show the Animal Liberation Front (ALF) signature and messages opposing the reform of Italy’s hunting legislation.

Vandalism against hunting facilities is making headlines in Italy once again. Several hunting hides (capanni da caccia) have been destroyed in the Veneto region, with their structures covered in graffiti opposing hunting and the reform of the legislation governing it in the country.

The incidents were publicly condemned this Wednesday, 4 November, by four organisations in the sector: the Cacciatori Veneti association, CONFAVI, ACR and FCR. The organisations released a gallery of photographs showing the damage to the facilities and the inscriptions left on their structures.

The graffiti includes the familiar ALF signature, standing for Animal Liberation Front (Animal Liberation Front), alongside messages calling for a boycott of the reform of Italy’s hunting law. The symbols visible in the images match those used in previous actions attributed to this animal rights movement.

The organisations accompanied the photographs with a strongly worded message directed at those responsible for the damage: “Destroying other people’s property does not defend any cause; it only demonstrates cowardice.”

The incident comes at a time of heightened tension over the reform of Italy’s hunting legislation. The bill seeks to amend Law 157/1992, which provides the basic legal framework for wildlife protection and the regulation of hunting.

The graffiti found on the Veneto hides directly links the property damage to this legislative controversy. However, the messages written on the facilities do not, on their own, identify the people who carried out the attacks. So far, no information has been released about arrests or police investigations relating to this incident either.

The appearance of the initials ALF recalls other incidents of vandalism recorded in Italy against facilities used by hunters.

One of the most notable previous incidents occurred in December 2019 in Montorfano, in the province of Brescia. On that occasion, eleven hunting hides in the municipalities of Rovato, Cologne and Palazzolo were wrecked. The damage was accompanied by threats and graffiti bearing the Animal Liberation Front signature.

More recently, in December 2025, six hides were destroyed in the Lower Valsugana area, between the municipalities of Grigno and Ospedaletto, in the province of Trento. The structures were found knocked down and marked with offensive messages directed at hunters. The ALF signature was also found in that case.

These previous incidents show that the destruction of hunting facilities is nothing new in Italy. The repeated attacks on hunting hides reveal a problem that goes beyond the war of words between supporters and opponents of hunting.

author: Jana Hoger
title: Update: Polizeihund bei Demo misshandelt – Staatsanwaltschaft stellt Ermittlungen ein
content:
Symbolbild


Bei einer Demonstration gegen den AfD-Parteitag am 11. Januar 2025 in Riesa kam es zu

gewaltsamen Einsätzen

 der sogenannten Polizeihunde. Wir von PETA Deutschland kritisieren dies scharf, erstatten Strafanzeige gegen die Verantwortlichen und fordern, dass der Einsatz von Polizeihunden endlich beendet wird. Erfahren Sie hier, was bei der Demonstration vorgefallen ist und warum Gewalt gegen „Polizeihunde“ kein Einzelfall ist.


Update vom 7. November 2026


Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden stellt Verfahren ein


Nachdem im Januar 2026 ein Video für einen medialen Aufschrei sorgte, das zeigt, wie ein sogenannter

Polizeihund

 bei einer Demonstration gewaltsam gegen einen Demonstranten eingesetzt wurde, erstatteten wir von PETA Deutschland Strafanzeige gegen die Verantwortlichen.


Im August 2026 wurde bekannt, dass die Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden in dem Fall nicht weiter ermittelt – angesichts des traurigen Videos mit absurden Begründungen. Die Staatsanwaltschaft erklärt diese Entscheidung in dem Einstellungsbescheid damit, dass ein „Verstoß gegen das Tierschutzgesetz […] nur vorliegen [würde], wenn man einem Tier ohne vernünftigen Grund aus Rohheit erhebliche Schmerzen zufügen würde.“ Der im Video dokumentierte Umgang des Beamten mit dem Hund sei keine „Rohheit“ im Sinne des Tierschutzgesetzes, da die ergriffene „Maßnahme […] zum Aufrechterhalten der öffentlichen Sicherheit und Ordnung erforderlich war […]“ und der Hund „nur kurz eingesetzt“ worden sei.


Die Staatsanwaltschaft begründet die Entscheidung darüber hinaus damit, dass „Diensthunde […] legal bei der Polizei als Hilfsmittel auch in Stresssituationen eingesetzt […]“ werden. Die Tiere würden dabei automatisch Belastungssituationen ausgesetzt. Die Interessen und das Wohl der Hunde rückten jedoch im Verhältnis zu den polizeilichen Interessen der Gefahrenabwehr in den Hintergrund, da die „Diensthunde“ zu diesem Zwecke ausgebildet würden. Der den Hunden zugeschriebene „Nutzen“ rechtfertigt laut Ansicht der Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden, dass die Tiere bewusst in Gefahrensituationen gezwungen werden.


PETA kritisiert Entscheidung der Staatsanwaltschaft: Gesetz erlaubt Gewalt gegen Diensthunde


Die Einstellung unserer Anzeige ist ein weiteres Beispiel dafür, dass das Gesetz die „Diensthunde“ nicht vor einem gewaltsamen Umgang und Missbrauch schützt. Hunde sind keine Einsatzmittel, sondern fühlende Lebewesen, die einen respektvollen, liebevollen Umgang verdient haben – nicht die missbräuchliche Verwendung  als Waffe oder Schutzschild.


Wir vertreten die Ansicht, dass moderne Polizeiarbeit ohne Tiere auskommt und fordern daher Politik und Behörden auf, „Diensthunde“ zu verbieten.


Originaltext vom 13. Januar 2025


Gewalt gegen Polizeihunde bei einem Einsatz gegen Demonstranten in Riesa


Videos von der Demonstration zeigen deutlich wie gewaltvoll einige Diensthundeführer:innen mit den „Polizeihunden“ umgehen. Einer der

Hunde

 wurde von einem der Beamten am Hals gepackt und gegen eine Leitplanke und einen Demonstranten gedrückt. Dadurch sollte der Hund offensichtlich dazu gebracht werden, den Demonstranten zu beißen. Der Hund zeigte hierbei unübersehbare

Anzeichen

 von massivem Stress, Überforderung und Meideverhalten. Ein weiterer völlig überdrehter Hund verbiss sich in den Arm eines anderen Polizisten.


https://www.instagram.com/p/DExO_Z1Mcvv/?hl=de


PETA erstattet Strafanzeige und fordert den Einsatz von Polizeihunden zu beenden


Dieser gewaltsame Umgang der Einsatzkräfte mit den Hunden ist tierschutzwidrig. Hunde sind nicht dazu da, für die Arbeit der Polizei ausgenutzt zu werden. Wir fordern deshalb, den Einsatz von Hunden bei der Polizei endlich einzustellen. Zudem erstatten wir bei der Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden Zweigstelle Meißen Strafanzeige gegen den verantwortlichen Polizisten. Ferat Kocak, Abgeordneter der Linken war als parlamentarischer Beobachter vor Ort und hat sich bereit erklärt in der Strafanzeige als Zeuge aufzutreten.


„Die aktuellen Aufnahmen aus Riesa zeigen eindeutig, dass Hunde bei Polizeieinsätzen nichts zu suchen haben. Wir hoffen, dass es den betroffenen Hunden gut geht und sie keine körperlichen Schäden von dieser grausamen Behandlung davontragen. Die Psyche der Hunde leidet nach solch einem Einsatz ganz sicher. Hunde sind von Natur aus freundliche, soziale Lebewesen. Durch gewaltsame Trainingsmethoden werden sie bei der Polizei ‚scharf gemacht‘ und zu einer Art Waffe konditioniert – gegen ihren Willen. author: Stelinsky
title: «Με τσακισμένα χέρια, γόνατα, συνθήματα»…
content:
σκέψεις γύρω από τις κατασταλτικές μεθοδεύσεις με αφορμή την υπόθεση Θεσσαλονίκης

Το πρωινό της 1ης Ιουλίου 2026 ο εγχώριος ηλεκτρονικός τύπος κατακλύζεται από ειδήσεις σχετικά με 3 εμπρηστικές ενέργειες στη Θεσσαλονίκη, που είχαν ως στόχο σπίτια πολιτευτών της Νέας Δημοκρατίας. Συγκεκριμένα, γίνονται αναφορές για «εμπρηστικές επιθέσεις με γκαζάκια στα σπίτια του προέδρου της Διοικούσας Επιτροπής Ν.Δ. Θεσσαλονίκης Ζήση Ιωακείμοβιτς, του πρώην βουλευτή Σάββα Αναστασιάδη και της πολιτεύτριας Αφροδίτης Νέστορα». Στην τελευταία περίπτωση, στην πυλωτή της πολυκατοικίας «υπήρχε αφρώδες υλικό που ανεφλέγη μετά την πυροδότηση του μηχανισμού, με αποτέλεσμα η φωτιά να εξαπλωθεί σε οχήματα». Η Βάγια Νέστορα, μητέρα της πολιτεύτριας, η οποία «είχε κατέβει από τον 5ο όροφο στο ισόγειο της πολυκατοικίας, λόγω των καπνών και της έκθεσής της σε υψηλό θερμικό φορτίο έπαθε σοβαρά εγκαύματα». Μεταφέρθηκε στη ΜΕΘ του Ιπποκράτειου Θεσσαλονίκης, όπου εξέπνευσε το απόγευμα της ίδιας ημέρας.1

Το μιντιακό κλίμα που διαμορφώθηκε γύρω από τις εμπρηστικές επιθέσεις στη Θεσσαλονίκη ενορχηστρώθηκε εξ ολοκλήρου από το κυβερνητικό επιτελείο της Ν.Δ., και ξετυλίχθηκε σε πολλά επίπεδα: Πρωτίστως, ποινικά, χαρακτηρίζοντας τις ενέργειες «τρομοκρατικές», και αναθέτοντας την εξιχνίασή τους στην αντιτρομοκρατική υπηρεσία. Ταυτόχρονα, στελέχη της Ν.Δ. αξιοποίησαν τον θάνατο της Βάγιας Νέστορα για να εξαπολύσουν μια επίθεση στα κόμματα της αντιπολίτευσης, με προεξάρχον το κόμμα ΕΛ.Α.Σ. του Τσίπρα να απορροφά τα –εμφυλιοπολεμικής κοπής– πυρά. Τις επόμενες ημέρες, στο μιντιακό πανηγύρι επικράτησε η ποινική διάσταση της υπόθεσης, η οποία επενδύθηκε από μια πρωτοφανή επιχείρηση λασπολόγησης, ηθικής απονομιμοποίησης και εγκληματοποίησης του αναρχικού χώρου, που «φωτογραφήθηκε» από το σύνολο των ΜΜΕ και των κομματικών δυνάμεων ως πολιτικά υπεύθυνος.

Την ίδια στιγμή που τα κυβερνητικά φερέφωνα παρήγαγαν ασταμάτητα λεπτομερές υλικό σε άρθρα και ρεπορτάζ, ο αναρχικός χώρος βρέθηκε σε μούδιασμα: Μέχρι και σήμερα, μήνες μετά, ελάχιστος λόγος έχει βγει γύρω από τα γεγονότα, και κυρίως γύρω από τη διαχείρισή τους, στην οποία θα εστιάσει αυτό το κείμενο. Για τον κόσμο της Θεσσαλονίκης, η συνθήκη αυτή είναι απολύτως φυσιολογική, αφού καλείται να διαχειριστεί μια σύνθετη κατάσταση, της οποίας τα φορτία και το βάθος απαιτούν ένα πολύμηνο διάστημα συλλογικής επεξεργασίας.

Σε περιπτώσεις που η κοινωνική πραγματικότητα διαμορφώνεται από κοινωνικές ομάδες και υποκείμενα έξω από τον αναρχικό χώρο, ο τελευταίος επιδεικνύει τα αντανακλαστικά του να «διαβάζει», να τοποθετείται, να ασκεί κριτική, ακόμα και να υπερασπίζεται ενέργειες και καταστάσεις, αλλά και όσα βρίσκονται στο στόχαστρο του κράτους. Στην υπόθεση της Θεσσαλονίκης, ο αναρχικός χώρος δεν επέδειξε αντίστοιχα αντανακλαστικά. Η «κριτική» αυτή απευθύνεται στον χώρο εκτός της Θεσσαλονίκης – σε όλα τα συντρόφια και τα συλλογικά σχήματα που έγιναν μέρος του μουδιάσματος, σε μια φάση που ο λόγος τους, και η συμβολή τους ήταν –και παραμένουν– «κρίσιμα»: Ανοίγοντας έναν διάλογο, που αναπόφευκτα θα διεμβόλιζε τον μονόλογο της κυριαρχίας, ανακόπτοντας το υπό διαμόρφωση μιντιακό κλίμα – διάλογος που, με συντροφικούς όρους, θα ανακούφιζε και κάποια από τα βάρη των συντροφιών της Θεσσαλονίκης, συνθέτοντας ταυτόχρονα μια πρώτη γραμμή πολιτικής υπεράσπισης για τις συλλήψεις που ακολούθησαν.

Ένας πολιτικός χώρος που φιλοδοξεί να απευθύνεται και να συνδιαλέγεται με την κοινωνία οφείλει να στέκεται με ειλικρίνεια και ευθύτητα απέναντι στα πράγματα: Εν προκειμένω, να ανοίξει μια συζήτηση, να τοποθετηθεί πάνω σε διαστάσεις των γεγονότων, ή επί της διαχείρισής τους. Η κοινωνία μεταφράζει τη σιωπή ως δήλωση ενοχής. Και ο εχθρός μας την αξιοποιεί ως «παραχωρημένο» έδαφος για να μονοπωλήσει τον δημόσιο λόγο.

Στις 10 Ιουλίου, μία ημέρα μετά την κηδεία της Βάγιας Νέστορα, συλλαμβάνεται ένας σύντροφος, μίας συντρόφισσα, και ακόμα ένα άτομο. Έξι μέρες μετά, η αντιτρομοκρατική συλλαμβάνει κάτω από το σπίτι του έναν ακόμη σύντροφο, και προσάγει μια συντρόφισσα η οποία και αφήνεται ελεύθερη μερικές ώρες αργότερα. Το τηλεοπτικό δικαστήριο που ξεκίνησε με την αναγγελία του θανάτου της Βάγιας Νέστορα, ευθυγραμμίστηκε με την αφήγηση της αντιτρομοκρατικής, εντείνοντας την επιχείρηση εγκληματοποίησης του αναρχικού χώρου. Και ενώ μέχρι σήμερα τα συντρόφια μας παραμένουν κατηγορούμενα, για τα ΜΜΕ αρκούσαν οι υποδείξεις του υπουργείου ΠΡΟ.ΠΟ. –μέσω της αντιτρομοκρατικής– για να παρουσιάσουν την «αδιάσειστη ενοχή» τους. Έφτασαν, μάλιστα, στο σημείο να …

author: Amy Goodman
title: Climate Finance Pledges at COP31 Amount to Mere “Pennies,” Policy Expert Says
content:
“The fossil fuel lobbyists are rampant in the halls,” says Rachel Cleetus of the Union of Concerned Scientists.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

As Democracy Now! continues broadcasting from the U.N. climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, we speak with Rachel Cleetus, climate program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists, about climate finance — the notion that efforts to mitigate the climate crisis must be funded. “Climate finance is not an abstract thing. It’s what countries need to be able to transition away from fossil fuels,” says Cleetus. “And right now we have pennies in these funds.” She notes that at a pledging event for the Adaptation Fund, which supports climate finance for developing countries, a mere $50 million was pledged. “It’s shameful, absolutely unjust, what’s happening here. And richer countries are continuing to block progress.” This comes as scientists say the world is set to overshoot the target, set by the 2015 Paris Agreement, of limiting global heating to 1.5 degrees Celsius.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org. I’m Amy Goodman.

As the climate negotiations here in Antalya, Turkey, enter their last days, we’re joined now by Rachel Cleetus, climate program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists.

Can you talk about what’s happened and what hasn’t happened, and particularly talk about — again, it’s a buzzword — but the 1.5 degrees Celsius overshoot, what exactly that means, and why you are so concerned, representing the Union of Concerned Scientists?

RACHEL CLEETUS: Amy, so, we came into this COP with some really sobering science that had been shared, which is that the world now inevitably is going to breach 1.5 C of global warming, that treasured guardrail that we had secured in the Paris Agreement. And it —

AMY GOODMAN: And 1.5 degrees Celsius is 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit.

AMY GOODMAN: And it’s hard for people to imagine. We’re talking about a degree. Why could that matter so much to the world?

RACHEL CLEETUS: Well, the crucial thing is to understand that this is a global average. And actually, in many places in the world, including in parts of the United States, it’s heating up much faster than that. And that small fraction, that’s causing massive ice sheets and glaciers to melt, like we saw the horrific tragedy in Nepal. It’s causing oceans to boil. We’re seeing these intensified hurricanes, extreme flooding, droughts, catastrophic wildfires, like we saw in the United States and around the world, and these extreme, deadly heat waves that have taken tens of thousands of lives just this year. That’s what that 1.5 C breaching means.

And we came into this COP with scientists saying, “This is where we are, but we still have a narrow window. We need to act. The choices we make now are crucial.” And we didn’t get here by accident. We got here because of burning fossil fuels. We got here because policymakers, including world leaders in halls like this, have just not acted with urgency. And the fossil fuel industry has been just blocking progress, spreading disinformation about science.

AMY GOODMAN: Why do they even get to be here?

RACHEL CLEETUS: That’s the extraordinary thing.

AMY GOODMAN: It’s like a conference on tobacco and cancer, and the cigarette industry is as much as half of the people represented.

RACHEL CLEETUS: It’s extraordinary. The fossil fuel lobbyists are rampant in the halls here, and their sole task here is just to block progress. And it’s not just them; it’s also petrostates like Saudi Arabia that’s in rooms right now blocking the best available IPCC science from being available for the next global stocktake of the Paris Agreement. So, fossil fuels, they’re the core cause of climate change, and they’re also — the fossil fuel lobbyists are the core obstructors of progress.

AMY GOODMAN: The biggest issue we’re hearing again and again is climate finance, meaning how do the countries least responsible for climate change deal, whether we’re talking about long-term adaptation or the crises countries face, like Nepal.

RACHEL CLEETUS: Yeah, what we’re seeing is such a collision of both the climate crisis, the inflation that’s been set off by this illegal war against Iran, the debt crisis that countries are spiraling and suffering from. And it’s rich major polluters that …
