author: Clare Carlile and Hazel Healy
title: Fertiliser, Big Meat and Biofuels Industry Among 260 Food Sector Lobbyists at COP31
content:
Polluting food and agriculture companies are present in large numbers at this year’s UN COP31 climate talks, with a total of 260 lobbyists on the ground in Turkey’s southern city of Antalya, new analysis shows.


The meat and dairy sector, which

produces

 over 14 percent of global emissions, brought 71 delegates, the highest number of all food and agriculture sectors. Its representatives outnumber delegates from Honduras, where millions of people currently

face

 severe drought. 


Fertiliser lobbyists showed the biggest jump in delegates year on year, with a 45 percent increase. The CEOs of several powerful trade groups representing the meat, fertiliser, pesticides and biofuels sectors are also present in Antalya. 


Some of the world’s largest agribusiness firms, including meat company

JBS

 and dairy multinationals

Nestlé

 and Danone, as well as pesticides firm

Bayer

 and food giant Unilever, also travelled to Turkey for the talks, which run from 9-20 November.


The analysis shows the power and influence enjoyed by the sector, with more than a hundred lobbyists participating as part of their country governments, lending them privileged access to negotiations. More than 44 percent of food and agriculture delegates travelled on country badges, up from 5 percent at COP27 five years ago.


For fertiliser firms, the share of delegates on party badges rises to 90 percent. Russia’s party included 12 delegates from two fertiliser companies linked to sanctioned individuals, DeSmog found. 


A version of this article was published by franceinfo.


DeSmog’s revelations come as disappointment sets in for advocates hoping for action to reform food systems, which account for a third of global emissions. Agriculture

negotiations

 have

broken down

 after four years of discussion, with some observers pointing to the contributing “role of vested interests” in their collapse.

 

At the time of going to press, all references to food and farming are

missing

 from the draft cover text, which informs the basis of a final deal at the talks. And a high-level

initiative

 to spur government action on methane is languishing on seven signatories.  


Both meat and fertiliser groups are keen to make their voices heard at a summit where the Turkish presidency has made curbing the short-lived “superpollutant gases” emitted by agricultural sectors – such as nitrous oxide and methane – a

top priority

.

DeSmog has witnessed meat industry groups lobbying to

weaken

 the accounting metrics for methane at side events while observers describe the high fertiliser sector turnout as “a big PR campaign” to be recognised as vital to food security.


The UN’s leading science body, the IPCC, says the world must make urgent and deep cuts to greenhouse gas emissions to avoid catastrophic climate change. Global heating is already set to

breach

 1.5C, with each additional degree of warming increasing deadly impacts from droughts, floods, and cyclones. 


“This is a direct affront to billions of people who are suffering from the climate emergency,” said Million Belay, co-founder and general coordinator of the Alliance for Food Sovereignty in Africa (AFSA). “They have created the crisis that we all live in. And they are here to influence the whole process through lobbying, thwarting a real discussion and action against emissions, and flooding pavilions with empty talk.”


Farmers are facing unprecedented

losses

 from droughts, floods, and tropical cyclones – 49 million more people

could face

 acute hunger in 2026-27 due to the El Niño weather system that has been turbo-charged by climate breakdown.

“We need to talk about the impact that lobbying is having on our democracy,” Nusa Urbancic from advocacy group

Changing Markets Foundation

 told DeSmog. “The number of agribusiness lobbyists is shocking and shows why agriculture has not yet made it into any official documents.” 


A spokesperson from Bayer said: “Global challenges need places where the world still comes together”. They added: “Combating climate change requires governments, civil society, local communities and the private sector to work together on effective solutions. This is particularly important for agriculture, which is severely affected by climate change”.

Nestlé told DeSmog: “COP31 is a major global gathering and an important opportunity to engage with governments, civil society, farmers and other stakeholders to accelerate climate action. Our engagement is focused …

author: Unknown
title: Peoples’ Climate Summit addresses energy trade and war in Gaza
content:
At the Peoples’ Climate Summit in Antalya, international environmental and solidarity organizations focused their discussions on the economic links between the fossil fuel industry and military violence. On the third day of the gathering, organized as an alternative to the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), discussions centered on the destruction of livelihoods in Gaza, the role of international energy supplies and demands for a comprehensive embargo against Israel. Participants examined the extent to which climate justice also required overcoming war, occupation and military expansion.


Representatives of Energy Embargo for Palestine, the Global Sumud Flotilla, the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) movement and various international solidarity networks were among those taking part in the event.


Destruction in Gaza as an ecological crisis


Asad Rehman of Friends of the Earth highlighted the long-term environmental consequences of the war in Gaza. He stated that the destruction of water supply and sewage systems, damage to essential infrastructure and soil contamination caused by munitions, debris and untreated wastewater had devastated livelihoods that could take decades to restore.


Rehman argued that this destruction should also be examined from the perspective of ecocide. He also raised the question of political and economic control over natural resources: “Who extracts which resources, from whom, for whose benefit and under whose authority? That is the fundamental question.”


Ana Sanchez drew a connection between Israeli military policy, international arms trade relationships and the rise of far-right movements. In her assessment, Israel benefited from diplomatic support while supplying military and security technologies to right-wing governments. She argued that an effective arms embargo must go beyond halting individual arms deals and encompass entire supply chains, including the disruption of fuel shipments.


“Solidarity means disrupting supply chains. That means a two-way embargo: neither buying nor selling. It means stopping fuel deliveries,” Sanchez explained.


She emphasized that the liberation of Palestine was not an issue separate from the climate movement. Rather, she said, the fossil fuel-based economic system, patriarchal power structures and military violence were closely interconnected. “There can be no climate justice without freedom for Palestine,” she stressed.


Criticism of oil shipments through Turkey


Celine Isimbi of Energy Embargo for Palestine addressed specific economic ties, highlighting the importance of international oil trade to Israel’s energy supply, particularly shipments from Azerbaijan. According to Isimbi, Israel obtains more than 40 percent of its crude oil requirements from Azerbaijan. The oil is transported through the Baku–Tbilisi–Ceyhan pipeline to Turkey’s Mediterranean coast, from where it is shipped to Israel by tanker.


Isimbi stated that her organization had documented a total of 77 oil shipments along this route to Israeli ports between May 2024 and June 2026. She alleged that vessels had temporarily switched off their automatic tracking signals to conceal their actual destination ports.


Isimbi also said that Turkey’s Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure had confirmed that ships had provided false information to port authorities and that legal proceedings had been initiated in connection with these incidents.


The activist called for fossil fuel supplies to no longer be considered separately from their military and political uses. She argued that an energy embargo must also cover transportation routes and the companies involved.


Calls for reparations rather than development aid


Abeer Al Butmeh of the Palestinian environmental network PENGON called for reparations and the restoration of destroyed livelihoods. She argued that international development aid alone could not adequately address the political and material consequences of the destruction. She pointed out that the Palestinian population must be able to make its own decisions regarding energy supplies, water resources, land and reconstruction. “Palestinians must determine their own future and have the right to remain on their land, return to it and rebuild it,” Al Butmeh stated.

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Mindanao folk add their voices vs Pax Silica
content:
Fauzhea Guiani, Anakbayan Southern Mindanao spokesperson, speaks during a protest in Davao City on November 17, 2026. Photo courtesy of Anakbayan Southern Mindanao

People in Mindanao added their voices in opposing the United States (US)-led Pax Silica, an initiative that aims to establish an industrial hub that could displace Indigenous and peasant communities.

Like in many areas, mobilizations led by various organizations in the island became massive when Filipinos were waiting for the arrival of US President Donald Trump for the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit.

In Mindanao State University – Iligan Institute of Technology (MSU-IIT), an estimated 3,000 students have reportedly joined the walkout protest on November 17 to observe the National Students’ Day, highlighting their calls to reject the Pax Silica initiative and its proposed Clark Advanced Manufacturing Park project to be constructed in New Clark City, Tarlac.

The said 1,600-hectare industrial hub is being promoted as an economic security zone (ESZ) that would strengthen shared supply chains in semiconductors and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies.

Young Davaoeños, led by Kabataan Party-list (KPL) Southern Mindanao, conducted an Oplan Sabit ahead of Trump’s visit, hanging banners in three overpasses in Davao City highlighting calls to oppose Pax Silica.

Kabataan Party-list Southern Mindanao members hang posters in overpasses in Davao City on November 16, 2026, ahead of the National Students’ Day. Photos courtesy of Kabataan Party-list Southern Mindanao

Cobbie Jan Canda, KPL Southern Mindanao chaiperson, said the US-led initiative may only lead to the exploitation of the country’s natural resources.

The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) earlier reported that 500,000 hectares of public forest lands in Mindanao are up for investment, of which 28.8 percent of these lands belonged to the Davao Region.

Read: 500,000 hectares of Mindanao forest lands up for privatization

The group also reiterated its opposition to the plan of establishing a military oil depot within the Davao Gulf, a proposed facility that can store up to 41 million gallons of US-owned fuel products and shall reportedly serve as an alternative point for US naval vessels away from the West Philippine Sea to avoid potential conflict with China.

“We will not allow that the country would be caught between the US-China conflict,” Canda said.

Youth-led anti-Pax Silica demonstrations were also launched in big state universities, namely MSU Main Campus in Marawi City and Central Mindanao University (CMU) in Maramag, Bukidnon, as well as in the island province of Tawi-Tawi, led by the Padantah Tawi-Tawi Youth Organization and Youth Advocates for Climate Action Philippines.

The religious sector also took part. Parishes and missions under the Iglesia Filipina Independiente – Diocese of Ozamiz in Misamis Occidental also expressed their strong denunciation against the Pax Silica initiative, which reportedly remains under negotiations to this date.

Read: Int’l groups show solidarity to Filipinos vs Pax Silica

Mindanao Development Authority (MinDA) Assistant Secretary Romeo Montenegro reportedly said that they were exploring options for Mindanao to supply the Pax Silica hub with production inputs, including raw minerals, if it becomes operational.

Montenegro’s statement reinforced an Indigenous youth group’s call to reject Pax Silica. (RVO)

author: Petala Ironcloud
title: Native American Candidates Won on Platforms Around Land, Water, and Data Centers
content:
National wins among Native politicians could augur change at the state level.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

The 2026 midterms didn’t only swell the ranks of progressives and green economic populists in Congress — they also ushered in a stunning number of Native American leaders in down-ballot races across the country. Among the state legislative races involving Indigenous candidates that have been called so far, Native American candidates won 83 percent of the time, according to ICT.

Montana led the way: 12 of 13 Indigenous candidates there, all Democrats, won legislative seats, including Natalie Weeks-O’Neal (Fort Peck Assiniboine and Sioux) in House District 31 and Katie Fire Thunder (Oglala Lakota) in House District 59.

In Nevada, Brian Wadsworth, a former Pyramid Lake Paiute Tribal Council member, won a seat on the Washoe County Commission representing the county’s rural north, becoming the first tribal member from any of the county’s tribal nations to serve on it, Wadsworth told Truthout. Native Republicans won too, including Emily McIntire (Muscogee) in Oregon and Heather Ellison (Navajo) in New Mexico.

In Alaska, Mary Peltola defeated the incumbent to became the first Native person to represent the state in the U.S. Senate.

Many of these candidates spoke to voters’ concerns on the campaign trail about the affordability of groceries and health care. In Northern Nevada, voters also raised concerns about water, land, and unchecked growth. And the offices these candidates won are increasingly in locales where fights over land, water, and AI data centers get decided, as the federal government weakens its obligation to consult tribes. “We have about 120 proposed hyperscale data centers for Indian Country,” said Krystal Two Bulls, executive director of environmental advocacy group Honor the Earth.

Locally, “these fights are currently being fought and won,” Two Bulls told Truthout. A U.S. Senate permitting bill, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, despite its name, focuses on narrowing environmental review processes and threatens tribal consultation on projects affecting tribal water, land, and cultural sites. “That’s pretty much going to gut any kind of protections or legs that tribes can stand on to push back against these corporations,” said Two Bulls. The bill passed a preliminary vote on November 9 but has yet to clear the next hurdle in the Senate.

National wins among Native politicians could augur change at the state level, especially in states with multiple Indigenous candidate victories. Montana’s wins were historic: “It’s not lost on us that we’re making history, being the largest American Indian caucus in the United States at the state level,” said Weeks-O’Neal, adding that the state’s main media has yet to cover this fact.

Two Bulls expressed hope that the Indigenous bloc will be able to exert real leverage, saying: “They can actually throw a lot of wrenches into the fast tracking that’s currently happening.”

Despite Two Bulls’ forward-looking ambitions for the new class of Native politicians, especially around AI, Weeks-O’Neal faces extant costs to her district: The Zortman mines, which extracted gold from the Little Rocky Mountains in the 1980s and ’90s, contaminated Montana’s water and still cost $3 million a year to treat. “The water is devastated. It is tainted in perpetuity. That means forever,” she said. “Whatever profit was made from the mine, I mean, I can’t imagine.” The site has been re-listed for $52.5 million with geologists estimating “that only 20% of the gold and silver [was] harvested, leaving plenty of reserves for investors or operators,” the listing states.

House District 31 includes much of the Fort Peck Reservation, whose median age is 30 and median household income is roughly $53,000, far below the national median of around $87,000. It’s no surprise then that voters’ primary concern is affordability, especially groceries. “They were struggling to even feed their families,” said Weeks-O’Neal. Trump’s administration has moved to slash the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, which could cut off access for 6.3 million people nationally.

Meanwhile Katie Fire Thunder’s constituents in South Bozeman, which is one of the wealthiest areas in the state, are also worried about affordability: Rising property taxes, driven by soaring land …

author: dialogocomospovos
title: Recuperação Espiritual
content:
Em sua formação no Assentamento Terra Vista, Moira Millán aprofundou a luta do povo Mapuche para além da terra: “A luta do Povo Mapuche é uma luta por um modo de vida na terra. Não é uma luta pela terra, mas por um modo de vida na terra.” Para ela, não basta tomar a terra; é preciso perguntar: “O que vamos fazer nessa terra?” A resposta mapuche passa por compreender o espaço na terra como espaço de descolonização. Por isso, a educação própria não pode ser igual à educação do Estado, que impõe formas de organização que não são originárias e silencia o pensamento e o mapudungun.


Moira explicou que, para os Mapuche, a recuperação territorial precisa ser, primeiro, uma recuperação espiritual. É um território onde o povo se repara, volta e recomponha um vínculo sagrado com a terra por meio das cerimônias e da filosofia própria. Nesse sentido, ela tocou num tema sensível também no Brasil: a religião colonial. Segundo Moira, quando as religiões cristãs chegam às comunidades indígenas, muitas vezes se esquecem das cerimônias e dos cantos, o povo vai tomando distância da identidade e da terra.


Na comunidade onde vive, há consenso de não permitir a entrada de igrejas cristãs: “só há espiritualidade Mapuche”. Também não há postos sanitários do Estado; a única forma de cura é com as autoridades da medicina Mapuche. A fala de Moira reforça que a luta mapuche é territorial, espiritual e política, e dialoga com as resistências indígenas e camponesas presentes no Terra Vista.

author: Alan Robinson
title: The Right to Irrationally Refuse Treatment: An Interview with Ron Thompson
content:
Editor’s Note: This Mad in the World report features an interview with activist and attorney Ron Thompson, interviewed by Locura en Argentina founder Alan Robinson.

From serving on the boards of the American Civil Liberties Union and the Bazelon Center, and participating in advocacy initiatives supported by the National Institute of Mental Health, to collaborating with pioneering figures like Judi Chamberlin, Loren Mosher, and Thomas Szasz, Ron Thompson has been an incisive observer of the psychiatric survivor movement since 1986. Here, he speaks from a very lucid and provocative perspective about the systemic flaws of biological psychiatry, the limits of legal reform, and why guaranteeing the right to refuse treatment on irrational grounds remains the final frontier for patient autonomy.

Ron Thompson: Thank you for the introduction, Alan. I am glad to be here.

Thompson: My introduction in 1986 was truly a revelation. By chance, I came across an article in the Washington Post that mentioned someone I recognized from my prep school days at Phillips Exeter Academy. The article concerned St. Elizabeths Hospital in Washington, D.C.—a psychiatric facility and prison. We had been on the same wrestling team together years prior.

I decided to track him down. When I visited him at St. Elizabeths, I was astounded by his condition and the stark contrast between his life and mine. Physically, it was obvious that his incarceration and treatment had severely damaged him. He was overweight, and his skin tone was unnatural. While he held unconventional ideas—he was the son of a prominent financial figure and imagined arranging grand financial deals between China and the United States—his thoughts made a distinct kind of sense when understood within his personal history.

We formed an immediate connection. Because he could not leave on his own, I was granted permission to take him off hospital grounds for meals at a nearby Chinese restaurant. Spending time with him made me realize how extraordinarily fortunate I had been 20 years earlier during my own encounter with the psychiatric system. When I was hospitalized decades prior. I was hospitalized as a voluntary patient, a status retained throughout my connection to the McLean Hospital near Boston, Mass in the town of Belmont.

Thompson: Many years have passed, but the treatment must have lasted approximately two and a half years. I entered the hospital in November, 1964 after a few weeks into my first semester at Georgetown University Law Center in Washington DC, when I woke up one morning and, according to memory, couldn’t see myself in the mirror. I called my parents and abruptly returned to their home in Dover, New Hampshire.

After what may have been only a few weeks, I told the doctors I was feeling sicker. Most remarkable of all their decisions, they decided that this was because of the drugs I was on, either Haldol or Thorazine, or both of them. And 3 or 4 months later, I told the doctors that I had to leave in-patient status or “something bad would happen,” whatever I meant by that. Again, the doctors made a remarkable decision, and said “ok,” despite that somewhat ominous phrase.

To summarize my treatment, it might be enough to say that my sickness was primarily due to a mother, who was not abusive in any ordinary way, but whose lifelong anxiety, combined with erratic and sudden emotional changes, and perhaps also with the example or ‘lesson’ of a father who lived with this difficult woman by more or less pretending no problem existed, led me to conclude that radical suppression of emotion was the way to deal with any and all kinds of emotional discomfort.

Thompson: It has now been 40 years since I began this work in 1986. My connection with NIMH began shortly after I got involved in advocacy. At the time, Joe Rogers—a prominent and dynamic figure in the movement—had visited me after I wrote a somewhat satirical piece about his style. Despite the critique, he engaged with me respectfully, and through those networks, I was introduced to a small, progressive unit within NIMH.

This unit was experimentation-oriented. They were boldly attempting to fund patient advocates and former patients to participate in national dialogues. NIMH began sponsoring my travel to conferences across the United States and even internationally, including a conference in Finland.

This support allowed me to engage with almost every major figure in the movement. I established a close dialogue …

author: Freedom Editor
title: Bullshit Burnham’s war on the disabled
content:
Andy Burnham promised an end to forty years of neoliberalism. Instead, he’s embraced the persecution of its favourite scapegoats

The news that the Milburn Review is to recommend the end of Personal Independence Payment (PIP), and the health element of Universal Credit for most young people under the age of 25, is not a surprise to those of us in the disability rights community, but it is horrific all the same.

According to Labour, it’s for their own good; no-one, intones Andy solemnly, wants to be trapped in a cycle of dependency, do they? Of course, this is all bullshit. Intentions matter, and neither the Milburn Review into the number of young people not in education, employment or training (NEET) or the Timms Review into PIP itself, were commissioned for the benefit of the young or the disabled, but for the benefit of the government’s bank balance.

Put simply—and no-one is questioning this—the number of claimants has increased significantly since the pandemic. One million young people are not in work or education. And the government doesn’t want to spend money on the problem.

But the clue is in the chronology. Though COVID has been memory-holed by many, not least government, which has worked assiduously to prevent Long COVID being recognised as a disability, the UK as elsewhere went through a once-in-a-century pandemic a handful of years ago. Apart from the death toll, which the COVID Inquiry acknowledges was worsened by government policy, many were left disabled and chronically ill.

That’s not the whole story, but it’s a big part of it, and as with COVID more generally it’s one government simply pretends doesn’t exist. The Burnham/Milburn rhetoric on disability is one of sympathy, that this is a ‘moral’ choice by government, that these ‘changes’ are an opportunity for a generational reset for young people who have, by Burnham’s own admission, been failed by politicians.

On that last we can agree, but Burnham’s no break with that catalogue of failure. Like his predecessors Starmer and Reeves, Burnham’s characterised PIP as an out-of-work benefit, when it is isn’t – it’s paid to ensure folks can be independent (the clue is in the name) and meet the additional costs which are incurred by being disabled in an ableist society. This is a wilful play into right-wing ‘scrounger’ rhetoric.

Burnham’s not wrong to mention that austerity had an enormous impact on the young in the coalition years, but lest we forget this is a man who lost a previous chance at the Labour leadership primarily because he refused to vote against coalition welfare cuts in 2015, a decision which fuelled a grassroots revolt in the Labour Party and the ultimate election of Jeremy Corbyn.

Indeed, what’s proposed here is a massive real-terms saving to government dressed up as empowerment for its victims—which is the classic Labour play. But anyone with any critical faculty can read Burnham’s words and know they are bullshit.

His constant references to parity of esteem in the education sector could have been written by any government, Labour or Tory, for the last sixty years. As with everything with him, it is surface-level, hoping to play on common-sensical shibboleths that will encourage folks to look past (or not at all at) the actual policy.

The same weekend his op-ed was published, a TikTok found its way online from the Labour account with Andy saying “we used to have a laugh…talk about pub snacks” before the Union Jack came prominently into play. The more things change, the more they stay the same, as the Burnham revolution boils down to idiotic chat about pork scratchings and pints whilst the young have what precious little support they get taken from them.

Labour’s messaging this week is to say that what they propose is more humane than what the Tories want to do, that they are offering a jobs guarantee and hope. But like all Burnham’s promises it’s a mirage. Milburn has proposed a reduction in employer national insurance for young people, but not yet; young people will still be paid less for the same work too.

Young people still won’t be able to access the mental health care they need. They will supposedly be able to apply to ‘local funds’ for support, funds which don’t exist and if they ever did based on prior experience would be unlikely to be responsive. But this rhetoric is just to salve the consciences of those not directly affected.

Disabled people, and disabled young people in particular, are neoliberal capitalism’s …

author: Unknown
title: AKP ilçe başkanıyla görüşmeyen ilçe sağlık müdürüne "istifa" baskısı iddiası
content:
Rize – Pazar İlçe Sağlık Müdürlüğü görevinden alınan İ.Ö'nün, AKP Pazar İlçe Başkanı Furkan Namlı’nın ziyaret talebini kabul etmediği gerekçesiyle geçen günlerde istifaya zorlandığı iddia edildi. Yeni Parti Rize İl Başkanı Saltuk Deniz, İ.Ö'nün görevine iadesini isteyerek, AKP yetkililerine “Kurum amirleri sizin hizmetkârınız değildir” dedi.

Edinilen bilgilere göre, 4 Ağustos 2026 tarihinde AKP Pazar İlçe Başkanı olan Furkan Namlı ve beraberindeki yönetim kurulu üyeleri, kurum ziyaretleri kapsamında Pazar İlçe Sağlık Müdürlüğü’nden telefonla randevu talep etti. İlçe Sağlık Müdürü Dr. İ.Ö’nün ilk talebin ardından müsait olmadığını belirttiği, ikinci telefon görüşmesinde ise 657 sayılı Devlet Memurları Kanunu’na tabi bir kamu görevlisi olduğunu ifade ederek siyasi parti ilçe başkanlarıyla makamında görüşmeyeceğini bildirdiği ileri sürüldü.

Rize'deki AKP yetkililerince bunun İl Sağlık Müdürü Prof. Dr. Gökhan Demiral’a ileterek Dr. İ.Ö’nün görevden alınmasını ya da istifa etmesinin istendiği, bunun ardından Dr. İ.Ö’ye istifa etmesi yönünde telkinde bulunulduğu ancak ilçe sağlık müdürünün bunu kabul etmediği savunuldu.

Dr. İ.Ö. bir süre sonra ise İlçe Sağlık Müdürlüğü'nden alındı.

Pazar İlçe Sağlık Müdürlüğü çalışanları da Dr. İ.Ö’ye istifa etmesi yönünde baskı yapıldığını ifade etti.

Yeni Parti Rize İl Başkanı Saltuk Deniz, Dr. İ.Ö’nün Pazar İlçe Sağlık Müdürlüğü'nden alınmasına tepki gösterdi. Kamu kurumlarında görev yapan yöneticilerin siyasi parti temsilcilerinin hizmetinde olmadığını vurgulayan Deniz, şu açıklamayı yaptı:

“Devlet kurumlarında çalışan görevlilerimiz siyasi parti temsilcilerinin hizmetkârı değillerdir. Kurum amirleri, hiçbir siyasi parti temsilcisi ile görevleri dışında görüşmek zorunda değildir. Daha önce de benzeri olaylar ilimizde yaşanmıştı. Rize İl Milli Eğitim Müdürü Halil İbrahim Akmeşe de İl Milli Eğitim Müdürlüğü görevine atanır atanmaz, daha koltuğuna oturmadan soluğu AKP İl Başkanlığı’nda aldı. Bunlar doğru şeyler değildir. Kurum amirleri sizlerin hizmetkârı değildir. Rahat bırakın çalışanları. Kurumlarda iş barışını bozmanın, amirleri ve memurları siyasal gücünüzü kullanarak görevlerinden almak ya da uzaklaştırmakla diğer kurum çalışanlarına gözdağı vermenin siyasi ahlakla da bağdaşmadığını düşünüyoruz. AKP sözcülerini ve İl Sağlık Müdürlüğü’nü bu konuyla ilgili açıklama yapmalarını, görevinden alınan doktorumuzun yeniden görevine iade edilmesini kamuoyu adına talep ediyoruz.”

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Petala Ironcloud
title: Native Youth Programs Are Building a Different Model of Mental Health Care
content:
These models are employing youth and grounding well-being in culture, relationships, and community.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Growing up in Eureka, a small city in Northern California, provided Roger “Chapreges” Jones an anchor in his Yurok culture. He took public K-12 Yurok language classes and Indian Ed covered school supplies. But when his parents divorced and he moved to Redding at 13, those resources vanished — and so did his appetite.

Chapreges got his first job at a Native American mental health clinic while grappling with an eating disorder hidden in plain sight. His new role at Two Feathers Native American Family Services became a kind of Trojan horse: He walked through the door looking for employment and found therapy waiting inside.

Founded in 1998 by a tribal consortium to strengthen Native family units in Humboldt County, Two Feathers has grown significantly since 2018, when its current executive director, Virgil Moorehead, joined. It went from having four staff members to having 32, including mental health clinicians, substance abuse counselors, and cultural coordinators.

Two Feathers serves a disproportionately large Native population across Northern California, where many Tribes and their citizens are either unrecognized federally or have been disenrolled. Critically, it serves Native families regardless of enrollment status — a stance that resists the disenrollment politics that plague underfunded tribes across Indian Country.

Chapreges is one of dozens of Native youth accessing Two Feathers services in a region where waitlists are long and federal funding cuts have gutted alternatives. A 2022 study from the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health echoes mounting research on the importance of cultural connection to Native youth’s mental health.

Chapreges’s experience speaks to that truth. He had struggled to acclimate to Redding without other Native youth or regular cultural resources beyond the annual Stillwater Powwow. In his sophomore year, he and his father, overwhelmed by the isolation, returned to Eureka, where Chapreges completed high school.

The following year, he became a youth ambassador at Two Feathers, promoting their culturally tailored programming: stick games, flower dance, trips to the local powwow, and the Young Bucks and Spotted Does programs for youth ages 8 to 12.

Moorehead is also a licensed clinical psychologist and has helmed a new era for the organization, implementing circular Native philosophy by creating a continuum of school- and family-oriented treatment services for Native youth and their families. Two Feathers’ approach reflects a broader Indigenous understanding of mental health that recognizes the effects of historical trauma while at the same time accounting for the distinct experiences of different Native communities.

One such program, the Acorn Youth Wellness Program, works with youth individually to bolster their cultural identity. “But I think giving them hope, you know, sense of belonging,” said Moorehead, “Those are all things that are measured.”

Moorehead said the program tracks attendance, cultural identity, and hope for the future. “I always say that if you don’t have kids that come to the program, you don’t have a program. And so through the way we did Acorn, it engaged kids and had them show up in the sense of coming back and back and back.”

In 2020, the California State Assembly’s Select Committee on Native American Affairs conferred the honor of a plaque, letter, and on-site visit recognizing the organization’s work to improve and stabilize the lives of Native youth and families in Northern California. The program’s success has attracted interest from other Native Nations seeking to replicate the model. Moorehead said he’s in early conversations with one tribe planning to launch their own version next year, though he declined to name specific nations in preliminary stages.

Another member of the Two Feathers staff, Jayla, who asked to be identified by first name only to protect her privacy, joined the organization at age 15 after seeing an employment ad. A year into her time at Two Feathers, in 2025, President Donald Trump proposed consolidating behavioral health funding. Despite the fact that Trump’s proposal has only been partially implemented, Jayla still sees the impact of it firsthand …

author: Sleshi Teshome Kehali
title: The Bone-Setters’ Ward: How Ancient Healers Are Filling Ethiopia’s Modern Healthcare Vacuum
content:
Reporting from Bahir Dar, Ethiopia


In a residential neighbourhood of Bahir Dar, in northwestern Ethiopia, patients visit the home of W/ro Birqe Yibre for help with injuries. Birqe, a traditional bone-setter known locally as a Wogesha, has practised for more than 20 years.


W/ro Birqe Yibre, a traditional bone-setter known locally as a Wogesha, sits in her residential courtyard in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia. She says she has practised for more than two decades. (Photo: Sleshi Teshome)


One of her patients, Yidersal Mengistu, came with a painful right foot and a bruised big toe after kicking a stone while playing football.


“I didn’t go to the hospital. To be honest, I prefer the traditional way,” Mengistu said. He explained that he had visited Birqe before for heel pain and believed her treatment had helped him. He also said she had treated him without charge on that earlier occasion.


“If I recover fully this time, I will pay her,” he said.


For Birqe, payment depends partly on what patients can afford. She said people who have money typically pay between 150 and 200 Ethiopian birr, while she treats those who cannot pay without charging them.


“If someone has no money, I treat them and tell them, ‘Go on, go home,’” she said. “You cannot turn away poor people.”


A study of 836 people with a history of injury in Mecha district, published in

BMC Complementary Medicine and Therapies

, found that 46.05 per cent had used traditional bone-setting services. Social acceptance was the most commonly reported reason for seeking this care. The findings reflect the study population in Mecha district and should not be taken as a national estimate.


For patients such as Mengistu, the decision is also shaped by personal experience and trust. But the treatment of fractures and other serious injuries can carry risks when patients delay seeking medical assessment.


Knowing When to Refer


Birqe said she distinguishes between injuries she believes she can treat and those that require hospital care.


“I handle muscle pulls and minor dislocations,” she said. “If someone comes with a serious, displaced bone or a deep fracture, I tell them plainly to go to the hospital. I don’t try to touch it.”


She said she was concerned about practitioners who accept serious cases despite lacking the necessary skills to manage them.


According to Birqe, some bone-setters bind injured limbs tightly with bamboo splints, locally known as Timaq, and continue treatment even when a patient’s condition worsens. She said some eventually advise patients to seek hospital care only after several visits.


“When parents bring me a child whose hand is already ruined, I tell them: ‘Run to the hospital, I won’t touch this,’” she said.


Her account highlights a distinction within traditional practice: while Birqe says she refers serious injuries, she believes other practitioners take on cases beyond their abilities. These claims describe her experience and observations; establishing how widespread such practices are would require further evidence.


A Crooked Arm


Thomas Habtamu, a student living in Bahir Dar, said a fall during a neighbourhood football match injured his left forearm. Because of his family’s financial difficulties, he did not go to a hospital and instead sought treatment from a local Wogesha.


“The healer kept massaging it week after week, telling me to be patient,” Habtamu recalled. He said the injury was close to the joint and that the treatment did not restore the arm to its normal position.


W/ro Birqe Yibre examines the injured foot and bruised big toe of Yidersal Mengistu in Bahir Dar. Mengistu said he injured his foot after kicking a stone while playing football and chose to seek traditional treatment. (Photo: Sleshi Teshome)


“He told me that if I ever fell down and hurt the arm again in the future, he might be able to reset it then,” Habtamu said.


Habtamu has never had the arm examined at a hospital. He said his forearm remains visibly bent and that he struggles with activities such as push-ups, lifting heavy objects and prolonged gym exercise.


He contrasted his experience with that of a friend who sustained a similar injury around the same time. According to Habtamu, his friend went to hospital, underwent an operation in which a metal plate was inserted, and recovered the use of his arm within about two months.

title: « L'émeute court plus vite que l'aliénation »
content:
Sommes-nous dans une situation pré-autoritaire ou pré-révolutionnaire ? L'insurrection est-elle un devoir en plus d'être un droit ? Faut-il articuler l'émeute au moment électoral ou pas du tout ? Nous nous posons ces questions avec Tristan Garcia (L'autorité est un chantage, 2026) et Patrice Maniglier (La terre ou le monde. Divergences cosmopolitiques. Avec Étienne Balibar. 2025).


À voir lundi 9 novembre :


Quand Marc Crépon affirme sur

C politique

 que l'incendie de la Mairie de Limoges le 17 octobre 2026 relève d'une « ivresse de la destruction » qui – d'une manière honnêtement

boomer

 – évoque pour lui la tarte à la crème du nihilisme des

Possédés

 de Dostoïevski, il ne se rend peut-être pas compte de l'hilarité universelle qu'il suscite chez à peu près tout le monde. Lorsque l'historien, professeur au collège de France, Patrick Boucheron, dans un entretien de Libération, le 31 octobre : dénonce ceux qui continuent de

« croire que la violence émeutière est toujours émancipatrice »

 et pose le constat que nous sommes en situation pré-autoritaire et pas prérévolutionnaire. Il ne se doute pas que nous rions tout autant.


Lundimatin

 n'a que faire des tautologies nihilistes et des dissociations sociales-démocrates. Notre position a toujours été celle de l'

Encyclopédie des émeutes

 : « Ce qui est intéressant dans l'émeute n'est pas une cause, mais un possible » (BE, II, 54). « Toute tentative des pauvres modernes pour organiser le débat sur le monde commence par une émeute : 1789, 1848, 1871, 1917, 1968, et en 1978 en Iran et au Nicaragua. » (BE, II, 55) C'est pourquoi l'émeute est pour nous « le début possible de la fin du monde » (55) et, en général, « un début de débat » sur cette fin (55). Toute émeute ne conduit pas à une insurrection ou une révolution, mais « il n'y a pas de révolution ni d'insurrection qui ne commencent par une émeute. » (55).


Nos invités ont peut-être d'autres idées sur la question, il faut néanmoins assumer que le débat sur le monde vient d'être relancé.

title: Das Recht auf sexuelle Selbstbestimmung
content:
Zwangssterilisation ist verboten. Dennoch erfahren Frauen mit Behinderungen häufig Druck von Angehörigen, Ärzt*innen oder Betreuer*innen, sich sterilisieren zu lassen.

Weißt du, wie viele Menschen ich begleitet habe, die darunter gelitten haben, dass sie sterilisiert wurden?“, fragte mich eine Beraterin am Telefon. Sie schult Menschen mit Behinderungen in Selbstbestimmung. Es war eines von hundert Gesprächen, die meine Kollegin Ramona Arzberger und ich geführt haben, um zur Verhütungspraxis bei Menschen mit Behinderungen zu recherchieren. Nach fast einem Jahr ist daraus der Film „Hauptsache, du kriegst kein Kind“ unseres Magazins „andererseits“ entstanden. Er begleitet mehrere Frauen in Deutschland und Österreich, die mit Lernschwierigkeiten leben und auf Unterstützung angewiesen sind. Drei von ihnen sind sterilisiert. Keine entschied allein. Elf Prozent der Frauen in deutschen Einrichtungen geben an, sterilisiert zu sein, so der Forschungsbericht zu Gewalt und Gewaltschutz in Einrichtungen der Behindertenhilfe des deutschen Bundesministeriums für Arbeit und Soziales von 2024. In Österreich waren es zuletzt 17 Prozent. In Deutschland habe fast die Hälfte der Betroffenen den Eingriff nicht von sich aus gewollt, heißt es in dem Bericht. In Österreich taucht in Befragungen dasselbe auf: Eltern, Ärzt*innen und Betreuer*innen hätten auf die Frauen eingewirkt. „Ich will auch mitmachen!“, platzte die Stimme von Hannelore Trtil ins Telefon, noch ehe meine Kollegin erfuhr, wer da sprach. Die 66-Jährige hatte unseren Flyer gesehen, der Betroffene erreichen sollte. In den 1980er-Jahren wurde sie in Wien „unterbunden“, ein anderes Wort für sterilisiert. „Die haben alle gesagt, man darf keine Kinder kriegen. Das habe ich nicht richtig gefunden. Und das habe ich nicht gewollt“, sagt sie im Film. Heute verbringt sie oft Zeit mit Kindern. Ihre OP-Akte hat das Krankenhaus vor etwa zehn Jahren vernichtet, nach Ablauf der Frist für Schadenersatz. Sie wird nie erfahren, welche Art von Sterilisation bei ihr gemacht wurde. Hannelore sagt auch, sie habe nie Sex gehabt, aus dem ein Kind hätte entstehen können. Diesen Satz haben wir in unseren Recherchen nicht nur von ihr gehört. Thea, die in Wirklichkeit anders heißt, wurde 2025 sterilisiert, in einem Alter, in dem manche noch nicht an Kinder denken. author: Tam Saavedra
title: WEI and UN Women Co-Launches Guide for Disability-Inclusive
content:
Across Asia and the Pacific, 350 million women and girls with disabilities navigate conflict, crisis, and climate instability. While they are frontline peacebuilders, community leaders, and human rights defenders, they remain systematically excluded from formal peace and security decision-making.

To break down these barriers, Women Enabled International (WEI) and the UN Women Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific have officially launched a landmark publication today: the Guidance Note on Disability-Inclusive National Action Plans on Women, Peace and Security in Asia and the Pacific. Released ahead of the annual UN Security Council high-level debate in New York, this first-of-its-kind guide provides a practical, policy-oriented blueprint for governments, policymakers, and civil society.

Read the full Guidance Note on Disability-Inclusive NAPs on WPS in Asia and the Pacific

Historically, women with disabilities in peace policies have been viewed narrowly as victims or passive recipients of protection. Co-drafted through consultations with 26 women and gender-diverse people with disabilities, in collaboration with Women Enabled International and the UN Women Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, this guide directly challenges that narrative. It grounds its framework in a human rights model of disability and the core movement principle: “Nothing about us without us”.

As WEI Executive Director Maryangel García-Ramos Guadiana stated during the launch:

“The true value of this Guidance Note is that it exists, not as a siloed document, but as a means to ensure we, as feminist disabled change-makers, are not left out of the agenda, but we are the ones who get to set the agenda.”

UN Women Regional Director for Asia and the Pacific, Christine Arab, added:

“National Action Plans on WPS that include everyone lead to peace that lasts.”

The publication was shaped by participatory research, drawing on focus groups and surveys with 26 grassroots leaders with diverse disabilities across the region. It addresses critical ground-level hurdles—including digital exclusion, inaccessible evacuation infrastructure, and ableism in mainstream spaces—ensuring that the voices of women, girls and gender-diverse people with disabilities form the foundation of the guidance.

The publication urges stakeholders to align National Action Plans (NAPs) with international standards—including the CRPD, CEDAW, and UN Security Council Resolution 2475—across all four WPS pillars:

Participation: Reserve seats for organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs)—especially women-led OPDs—on NAP steering committees with full accessibility support.

Participation: Reserve seats for organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs)—especially women-led OPDs—on NAP steering committees with full accessibility support.

Prevention: Recognize women and gender-diverse people with disabilities as active peacebuilders and integrate intersectional early-warning indicators.

Prevention: Recognize women and gender-diverse people with disabilities as active peacebuilders and integrate intersectional early-warning indicators.

Protection: Address unique forms of violence (such as caregiver abuse or institutionalization) and guarantee accessible shelters and evacuation procedures.

Protection: Address unique forms of violence (such as caregiver abuse or institutionalization) and guarantee accessible shelters and evacuation procedures.

Relief & Recovery: Ensure transitional justice mechanisms, reparations, and post-conflict upskilling actively include women with disabilities.

Relief & Recovery: Ensure transitional justice mechanisms, reparations, and post-conflict upskilling actively include women with disabilities.

The guide also features a practical Disability-Inclusive WPS NAP Checklist to help stakeholders evaluate progress at every stage of policy implementation.

This Guidance Note was made possible with the generous support of the Government of the Republic of Korea (through the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family) as part of the project “Promoting Leadership of Future Generation Peacebuilders and Change-makers in Asia and the Pacific”, and of the Australian Government under the Regional Framework Towards Peaceful, Inclusive Societies (2023–2027).

author: Nina Garcia Steel
title: Crossing Dimensions of Pain Without Losing My Soul
content:
A

s I sit here in my—as I like to call it—Oasis in the Desert, looking out my window at the morning clouds gloriously dancing to the tune the songbirds sing every morning is simply a treasure. I can smile at the sun and sway with the wind as it tickles my senses. I enjoy this morning view as I sip a cup of sweet herbal tea and take in the rays of light.


There was a time when such treasures were absent in my mind. I was living with undeniable pain that I could not explain, except in my poetry.


Photo by Nina Garcia Steel


It’s my heart that aches the most.


The feeling of nerves tearing and bones slowly breaking.


Flares of fire running through my veins.


The words that everyone took as metaphorical were literal words of agony from trauma that started decades earlier. It would take over half a century to discover the root cause of the autoimmune conditions that developed, the near dementia scares. At one point, I was having severe neurological attacks where I lost control of my limbs entirely, making them feel as though they were being tossed around like a rag doll. I picked three alcoholic husbands and stayed in abusive relationships. Little did I know that all of this was coming from the same place:

unprocessed trauma

.


It took me by surprise too. I had been making decisions about who I chose to be my mate based on what I thought was normal from what I experienced as a child. I had suffered sexual abuse more than once, starting when I was only 7 at the hands of a friend’s oldest brother, then an uncle who was visiting, with the worst culprit being my own father. What does a horrific experience like that do to the mind of an innocent child? Nobody was ever prosecuted, my therapy was abruptly stopped, and nothing was done. Left without justice or support, I was left to navigate the aftermath entirely on my own. This meant those early patterns quietly and unknowingly dictated my choices for years.


Decades later, the trauma manifested itself as depression. The connection wasn’t obvious because nobody asked the core question: What happened in your childhood?


So many individuals struggle with trauma that they cannot even name, for we are told, even by medical professionals, that we must focus on our future and that going backward is not in their school of thought. However, trauma is the poisonous seed that grows weeds of unnecessary pain that need to be destroyed at the root.


I walked with pride for so many years, challenging the status quo despite what had happened. I buried it without realizing that everything always comes back if not properly addressed. The pain of betrayal is doubly sharp when there’s unprocessed trauma in the background. It is unfortunate that the questions that could have shaped my treatment were not asked.


I always did things differently, even as early as 6 years old when I was selected to teach a kindergartener English, showing a precocious initiative and drive to bridge gaps long before I understood what systemic obstacles even were. I remember thinking that it was important for my student, Alicia, to learn hopscotch as that would make it easier for her to integrate with the other children. I was an ESL assistant from third to sixth grade. Selling shiny rocks door-to-door for ice-cream money at age 6, writing formal letters in Spanish to my grandfather at age 8. At just 14 years old, I served as the inventory buyer for our family shoe store. I was entrusted to travel on buying trips with an adult and curate the shoes for our inventory.


Learning the mechanics of commerce, spatial merchandising and inventory selection at such a young age taught me how to analyze systems, spot value, and exercise practical strategy long before I ever had to apply those skills to my own survival. At 15, that same drive led me to approach my high school principal with a proposal to redesign the school uniform. I saw how the existing uniforms lacked functionality and aesthetic timelessness, so I designed an updated, structurally timeless uniform that my school adopted. I was already practicing the art of seeing what needed change, organizing a solution, and taking decisive action.


I dared not dwell on the horror of the abuse I had experienced, not realizing that my body would keep score. At that stage, blocking the pain was pure survival. I hadn’t yet allowed my mind to acknowledge the true scope of what had happened — confronting it all at once would have destroyed me, so I compartmentalized …

title: Agustín Guillamón - Les comités de défense de la CNT à Barcelone (1933-1938)
content:
Auteur·e

: Agustín Guillamón

Titre

: Les comités de défense de la CNT à Barcelone (1933-1938)

Date

: 2017


 Tampon du Comité de Défense Local de Barcelone


LES COMITÉS DE DÉFENSE DE LA CNT À BARCELONE (1933-1938)


 Des Cadres de Défense aux Comités révolutionnaires de Quartier, aux Patrouilles de contrôle et aux Milices Populaires


AGUSTÍN GUILLAMÓN


 Première édition en espagnol : avril 2011. Seconde édition en espagnol : septembre 2011. Aldarull edicions. Barcelone.


 Ce livre a été traduit par le Collectif Anarchiste de Traduction et de Scannérisation (CATS) de Caen (et d’ailleurs) en avril et mai 2012, avec le concours précieux de l’auteur. Merci à S. de “La Bataille Socialiste” (

http://bataillesocialiste.wordpress.com/

) pour la mise en relation avec l’auteur. D’autres traductions subversives du CATS sont librement téléchargeables et diffusables sur son site :

http://ablogm.com/cats/


 Un premier brouillon initial (très bref) de ce travail fut publié dans le numéro extraordinaire de Solidaridad Obrera (janvier 2010) dédié au centenaire de la CNT.


 Plus de dirigeants, plus d’État Pour profiter de nos combats.


 — Raoul Vaneigem, La vie s’écoule, la vie s’enfuit


 Vivere militare est.


 — Sénèque. Lettres


 I didn’t say it would be easy, Neo. I just said it would be the truth.


 — Morpheus dans Matrix, Larry et Andy Wachowski.


 « Les révolutions sociales, ces tentatives de réorganisation de la production et de la société sur des nouvelles bases, sont extrêmement rares dans l’Histoire. Au delà des circonstances particulières dans lesquelles elles surgirent, elles nous apportent toujours une expérience irremplaçable, dans leurs succès comme, surtout, dans leurs échecs. Le grand enseignement de la révolution de 1936 a été la nécessité incontournable de la destruction de l’État ».


 Barricade construite le 19 Juillet 1936 sur le Paralelo, face à « El Molino ». Ici les Comités de Défense et le Syndicat du Bois de la CNT mirent en déroute l’armée soulevée.


1. DU RAPPORT DE SHAPIRO À CELUI D’OCTOBRE 1934


 Un rapport confidentiel, à la diffusion réduite, d’Alexandre Shapiro

[1]

, secrétaire de l’AIT, élaboré durant son séjour en Espagne en 1932-33, relatait ce qu’étaient et comment fonctionnaient les Comités de Défense, organisés exclusivement pour des tâches insurrectionnelles de choc, comme celle du 8 janvier 1933, dont il fut témoin. Ce rapport de Shapiro, sur les Comités de Défense, fut réalisé en pleine polémique entre FAIstes et trentistes

[2]

 sur l’opportunité, ou non, de la tactique d’insurrection immédiate, localiste et permanente. Shapiro fit une critique dévastatrice de l’improvisation, du manque d’organisation et de préparation de l’insurrection de janvier. Il dénonça, avec dureté, le fait qu’une même personne puisse détenir des charges aux secrétariats de la CNT et du Comité National de Défense, pour le confusionnisme que cela créait. Il démontra que, dans la pratique, s’était produite une soumission de la CNT aux décisions du Comité National des Comités de Défense (CNDC).


 Le rapport de Shapiro, qui bénéficiait de l’aide inestimable d’Eusebio Carbó, décrivait de cette manière les Cadres de Défense, existants en 1933 : « Ces Comités de Défense, qui existaient déjà depuis un certain temps, avaient comme unique but de préparer les armes nécessaires en cas d’insurrection, d’organiser les groupes de choc dans les différents quartiers populaires, d’organiser la résistance des soldats dans les casernes etc… ».


 Alors même que l’insurrection des Asturies était encore en cours, le CNCD constatait, dans un rapport

[3]

, l’échec de la tactique insurrectionnelle, défendue par le groupe Nosotros, connue populairement sous le nom de « gymnastique révolutionnaire », qu’il accusait précisément d’être responsable du manque de préparation de la CNT pour intervenir, au niveau national, dans l’insurrection d’octobre 1934. Le moment était venu de dépasser cette tactique, parce qu’elle avait démontré le caractère absurde et dangereux d’une insurrection locale à un moment inadéquat, sans une sérieuse préparation préalable, qui soumettait les libertaires à la répression étatique, sans jamais obtenir une extension populaire à tout le pays, ni l’adhésion des autres organisations, nécessaire pour affronter avec succès l’appareil militaire et répressif de l’État. Le pire de tout est que cette répression avait démantelé l’appareil militaire clandestin de la CNT, après les insurrections …

В маленькой редакционной комнате еженедельной пропагандистской газеты мы с наслаждением предавались дружеской беседе между товарищами, как вдруг вошёл рослый парень с ремнём за плечами.

Он весело поздоровался с присутствующими, расстегнул ремни, поставил ящик на пол и сел на него, вытирая пот.

Пока мы ждали, что он заговорит, мы молча рассматривали его. Это был высокий, широкоплечий юноша с чёрными усиками на смуглой, загорелой коже и живыми, искрящимися глазами, как пенистое вино. Одет он был в деревенскую одежду, с некоторыми городскими штрихами или отголосками города.

Наконец, с улыбкой, очень непринуждённо, гость назвал своё имя.

Администратор газеты прекрасно знал его как неутомимого активиста, который очень часто писал ему – то из одного населённого пункта, то из другого – и с дьявольской энергией распространял брошюры. Где бы он ни проходил, люди массами подписывались на газету. Если он не был коммивояжёром, то уж точно был Вечным жидом[1]… – Вечным жидом пропаганды, – сказал парень с ящиком, широко и довольно улыбаясь.

И поскольку на наших лицах откровенно разливалась жадная любопытность, он принялся в общих чертах рассказывать о своей кочевой жизни.

В городе он был механиком и уже зарабатывал хорошую зарплату. Но, будучи человеком читающим и стремящимся к знаниям, завсегдатаем собраний, жадно ловившим каждое слово из дискуссий, которые велись в помещении профсоюза, он вскоре воспламенился нашим прекрасным идеалом человеческого освобождения. И тут же его охватила ненасытная жажда обращать в свою веру, тут же его озаботила великая проблема сельской пропаганды, сеяния за пределами промышленных центров – по этим обширным невозделанным полям провинции, тревожным и полным тайны. Далеко ли может зайти любая попытка городского рабочего, одинокого и встречающего враждебность? Почему бы не последовать прекрасному примеру русских революционеров, которые идут жить и работать среди крестьян?

Молодой и крепкий, без семейных обязательств, в один прекрасный день наш парень отправился по этим землям. Он запасся полезными и дешёвыми предметами, которые продавал с минимальной прибылью. Он изучил основы различных ремёсел и был на селе услужливым умельцем на все руки. В деревенских хижинах не было мебели или утвари, которую он не сумел бы починить или даже изготовить. Он даже чинил грубую обувь, за неимением сапожника, и нередко видели, как он вносил свой изобретательный вклад в ремонт или строительство домов…

При этом он довольствовался малым. Есть и спать – как придётся: иногда лучше, иногда хуже; иногда за несколько грошей, иногда в уплату за работу. В жаркое время он не брезговал спать под открытым небом, на гумнах или под скирдами. Умирать – не умирал. В общем: жил помаленьку – и со здоровьицем…

Таким образом он быстро завоёвывал сердца и доверие людей из деревень и маленьких городков, которые внимательно слушали его беседы и публичные чтения, охотно принимали его брошюры и газеты, задумчиво следили за ясными и светлыми картинами будущего, будущего с большей свободой и большим довольством.

Мы с волнением смотрели на доброго сеятеля, запоминая его облик и черты, словно пытаясь увидеть воплощение той благороднейшей страсти и того животворящего героизма.

— Вот уже пять лет веду эту жизнь, – просто заключил он.

Мы предположили, что он имеет в виду холеру и месть властей. Нет; мы поняли неправильно: речь шла об узах любви. Случаев и соблазнов ему не хватало; и не то чтобы он хвастался, но о многих он знал, что они не сказали бы ему «нет»… Но, честно говоря, решение не казалось ему из самых лёгких, как и не находил он лёгким найти женщину, которая бы ему подошла. Ужасная проблема…

И когда доблестный парень собрался уходить, уже приготовив свой запас печатной …

Author:

An Anarchist FAQ


PDF File Size:

The Anarchist FAQ presents a compelling vision of parenting based on freedom, mutual respect and trust in children’s natural capacity for self-regulation, challenging the authoritarian assumptions embedded in conventional family structures. Its strongest contribution is connecting the personal and political, arguing that raising children without coercion, punishment or imposed moralism is itself a form of anarchist practice. It places freedom, mutual respect and autonomy at the heart of parenting. It challenges us to reject the authoritarian structures of the traditional family and recognise that raising free, confident and independent children is an essential part of building a free society.


Source:

 An Anarchist FAQ found at

https://ananarchistfaq.anarcho-copy.org/

Anarchist Parenting


 An Anarchist FAQ


 


Introduction:

 What methods of child rearing do anarchists advocate?


Part 1:

 What are the main obstacles to raising free children?


Part 2:

What are some examples of libertarian child-rearing methods?


Part 3:

 If children have nothing to fear, how can they be good?


Part 4:

Part 5:

What is the anarchist position on teenage sexual liberation?


Part 7:

 But isn’t this concern with sexual liberation just a distraction from revolution?


Introduction:

What methods of child rearing do anarchists advocate?


Anarchists have long been aware of the importance of child rearing and education. We are aware that child rearing should aim to develop

“a well-rounded individuality”

 and not

“a patient work slave, professional automaton, tax-paying citizen, or righteous moralist.”

 In this section of the FAQ [see

here

] we will discuss anarchist approaches to child rearing bearing in mind

“that it is through the channel of the child that the development of the mature man [or woman] must go, and that the present ideas of . . . educating or training . . . are such as to stifle the natural growth of the child.”

 [Emma Goldman,

Red Emma Speaks

, p. 132 and p. 131]


If one accepts the thesis that the authoritarian family is the breeding ground for both individual psychological problems and political reaction, it follows that anarchists should try to develop ways of raising children that will not psychologically cripple them but instead enable them to accept freedom and responsibility while developing natural self-regulation. We will refer to children raised in such a way as

“free children.”


Work in this field is still in its infancy (no pun intended). Wilhelm Reich was the main pioneer in this field (an excellent, short introduction to his ideas can be found in Maurice Brinton’s

The Irrational in Politics

). In

Children of the Future

, Reich made numerous suggestions, based on his research and clinical experience, for parents, psychologists, and educators striving to develop libertarian methods of child rearing (although he did not use the term “libertarian”).


In this and the following sections we will summarise Reich’s main ideas as well as those of other libertarian psychologists and educators who have been influenced by him, such as A.S. Neill and Alexander Lowen. We will examine the theoretical principles involved in raising free children and will illustrate their practical application with concrete examples. Finally, we will examine the anarchist approach to the problems of adolescence.


Such an approach to child rearing is based upon the insight that children

“do not constitute anyone’s property: they are neither the property of the parents nor even of society. They belong only to their own future freedom.”

 [Michael Bakunin,

The Political Philosophy of Bakunin

, p. 327] As such, what happens to a child when they are growing up

shapes

 the person they become and the society they live in. The key question for people interested in freedom is whether

“the child [is] to be considered as an individuality, or as an object to be moulded according to the whims and fancies of those about it?”

 [Emma Goldman,

Op. Cit.

, p. 131] Libertarian child rearing is the means by which the individuality of the child is respected and developed.


This is in stark contrast to standard capitalist claim that children are the

property

 of their parents …

Anarchie ist ein fortlaufender Prozess zur Demontage von Autorität.

Anarchie ist die unerbittliche Verneinung von Herrschaftsstrukturen, das Bestreben, sich kleine Bereiche des Lebens frei von Ausbeutung und Leid zu schaffen.

Anarchie ist der kompromisslose Vorstoß gegen Unterdrückung und die lautstarke Forderung nach Autonomie und Selbstbestimmung, die Ablehnung aller Klassen, Institutionen und Dogmen, die geschaffen wurden, um Menschen zu beherrschen.

Anarchie ist vor allem eine Praxis, nicht eine Theorie. Es geht darum, aktiv daran zu arbeiten, autoritäre Verhältnisse zu beenden, wo immer sie existieren, und nicht-autoritäre Alternativen aufzubauen. Es geht nicht darum, eine Lebensweise für einen imaginären Ort, eine imaginäre Zeit und imaginäre Menschen vorzuschreiben. Es geht um reale Menschen und die Bewältigung realer Probleme.

Anarchie ist eine lebendige und atmende Praxis, die wir in unser tägliches Leben einbauen. Eine persönliche Haltung gegen die Herrschaft, die alle unsere Entscheidungen beeinflusst und so den Verlauf unserer Existenz prägt.

Es gibt kein Endziel für Anarchie. Sie ist ein fortwährender, nicht enden wollender Kampf gegen hierarchische Strukturen und die Autoritätspersonen, die im Luxus an der Spitze dieser Strukturen sitzen.

Anarchie ist der Wunsch nach Freiheit von Tyrannei. Anarchie sind unzählige Generationen verschiedener Menschen mit dem Drang, freier zu sein als sie es unter den Systemen sind, die sie gewaltsam regieren.

Anarchie ist die Ablehnung der Regierung, der Staaten, der Grenzen, des Kapitals, des Patriarchats, des Gender-Essenzialismus, der Sklaverei, der Ideologie, der Rechten, der Linken, des Klerus, der Demokratie, des Privateigentums, der Technokratie, der Kernfamilie, des Humanismus, des Imperialismus, der Gefängnisse, der Fabriken, der Gründerväter, der Bürokratie, der Ethnokratie, der Heteronormativität, der Idole, der Tradition, der Polizeiarbeit, der Neuronormativität, des Ökozids, der Zivilisation und jeder anderen Form von Autorität.

Anarchie ist Gemeinschaftsgärten, Umsonstläden, Graffiti, 3D-gedruckte Waffen, FKK, vegane Potlucks [1], Hausbesetzungen, Lebensmittelwälder, Sabotage von Pipelines, freie Software, die Befreiung von Kühen, Ladendiebstahl, das Sichern von Saatgut alter Kulturpflanzen, die Bildung autonomer Zonen, Attentate auf Tyrannen, Guerilla-Gärtnern, Zines schreiben, Regenwasser auffangen, Wahlurnen verbrennen, Biodiversität, Abschaffung der Whiteness, Hacken, Aquaponik, Musik machen, Upcycling, Polizeistationen abfackeln und Wildblumen in der ganzen Landschaft säen.

Anarchist*innen sind jene Personen, die sich weigern, von irgendjemandem oder irgendetwas regiert, beherrscht oder dominiert zu werden. Anarchist*innen sind wütende, verbitterte, verlorene, ängstliche, desillusionierte, gewalttätige, friedliche, mutige, idealistische, mitreißende, furchtlose Träumende.

Ein*e Anarchist*in steht allein gegen die riesige Flut der Autorität, die in alle Richtungen ansteigt. Anarchist*innen verbinden sich mit jeder geschundenen, geknechteten Seele im gemeinsamen Angriff gegen die rücksichtslosen Systeme, die uns entmachten und entfremden sollen.

Anarchie ist geprägt von endlosen Widersprüchen, existenzieller Angst und unerträglichen inneren Konflikten, und doch ergibt Anarchie für jede Person, die entsetzt oder wütend ist über die groben Ungerechtigkeiten, die diesen kleinen blauen Planeten verschlingen, einen perfekten Sinn. Anarchie ist für jede Person, die ein Leben in Würde anstrebt.

Anarchie ist ein unmögliches, absonderliches, aber für unser Überleben notwendiges Streben.

author: Archipelago Anarchist Archive
title: Archipelago Anarchist Archive, Perpustakaan Anarkis, and Anarsip: Jurnal Arsip & Perpustakaan Anti-otoritarian (A Brief Introduction)
content:
Initiatives in anarchist archiving, librarianship, and journals of archives & libraries in Indonesia

The Archipelago Anarchist Archive (AAA) is an informal, alternative archives and library initiative established in 2024 with the aim of preserving and distributing anti-authoritarian materials. AAA is driven by a number of anarchist archivists and librarians from various cities in Indonesia.

The materials that AAA focuses on are those produced in, and related to, the archipelago (known as Indonesia), whether in Indonesian or in non-Indonesian languages. These materials can take the form of texts, photographs, audio, video, and so on. All of AAA's digital archive collections can be accessed through the Internet Archive.

Link to the Archipelago Anarchist Archive collection: https://archive.org/details/@archipelago-anti-authoritarian-archive

Perpustakaan Anarkis (Anarchist Library) is an preservation and distribution project for anti-authoritarian materials based on plain text. Plain text was chosen because it makes it easier for authors and translators to distribute their work, easier for publishers to reproduce it, and easier for those who wish to archive it[1]. Perpustakaan Anarkis understands anti-authoritarianism in a flexible manner, though not without limits. Therefore, it can be said that Perpustakaan Anarkis accepts and includes both anarchist materials (from all tendencies, except anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-nationalism) and materials that can enrich anarchism, such as avant-garde(ism) that challenges not only the boundaries of art but also the state and centralized power, libertarian Marxism, autonomism, democratic confederalism, and so on. In addition, Perpustakaan Anarkis also accepts and includes reportage from the front lines (confrontation) and the home front (care) of flashpoints of popular struggle and resistance, labor strikes, and so on.

Because in anarchism, decentralization and prefiguration are important. And by practicing decentralization and prefiguration, we (and us all) no longer need to wait to act and be overly dependent on a single central point.

Besides anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-nationalism, Perpustakaan Anarkis is also not intended for authoritarian Marxists, misanthropic individuals, extractive technologism (automation that subordinates), avant-garde(ism) that leads to fascism, and other authoritarian tendencies and centralized power.

[1] Authors and translators can distribute their works without the hassle of layout, editing, cover design, and other technical work. Conversely, publishers no longer need to go through the trouble of dealing with writing and translation. And archivists—in addition to finding archiving easier—will receive various versions of the work.

Link to the Perpustakaan Anarkis collection: https://id.anarchistlibraries.net/special/index

Anarsip: Jurnal Arsip & Perpustakaan Anti-otoritarian (Anarsip: Journal of Anti-authoritarian Archives & Libraries) (published periodically, every 6 months) is a space for theorizing–practicing–theorizing–practicing anarchist archives and librarianship. Because we believe that anarchist archives and librarianship should not stop at merely the definition of "managed by, and archiving materials of, anarchist(s) and/or anti-authoritarian [movements and ideas]," but also means using methods, practicing ways of working, and thinking in an anarchist and/or anti-authoritarian manner. If the Situationist International said "to be avant-garde is to move in step with reality" (Internationale Situationiste #8); then we say "to be anarchist archiving and librarianship is to move in step with reality and anarchism."

Link to follow the developments of Anarsip: https://id.anarchistlibraries.net/special/anarsip-jurnal-arsip-perpustakaan-anti-otoritarian

Archipelago Anarchist Archive (AAA) adalah inisiatif pengarsipan dan perpustakaan informal nan alternatif yang didirikan pada tahun 2024 dengan tujuan mempreservasi sekaligus mendistribusi materi-materi anti-otoritarian. AAA digerakkan oleh sejumlah arsiparis dan pustakawan anarkis yang berasal dari berbagai kota di Indonesia.

Adapun materi-materi yang menjadi fokus dari AAA adalah materi-materi yang diproduksi di, dan yang berkaitan dengan, wilayah kepulauan (yang kini disebut sebagai Indonesia) baik itu yang berbahasa Indonesia maupun yang berbahasa non-indonesia. title: Carl Ahlteen - Josef Hillström
content:
Författare

: Carl Ahlteen

Titel

: Josef Hillström

Undertitel

: (1 års minne)

Källa

: Allarm november 1916


 Ett år har nu gått till ända sedan den tiden då vi ännu hade vår präktige kamrat i livet.


 Vi alla, som i fjor i slutet av oktober och b örjan av november månad tillhörde organisationen, minns allt för väl med vilken spänning vi emotsågo den dagen då Hillström skulle återfå friheten.


 Få av oss kunde trots allt tro att den

kristna statsliga

 mordlusten skulle ta ett sådant uttryck som detta: mörda en människa, endast därför att hans hjärta klappade för proletariatets frigörelse. Han, denne präktige kamrat anklagades för mord av en f. d. polisman, handlare, där tyckte man sig finna bevis nog. Hur hade det varit om det endast hade varit en handlande, ej en f. d. polisman? Å på det sätt den kristna staten gick tillväga mot Josef Hillström kunde de utan vidare anklaga en som fanns i New York eller någon annan avlägsen stad, för brottet i Salt Lake, Utah. Man behövde ej det ringaste bevis i fallet Josef Hillström därför skulle det givetvis ej behövas i det andra fallet heller.


 En sak var det som var nog: Josef Hillström diktade arbetarsånger av sådan art att gamla och unga rycktes med för dess känslighet och sanningsrika manande innehåll.


 Hade Hillström diktat kristna sånger, hade han levat den dag som i dag är, och varit omgjordad med lyx och överflöd. Hade Bruno ljugit lika fräckt som de kristna prästerna i Rom hade han ej blivit bränd på bål.


..Å du förbannade kristna rättvisa, du mördar ädla män och sanningssökare. Hitintills har du undgått straffet, men det väntar dig! Lederna tätna!


 Den kristna fräcka råheten har förmått att hålla sig vid liv en rätt lång tid, men den tidens längd som återstår är nog snart räknad. Över hela jorden höres hoten av starka män, och lederna tätna. Det bådar domsdagar för förtrycket.


 Strax efter Hillströms häktning erhöll jag brev från honom vart han omtalade hur det kom sig att han var i fängelset. Han själv ansåg det hela som en komedi, och kunde givetvis aldrig tro att man i en tidsålder som denna kunde begå ett sådant brott mot honom som blev gjort.


 Regelbundet hade jag brev och vykort från honom, och regelbundet sände jag honom tidningar, vilka han fick mottaga ända tills i juni månad 1915. Han bad mig då sända dem till en kvinnlig kamrat som personligen gav honom dem. Inom kort blev detta också omöjligt.


 Hela tiden hade vår präktige kamrat hoppet framme, alltid framhöll han att snart skola de väl i alla fall inse sitt brott mot mig och frigiva mig. Efter möjligheterna att få läsa böcker och tidningar blevo stängda, förstod vår kamrat vad saken gällde, han förstod att det kristna packet ej kunde tillfredsställas med mindre än att se hans huvud på ett fat.


 Han förstod att endast en räddning återstod för honom, det var att massorna organiserade sig och ryckte honom ur mördarhordens händer. Rättvisan genom borgarnas lag trodde han berättigat nog ej mera på.


 Över hela Amerika hölls "Joe Hill" möten, över hela Amerika talade man sympatiskt, och i form av kontanter lade man sin tribut. Man gjorde allt man kunde sade man.


 Ja man gjorde allt man kunde fredligt - vad som var tillåtet av Hillströms mördare - men var det nog? Tänk än en gång efter arbetare om det var nog. Vi ha tre kamrater nu sittande väntande på samma som "Joe Hill" kamraterna på "Messeba Range". Skall man även i detta fall hålla sig inom ramen av borgarnas lag? Skall man efter den blodiga rättvisan fullbordat sitt verk med dem säga: vi gjorde allt vi kunde.

vad är rätt för borgaren och borgarens stat?


Jo! att fylla sitt eget behov, göra vad som passar deras intresse. Om detta blir gjort inom eller utom ramen av den s. k. rättvisan, eller med eller mot slavarnas vilja bekymrar ej dem det minsta. Slavarna de måste innan de handla ha reda på om det är rätt, och i sin stora enfald gå de till sina dödssvurne fiender och fråga om det är rätt.


Idiotiskt handlingssätt, utfört av slavar och viljelösa, och av dem endast.


 Borgarna ha, på grund av slavarnas feghet

makt

 och detta är nog för dem att få rätt.


 Slavarna uraktläto att organisera sig och med makt uttaga Hillström.

Den 19 november kom, och hydran frossade av det unga, flytande, varma, kamratblodet.

 Några minuters blodflöde och hon var tillfredsställd. Han låg där nu dödad denne vår präktige kamrat. Hans ädla hjärta hade upphört att slå, hans hand kunde ej mera föra den penna som på en kort tid sände ut så många …
