Expropriation des capitalistes :

Maria « Maryusa » Nikiforova (1885–1919)

« Un programme politique n’a de valeur que lorsque, sortant des généralités vagues, il détermine bien précisément les institutions qu’il propose à la place de celles qu’il veut renverser ou réformer. »

OLIVIER BESANCENOT ET MICHAËL LÖWY ont publié un ouvrage intitulé Affinités révolutionnaires, Nos étoiles rouges et noires, qui entend mettre en relief les « alliances et solidarités agissantes entre les deux mouvements ». Les deux auteurs veulent, disent-ils, « éclairer ce versant ignoré, souvent délibérément, qui révèle la fraternité de leurs combats ». Cela me paraît une excellente idée[1].

Le présent ouvrage n’est cependant pas à strictement parler une réponse à Affinités révolutionnaires : en effet, le mode d’exposition de leurs idées choisi par Besancenot & Löwy, au moins dans la partie historique, ne permet pas de répondre, parce que leur argumentation est trop allusive et vague, fondée sur un exposé extrêmement approximatif des faits. C’est pourquoi, plutôt que de répondre, j’ai simplement choisi d’aborder les mêmes faits, les mêmes questions, mais à notre manière : le lecteur se fera lui-même une idée.

Il peut déjà se faire une idée de la conception qu’ont Besancenot & Löwy des « affinités révolutionnaires » en constatant la présence d’un portrait pleine page de Marx, mais aucun portrait de Proudhon, Bakounine, Kropotkine.

Chaque fois que le marxisme est en crise, il fait le choix entre deux attitudes, selon les cas :

author: infolibre
title: Παρέμβαση στη λέσχη ΑΠΘ, Πέμπτη 19/11, στις 12.30
content:
Παρέμβαση στη λέσχη του ΑΠΘ από φοιτητικά σχήματα ενάντια στους ελέγχους και τους φραγμούς που μπαίνουν στην δυνατότητα σίτισης στη φοιτητική λέσχη αλλά και τα σχέδια θέσπισης οικονομικού αντίτιμου για την πρόσβαση στην παροχή αυτή. Φοιτητές/τριες απαιτούν δωρεάν και μη ελεγχόμενη σίτιση για όλη τη κοινωνία και αξιοπρεπείς συνθήκες εργασίας για τους εργαζομένους στη λέσχη του ΑΠΘ.


Καλέσματα:


Αυτόνομο Σχήμα ★ Πολιτικών Μηχανικών


Πρυτανικές αρχές και κράτος, κεφάλαιο και ιδιωτικές εταιρείες, φαίνεται να γνωρίζουν καλύτερα πόσο πεινάμε και πόση ανάγκη έχουμε ένα πιάτο φαγητό – μπορει και δύο – ως φοιτητά και μη, σε μια καθημερινότητα που σε λίγο θα πληρώνουμε και τον αέρα που αναπνέουμε.Προφανώς, το θράσος τους δεν μας προκαλέι καμία έκπληξη, καθώς ο κεφαλαιοκρατικός τους τρόπος προσέγγισης της πραγματικότητας δεν θα μπορούσε να καταλήγει σε διαφορετικό αποτέλεσμα απο την στοχευμένη και μεθοδευμένη διαδικασία ιδιωτικοποίησης της πανεπιστημιακης λέσχης, που πολλά χρόνια παραμονεύει.


Κομβικό σημείο ωστόσο αποτελέι ο Ιούλιος του 2022, με την ψηφιση του άρθρου 296 του νόμου 4957/2022 και την εφαρμογή του τελικά την 1η Ιουλίου του 2023, όπου καταργείται ως ανεξάρτητο νομικό πρόσωπο δημοσίου δικαίου η πανεπιστημιακή λέσχη του ΑΠΘ, μαζί με τα ταμεία Διοίκησης και Διαχείρισης Πανεπιστημιακών Δασών και Αγροκτήματος. Τα τρία αυτά νομικά πρόσωπα, συγχωνεύονται και ενσωματώνονται στην διοικητική δομή του Αριστοτελείου, κάτω από τις μύτες μας, παρά τις καταγγελίες της συγκλήτου ΑΠΘ, των διαφόρων τμημάτων και των φοιτητών, για το γεγονός ότι η συγχώνευση αναμένεται να προκαλέσει σοβαρά λειτουργικά και οικονομικά προβλήματα στη σίτιση. Με απλούστερα λόγια, καταργείται το αυτόνομο ταμείο της λέσχης και πλέον η σίτιση εντάσσεται στον κεντρικό προϋπολογισμό του πανεπιστημίου, του οποίου προτεραιότητα κάθε τι άλλο πέρα από το τι θα φάμε είναι. Κάμερες, security, τουρνικέ, ερευνητικά προγράμματα για ελληνικό στρατό, ΝΑΤΟ και Ισραήλ, και μια διοίκηση της οποίας τα χέρια είναι “δεμένα” από το κράτος καθώς δεν επιτρέπεται νομικά να καλυφθούν τα έξοδα σίτισης για μη δικαιούχους κάρτας, με πρώτο ρουφιάνο τις πρυτανικές αρχές. Άραγε, πόσο μας ωφελεί μια διοίκηση, ένας νόμος και ένα κράτος που δεν αντιλαμβάνεται την σίτιση ως κοινωνικό δικαίωμα, αλλά ως στεγνή λογιστική εξίσωση;


Η διαδικασία εντατικοποίησης των ελέγχων με απώτερο σκοπό τελικά την καθιέρωση οικονομικού αντίτιμου για τους μη δικαιούχους κάρτας σίτισης και την πλήρη ιδιωτικοποίηση της πανεπιστημιακής λέσχης, σίγουρα δεν ξεκίνησε το 2022, ούτε αποτελεί στόχο μιας μεμονωμένης πρυτανικής αρχής ή κομματικής γραμμής. Η ιδιωτικοποίηση του θεσμού της παιδείας είναι έκτρωμα τόσο του ίδιου του παθογενούς καπιταλιστικού συστήματος που επιβάλει όρους κεφαλαίου και γελοία οικονομικά κριτήρια στις ανάγκες μας, όσο και του κράτους που το προστατεύει.


Εναντιωνόμαστε σε όλα τα παραπάνω . Συνεχίζουμε τους αγώνες μας . Διεκδικούμε τα αυτονόητα και δεν κάνουμε ούτε βήμα πίσω.


Αύριο στις 12:30, σπάμε τον έλεγχο της φοιτητικής λέσχης και εξασφαλίζουμε το μοίρασμα φαγητού σε όλα.


Γιατί το μόνο κριτήριο που αναγνωρίζουμε για το ποίοι/ες/α και το πόσο θα φάμε στην λέσχη, είναι η πείνα μας.


Τροφή για σκέψη και τροφή για τα στομάχια μας.


Αυτόνομη Παρέμβαση στους Ηλεκτρολόγους και τους Μηχανολόγους


Παρέμβαση στη Λέσχη ΑΠΘ την Πέμπτη 19/11 στις 12:30


ΣΤΗ ΛΕΣΧΗ ΘΑ ΤΡΩΜΕ ΜΕ ΜΟΝΟ ΚΡΙΤΗΡΙΟ ΤΗΝ ΠΕΙΝΑ ΜΑΣ


Τα τελευταία χρόνια βλέπουμε μια προσπάθεια να καθιερώθει ο έλεγχος κάρτας σίτισης στη λέσχη του ΑΠΘ. Τόσα χρόνια ο έλεγχος ήταν υποτυπώδης, αν όχι ανύπαρκτος, όχι επειδή μας κάνουν χάρη, αλλά ως κεκτημένο αγώνων και παρεμβάσεων. Φέτος όμως βλέπουμε μια όξυνση του ελέγχου με την αύξηση των security που κλείνουν τις πόρτες εισόδου και την τοποθέτηση συναγερμών σε περιφερειακές πόρτες, συγκεκριμένα στις εξόδους κινδύνου του κτιρίου, ώστε να μην μπορούν να μπαίνουν και να βγαίνουν άτομα από εκεί.


Η λέσχη του ΑΠΘ υπάρχει για να καλύπτει τις ανάγκες μας για φαγητό και κριτήρια στην πείνα δεν χωράνε. Συνεχώς ακούμε πως τα κριτήρια είναι ελαστικά οπότε πάντα όλες θα τρώμε δωρεάν παρ’ όλα αυτά κανείς δεν μας εγγυάται ότι στο μέλλον δεν θα αυστηροποιηθούν ή δεν θα χρειάζεται να πληρώνουμε 4 και 5€ για νερωμένα μακαρόνια και προχθεσινή σαλάτα. Ως φοιτητά που δεν νοιαζόμαστε μόνο για την πάρτη μας θέλουμε το φαγητό που προορίζεται για εμάς ,αλλά προφανώς περισσεύει, να διατίθεται και σε άλλα κομμάτια της κοινωνίας. Θέλουμε να μοιραζόμαστε το γεύμα μας με μεταναστά, άστεγα και όποιο άλλο άτομο δεν …

title: Women's Peace Monitoring Commission established in Istanbul
content:
The Women's Peace Monitoring and Follow-up Commission announced its establishment following preparatory meetings involving approximately 100 women.


The commission announced its establishment at a press conference held at the Kadın Zamanı Association. It aims to be represented on the Independent Monitoring Board to be established under the framework law adopted by Parliament. Representatives of women's organisations and many other women attended the meeting, where participants chanted the slogan "Jin, jiyan, azadî" (Woman, Life, Freedom).


The statement emphasised that lasting peace requires more than an end to conflict. It also involves confronting the past, uncovering the truth, ensuring justice and rebuilding society.


The statement drew attention to the impact of war, forced displacement and losses experienced across generations on women, stressing that women's equal participation and authority in decision-making mechanisms are fundamental to lasting peace.


The statement noted that women experience war and conflict in different ways, including imprisonment, poverty, male violence, labour exploitation and displacement, but that these experiences are often made invisible in peace processes. The commission stressed the need for independent monitoring of the process from a gender equality perspective.


The commission said that its first priority would be to monitor the implementation of Framework Law No. 7595, adopted by Parliament, and the recommendations contained in Sections 6 and 7 of the parliamentary commission's report.


The statement continued: "Following a meeting involving approximately 100 women, we decided to move forward as the Women's Peace Monitoring and Follow-up Commission. We hereby announce the establishment of our commission. We are still at the beginning of this journey. Our first priority will be to monitor the implementation of Framework Law No. 7595 adopted by Parliament, the rationale behind the law and the recommendations contained in Sections 6 and 7 of the commission's report, as well as the legal and political steps necessary to resolve the Kurdish question and democratise Turkey. We aim to monitor these steps, the laws enacted and the mechanisms established, their impact on everyday life, the obstacles they face, their shortcomings, what remains undone and what is made invisible, through women's eyes and drawing on the experience of the women's freedom struggle. We also aim to make our voices heard on these issues. We believe it is essential to exert pressure in favour of peace wherever the necessary steps are not taken. In this process, we need to speak out more, not remain silent. We will do this through reports, visits, monitoring delegations, various subcommissions and other methods we develop together, and we will regularly share our findings with the public. Above all, we call on all women to monitor this process with us and join the commission at every stage. Let us take responsibility together for building an equal and lasting peace. We remind those in positions of decision-making authority: We are watching you. We women will hold you accountable for peace!"

author: Unknown
title: Janet Biehl: Democratic integration should guide the peace process
content:
American writer and social ecology thinker Janet Biehl, in an assessment she wrote on Abdullah Öcalan’s 27 February 2025 Call for Peace and a Democratic Society, emphasised the importance of democratic and legal steps for advancing the peace process in Turkey.


Statements and letters prepared as part of an international solidarity campaign launched with the participation of 97 intellectuals will be published as an English-language e-book by Daraja Press.


Janet Biehl’s foreword to the book, entitled “The Call for Peace and a Democratic Society”, was also conveyed to the Imrali Delegation.


In her article, Janet Biehl said that the Framework Law adopted by Parliament was of vital importance for advancing the process. She said that, following confirmation by the National Security Council of the PKK’s disarmament steps, the way could be paved for the reintegration into social life of political prisoners and some PKK members living abroad.


However, Janet Biehl emphasised that, alongside the implementation of the legal framework, additional confidence-building measures were also necessary. In this regard, she outlined a number of demands, including clarifying Abdullah Öcalan’s status, ending the appointment of trustees, releasing political prisoners, guaranteeing the healthcare rights of sick prisoners, and lifting restrictions on Kurdish political activities and the media.


She also identified the release of Selahattin Demirtaş and Figen Yüksekdağ, as well as guarantees allowing PKK members who lay down their arms to participate in politics, as necessary steps.


A pluralistic and democratic society


Biehl said that the assessments made by other intellectuals featured in the book also set out the objectives of the peace process. Key themes emerging from these contributions include a multi-ethnic political system, the coexistence of peoples on equal terms, the democratisation of the nation-state and the construction of a pluralistic society.


Referring also to Abdullah Öcalan’s principle of “democratic integration”, Biehl highlighted the importance of establishing a system in which different peoples can coexist within a shared political sphere, free from relations of domination.


Biehl concluded her foreword with the following words: “I hope that these voices and ideas will serve as guiding lights for the peace process over the coming months and years.”


Janet Biehl


Janet Biehl is an American writer, translator and social ecology thinker. Having worked alongside Murray Bookchin for many years, she is known for her work on social ecology, libertarian municipalism and democratic confederalism.

author: CNT Madrid
title: Rechazar su presente, imaginar nuestro futuro: la I Estratégica de CNT Madrid
content:
Entramos en un nuevo ciclo de luchas inaugurado con la acampada de Sol en nuestra ciudad y con la huelga general que convocamos el pasado 11 de noviembre. Para abordarlo, la CNT de Madrid necesita fijar su rumbo. Por ello, el sindicato celebra

estos días 20 y 21 de noviembre

 su primera asamblea Estratégica.


Estratégica es el nombre con el que la militancia del sindicato de oficios varios de Madrid capital adherido a la Confederación Nacional del Trabajo ha dado a conocer lo que es una

asamblea extraordinaria

 que pone punto y aparte a varios meses de discusiones y debates en nuestra interna. Durante cerca de medio año, compañeras de toda nuestra organización vienen trabajando con ahínco en dotarnos de un espacio para decidir cuestiones fundamentales que atañen al futuro de CNT Madrid.


El papel del sindicato en la lucha de la vivienda, afianzar la presencia de nuestra anarcosindical en los barrios de Madrid, tener clara una postura frente a la inteligencia artificial. No son pocos los desafíos que como clase trabajadora organizada debemos afrontar. También tenemos la certeza de que son muchas las manos militantes que han ido llegando en los últimos meses al sindicato, en respuesta a una llamada tan simple como necesaria: solas no podemos, juntas sí.


Por eso CNT Madrid ha convenido que este encuentro de la Estratégica 2026 debe servir también como un lugar de encuentro para un período de reflexión ante todo lo que se nos viene. Por eso, de hecho, el leitmotiv que nos lleva a esta primera Estratégica es un eslogan muy sencillo:

rechazar su presente, imaginar nuestro futuro.


Rechazamos el presente que nos pretenden imponer, uno en el que el rentismo y el capitalismo continúan asfixiando a una clase trabajadora que además sufre la violencia política, económica y policial de una ultraderecha tan embrutecida como siempre.


Frente a ese presente que nos pretenden imponer, la CNT de Madrid empieza a imaginar nuestro futuro. Pero no desde posiciones vagas o de ensoñaciones improductivas: poniendo en orden nuestras prioridades, tácticas y finalidades, siempre en consonancia con la Confederación Nacional del Trabajo a la que orgullosamente nos adherimos, y que lleva más de un siglo estando donde tiene que estar: en la lucha.


Si quieres participar y construir también sindicalismo de base, no esperes más y afíliate. Si no vives en Madrid hay un cada vez mayor número de sindicatos de la CNT repartidos por todo el territorio.

Rechaza con nosotras su presente: imaginemos nuestro futuro.

author: dialogocomospovos
title: A palavra semente nunca morre
content:
Durante o intercâmbio no Assentamento Terra Vista, a conversa com Mestre Isaac revelou um profundo conhecimento sobre os ciclos da natureza e o manejo da terra. Ele explicou que a lua orienta todo o plantio: na lua crescente, tudo o que se planta cresce; na minguante, o que se planta é guardado, dá pouco, mas o pouco serve para guardar semente. A lua nova, por sua vez, significa força — é o momento de plantar raízes como mandioca, cacau, laranja e café, pois são bens de raiz.


Isaac ensinou que a mandioca, na lua nova, deve ser picada e deixada na sombra para secar o leite antes de ir à terra, senão a terra puxa o leite e ela não carrega; na lua crescente, três guias após a nova, planta-se e ela cresce comprida, sem curvas. Ele destacou a importância de se aliar à natureza: na horta, não bate veneno, e para controlar lagartas usa casca de ovo em gravetos, pois a lagarta se identifica como ovo e não bota mais no local.


Também falou da diversidade: plantar quatro ou cinco qualidades de feijão juntas faz uma carregar mais que a outra, quebra a praga e enriquece o alimento. É preciso ter variedades, capim santo, cidreira, erva-doce, tudo que existe. Por fim, Isaac refletiu que semear é semear semente e conhecimentos: “vocês vieram de lá para cá com esse objetivo, e nós passamos os nossos daqui para lá. A palavra semente nunca morre.”

author: Unknown
title: Women call for closure of Silopi Thermal Power Plant
content:
The Free Women’s Movement (TJA) held a press conference about the Silopi Thermal Power Plant, owned by the Ciner Group and located between the towns of Bêspin and Gite in the Silopi (Silopya) district of Şirnak (Şirnex). The statement, attended by numerous women and representatives of democratic organisations, drew attention to the plant’s effects on the environment and public health.


Reading the statement, Dilan Elçi, co-chair of the Şirnak branch of the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD), said that the right to clean air, water and soil was being violated by coal mining activities on Mount Cudi and the thermal power plant. Stating that the exploitation of nature and the oppression of women stem from the same patriarchal and capitalist mindset, Dilan Elçi said environmental destruction directly affects women’s livelihoods, economies and social lives as well.


Dilan Elçi stated that sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, dust and heavy metals emitted from the plant’s chimney pose a danger to human health and other living beings. She called for the plant’s impacts to be investigated through independent scientific research and for the findings to be made public.


Emphasising that peace with nature is also a fundamental issue within the framework of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, Dilan Elçi called for coal mining activities on Mount Cudi to be halted and for the Silopi Thermal Power Plant to be shut down completely.


The statement concluded with chants of “Bê xezayê jiyan nabê” (“There can be no life without nature”) and “Jin, jiyan, azadî” (“Woman, life, freedom”), followed by a sit-in protest.

author: Barracuda Media
title: Cartel e trabalho escravo: as acusações contra a Cutrale que o Deutsche Bank ignorou
content:
Vazamento mostra escândalos de um dos maiores bancos do mundo. A

 Pública

 é o único parceiro no Brasil. Leia o especial

Inside Deutsche Bank


aqui.


Vazamento mostra escândalos de um dos maiores bancos do mundo. A

 Pública

 é o único parceiro no Brasil. Leia o especial

Inside Deutsche Bank


aqui.


Quando o bilionário José Luís Cutrale faleceu em 2022, não faltaram obituários e reportagens elogiosas ao empresário. Dono de uma das maiores empresas do agronegócio brasileiro, a Cutrale, ele foi descrito como “

rei da laranja

” e exaltado como a “

primeira estrela global do agro brasileiro

”. Para seus herdeiros, José Luís deixou uma fortuna pessoal estimada em quase 2 bilhões de dólares e uma companhia responsável pela produção de algo entre um quarto e um terço do suco de laranja consumido no planeta.


Mas, além dos números impressionantes, Cutrale e sua companhia homônima também acumularam acusações trabalhistas ao longo das últimas décadas – inclusive de trabalho análogo à escravidão – e foram o alvo central de processos

judiciais

 e

administrativos

 pela suposta formação de cartel, dentro e fora do Brasil.


Relatórios internos sigilosos e trocas de e-mails do Deutsche Bank (DB) acessados pela

Agência Pública

, no entanto, mostram que as suspeitas contra a empresa de suco de laranja e seu dono foram repetidamente amenizadas por funcionários do banco alemão

 – um padrão de comportamento que se repetiu com outros clientes brasileiros de peso implicados em casos polêmicos ou até mesmo acusados de crimes.


Um calhamaço em alemão de 1.148 páginas é o elemento central da história. O relatório de “Conheça Seu Cliente” (Know Your Costumer, ou KYC, na sigla em inglês) sobre a família Cutrale, suas empresas e suas ligações revela que o banco alemão tinha conhecimento dos problemas e polêmicas ligadas ao magnata do suco de laranja, mas que optou por diminuir sua relevância, preferindo destacar que Cutrale “goza de reputação internacional impecável” e seu suco de laranja é “consumido no mundo todo”.


Relatório do Deutsche Bank lista empresas ligadas à família Cutrale que eram clientes do banco


O material é parte do

Inside Deutsche Bank

, investigação transnacional da qual a

Pública

 faz parte, baseada no vazamento de mais de 15 milhões de documentos do banco, obtido pelo jornalista indiano Josy Joseph e por Khadija Sharife, jornalista investigativa sul-africana. O projeto tem coordenação global da Barracuda Media e do Centro Lationamericano de Periodismo de Investigación (CLIP) na região.


Os documentos vazados para o projeto mostram,

segundo detalhado em diversas reportagens

, como o banco alemão repetidamente ignorou sinais de alerta de possível lavagem de dinheiro e violações de sanções e como descumpriu suas próprias regras para clientes poderosos.


Em resposta aos assuntos levantados pelo projeto Inside Deutsche Bank, o banco afirmou que as questões apresentadas pelos jornalistas “remontam a muitos anos atrás, em alguns casos, décadas. Quando pertinente, essas questões foram analisadas na época e discutidas com órgãos reguladores e autoridades competentes, conforme necessário”, afirmou o banco.


“Hoje somos um banco diferente”, acrescentou a instituição.


Além da Cutrale, documentos internos mencionando empresas como BRF e JBS, Vale,

Banco Safra

, Andrade Gutierrez e Braskem revelam, em diferentes graus, as prioridades do DB e de seus funcionários – mesmo quando as evidências pediam precaução.


A primeira

reportagem

 da série detalhou uma grande controvérsia em torno do BTG Pactual de André Esteves, com quem o chefe de Commodities do Deutsche Bank se recusou a fazer negócios, chamando-o de “pilantra”. Outros executivos defenderam a relação com o banco, dizendo ser um dos principais clientes do DB no Brasil.


Suco de laranja


A versão do relatório disponível no vazamento é datada de 2018, mas outros documentos internos do Deutsche Bank citam revisões em relatório de KYC sobre a Cutrale pelo menos desde 2015. Esse tipo de relatório costuma ser produzido sempre que um novo cliente vai ser adotado pelo banco – o que ocorreu, no caso da citricultora, em pelo menos 2021. Assim é possível que a instituição já soubesse dos problemas vinculados à empresa desde muito antes.


As mesmas justificativas utilizadas para minimizar os problemas aparecem em outros documentos ao longo dos anos anteriores ao KYC.

author: CNT Santander
title: 20N: Manifestación Antifascista
content:
Este viernes 20, a las 19:30h en la Plaza Porticada en Santander, tenemos una cita muy importante en las calles con diferentes colectivos, sindicatos, partidos y asociaciones, para dejar claro que no queremos fascistas en nuestros barrios.


Para gritar alto:

¡Ni juventud para el odio, ni futuro para el fascismo!


Nos hacemos eco del Manifiesto de la Asamblea Antifascista, creado por diferentes colectivos, con un mismo sentir y objetivo común: derrotar al fascismo.


«Europa arde. Es el momento para que el estado español lo haga también. El hartazgo de la clase trabajadora, la población estudiantil, las personas pensionistas, las mujeres, las personas racializadas y las disidencias, se ha pronunciado bien alto en todas las plazas del país, han dicho: ¡basta ya! a este sistema que cada día nos subyuga más.


Nunca hemos creído en su modelo capitalista neoliberal de consumismo desenfrenado impuesto por las élites y los grandes empresarios, ni en su individualismo y competitividad constante para que nos enfrentemos entre nosotras, que nos desgasta, desangra y nos conduce a una vida de miseria y precariedad laboral.


En su delirio por seguir aumentando sus crasas ganancias nos arrastran a una vida de explotación donde el esfuerzo diario nos lleva a vender nuestro trabajo por salarios que ya no dan ni para la básica subsistencia, donde apenas nos queda tiempo libre para vivir y respirar.

Los sueldos no llegan ni para tener un hogar digno porque se lo venden a fondos buitre que nos expulsan de nuestros barrios, están desmantelando todos nuestros servicios públicos y juegan con nuestro dinero destinándolo a seguir financiando las guerras salvajes basadas en el imperialismo, el colonialismo y los genocidios más atroces.


Nos están robando, cada día un poco más, todos los derechos laborales, económicos y culturales, que fueron adquiridos a través de décadas de dura y sangrienta lucha obrera.


El sacrificio de nuestras antepasadas debe servir para prender la mecha de este inconformismo que nos hierve en la sangre y de una valentía sin cadenas que nos aten, porque la batalla será ardua. Nos encontramos en un punto de

«no retorno»

 con el auge del fascismo y la fuerza represiva desbordada de los perros del estado.


Porque como decía Olmo en ‘Novecento’:

«Los fascistas no son como los hongos, que nacen así en una noche, no. Han sido los patronos los que han plantado los fascistas, los han querido, les han pagado. Y con los fascistas, los patronos han ganado cada vez más, hasta no saber dónde meter el dinero. Y así inventaron la guerra… Pero siempre pagamos nosotros. ¿Quién paga? El proletariado, los campesinos, los obreros, los pobres»

.


La clase trabajadora ya no enviará a sus hijas e hijos a ninguna guerra.


La libertad nunca fue fácil de conquistar, ahora somos más fuertes, más inteligentes y conocemos cómo acaba la historia si no les hacemos frente estando unidas.


Debemos plantar cara, sin miedo, aunque su fuerza represiva actúe con una violencia descarnada y sin escrúpulos, sobre la clase trabajadora y todas aquellas personas que deciden alzar la voz para pelear por su derecho a una vida digna. En Cantabria, sabemos muy bien lo que sucede cuando esa fuerza se desborda, en nuestra memoria siempre estará Gonzalo Ruiz, obrero campurriano asesinado en Reinosa por la Guardia Civil en la primavera del 87.


Debemos enfrentarnos a ellos, destruir el beneplácito con el que se postran ante el avance de la extrema derecha y el fascismo, permitiendo las expresiones de odio y la violencia contra aquellas personas que piensan diferente, que viven y sienten alejados de la hegemonía heterobásica y tradicional instaurada en su sistema.


Porque siempre vivimos en los márgenes de su mal llamada

«democracia»

, en un estado que olvida la historia acontecida y que no permite desenterrar la memoria histórica, que no frena la apología de un fascismo, ahora heredado, que llenó todo el territorio español de huesos en las cunetas.


Es hora de avanzar hacia el centro, de tomar las calles, de arder en rabia controlada y lucha colectiva para destruir todos sus pilares, porque como dijo Durruti:

«Al fascismo no se le combate, se le destruye»

, y el fascismo no es más que una de las fuerzas empleadas por el sistema capitalista para dividir a la población, para mostrar su racismo y su odio, para convertir en culpables de las crisis económicas a las personas migrantes, a las feministas, a las personas del colectivo LGTBIQ+ y aquellas …

author: Josiah David Quising
title: Legality of burning effigies
content:
Throughout history, the burning of effigies was never shown to be with intent to injure another, but rather consistently presented as a form of expression and indignation.

Filipinos using effigies to depict resistance and protest is said to have originated from the higantes of Angono, Rizal as a way to mock abusive hacenderos in the late Spanish colonial period. Decades later, Filipino activists have kept the tradition alive across multiple administrations, but not without opposition. The Philippine National Police (PNP) often releases warnings against burning effigies ahead of protests, claiming that burning protest materials would violate either the Republic Act No. 8749 (Clean Air Act) or Batas Pambansa No. 880 (Public Assembly Act). Just yesterday, Cebu activists were accused by the local police of violating the law when they set an effigy on fire.

But does burning effigies really violate the law? The PNP has cited Section 20 of the Philippine Clean Air Act which bans incineration of “municipal, biomedical, and hazardous waste” as the basis of their warning, stating that burning effigies would pollute the air.

A plain reading of the law would show that the ban on incineration does not prohibit all types of burning but instead specifically prohibits the burning of “waste”. While the Clean Air Act itself does not define “waste”, Section 3(kk) of R.A. 9003 or the Solid Waste Management Act defines “solid waste” as “all discarded household, commercial waste, non-hazardous institutional and industrial waste, street sweepings, construction debris, agricultural waste, and other non-hazardous/non-toxic solid waste.”

By plain definition, effigies cannot be categorized as “waste” as they are not “discarded” materials but rather art forms created for a specific purpose. The Supreme Court clarified this in MMDA v. Jancom (2002) where it held that Section 20 of the Philippine Clean Air Act does not absolutely prohibit incineration. It prohibits only burning processes involving municipal, biomedical, or hazardous wastes that emit poisonous and toxic fumes. This means that even in the absurd scenario where effigies are considered as “waste” materials, burning of the same would still not be considered a violation of the Philippine Clean Air Act.

“Poisonous and toxic fumes” are defined by Section 5(t) of the Clean Air Act as “any emissions and fumes which are beyond internationally-accepted standards, including but not limited to the World Health Organization (WHO) guideline values.”

This shows that without proof that the burning of effigies during protests would result in emissions of fumes “beyond internationally-accepted standards,” burning of effigies does not automatically violate the Philippine Clean Air Act.

Another law commonly cited by the PNP is Section 13(g)(3) of the Public Assembly Act which prohibits the “malicious burning of any object in the streets or thoroughfares”. The Supreme Court in Villareal v. People (2012) has defined “malice” or “malicious” as the deliberate, wrongful, or evil intent to injure another, or an act done with criminal indifference to another’s rights and without legal justification.

In other words, the intent or reason for the burning matters. Throughout history, the burning of effigies was never shown to be with intent to injure another, but rather consistently presented as a form of expression and indignation.

Ultimately, no law directly prohibits the burning of effigies. The PNP should stop distracting everyone from the issues brought to light by setting fire to art. At the end of the day, the government should address the message itself rather than fixate on how it was delivered – perhaps then we can return to calmly submitting position papers. (DAA)

He teaches Public International Law, Legal Research, and Thesis at the Far Eastern University Institute of Law, where he also advises the Far Eastern Law Review. His lawyering work centers on labor rights, environmental justice, and the protection of human rights defenders. author: Unknown
title: John Nyström - Ett ve!
content:
Författare

: John Nyström

Titel

: Ett ve!

Källa

: Allarm november 1916


 Du mördarliga i Saltsjöstaden;

 Vi glömma aldrig den hemska dagen,

 Då du vår sångarvän lät mörda -

 Men som du sår får du också skörda.


 Ett hat, ett ve ha vi alla svurit,

 Ty Hillströms hjärta har du sönderskurit

 Och detta hat rört upp en stark orkan,

 Som snart skall nedslå uti Saltsjösta'n.


 Rebellens liv det var en väldig gnista

 Som modet tände intill det sista.

 Ja, in i döden ljöd hans maningsord:

 "Kom, tag tillbaka, slav, din stulna jord."


 En man, som Hillström, ej finnes många,

 Därföre skulle du honom fånga.

 Och bjuda gengälden en säker död.

 Du, världens avskum, du överflöd!


 I tvänne år låg han där inburad

 Bak grå och dödstysta fängselmurar.

 Han gick till döden som till dukat bord,

 Men glöm ej, mördare, hans sista ord!


 Ett tack du kämpe, för vad du stridit,

 För vad du plågats och för vad du lidit.

 Så sant vi lever skall vi hatet så

 Och fler och fler skall i ledet stå.

author: Unknown
title: Walfrid Engdahl - Joe Hill
content:
Författare

: Walfrid Engdahl

Titel

: Joe Hill

Källa

: Allarm november 1916


 Hans sånger leva, men han är död. Varför skola vi nu igen gräva upp honom för dyrkan och kanonisering? Varför skall han prisas? Därför att han var en man! Kunde han hjälpa att han var det? Borde inte alla revolutionärer vara män?


 Sannerligen han var bätter än vi. I ett av sina sista brev till en kamrat skrev han något liknande:


 "Slösa ej tid över mitt minne - organisera."


 Det var manliga ord, värda att minnas av envar.


 Han skrev sånger, låt oss sjunga dem. De väcka slavarna mer än artiklarna om den döde och de döda gör.


 Skall en människa prisas därför att hon skrivit sånger, eller skrivit vad som helst? Kunde han undgå att skriva dem? Han kunde det lika litet som näktergalen kan undgå sjunga vackra sånger i härliga aftnar och länder som äro gynnade av hans närvaro.


 Vi tyckte alla om Josef Hillström och vi talade och skrev därom för ett år sedan. Vår tid är kanske för dyrbar för att offra den på döda ben, nära och hur kära de voro oss.


 Det är väl knappast en dygd att vara revolutionär. Det är snarare den vakne arbetarens självskrivna plikt. Det är vårt intresse att vara det och ingen som helst moralisk känsla. Att hans liv var en strid, som slutade så tragiskt, det hembar han njutning av själv medan han levde. Ty striden ger en njutning. På själva avrättningsplatsen stod han ännu som den betvingade segraren: han darrade ej så mycket som de, vilka sköto honom.


 Han var segrare över alla känslor, stod över mängden, och han kände det. Hans arbete levde efter honom. Han dog i rätta ögonblicket, aktad, ärad, avhållen av alla, utom de svarta mördarna. Han var rörelsen och rörelsen var han, liksom han var en del i universum, avskild genom sin individuella kropp och dock ett med det hela. Den skarpsynte revolutionären vet, att hans avrättning är ett tecken på organisationens livskraft och så går han beslutsamt in i dödens omfamning i förvissningen därom.


 Joe Hill hade njutning nog, ty det finnes ingen njutning så stor som känslan av en manlig gärning.


 Vi bli sjuka om någon vågar kritisera medlemmarna i vår organisation. Varför skola vi då ej vara rättrådiga nog att ta bort även berömmet. Är det ena klandervärt borde det andra vara det också, utan att meningen med en rörelse och dess organ är ett inbördes beundra och smickra varann.


 Min enskilda mening är, att det är nödvändigare för oss att kritisera och få fram våra fel och våra bristfälligheter än det är att få fram våra fördelar. Våra gärningar och vårt uppträdande återspelgar allt. De stora handlingarna tala alltid väl om oss, i sig själva, men det är de låga handlingarnas sätt att tala på sitt vis också. Den värdefullaste kritik en rörelse får är från dess egna medlemmar och den oskattbaraste kritiken individen mottager är från sin bästa vän. Endast en sådan medlem - endast en sådan vän är värd att äga.


 Jag vill ej följa med på smickrets dyiga väg. På höjderna där de stora och mäktiga stormarna gå fram, där den eviga spänningen är, där är revolutionärens givna plats.


 Vad är berömmet värt? Ännu aldrig fanns en människa som vann det minsta grand därpå. Jag har sett människor som ständigt erhållit smicker och beröm, och hurdana ha de blivit! Äckliga, vämjeliga, självförnöjda stackare. Fy fan! Å andra sidan har jag sett dem, som dag ut och dag in utstått kaskader af klander och kritik och de ha varit män: djärva, dådlystna, energiska, viljestarka - djävliga.


 Låt oss inte skända de dödas gravar med årliga kanoniseringar. Vi bör inte tänka om vad vi tänkte i fjol, utan tänka något nytt. Ha vi inte handlingar nu att tänka på mångfaldiga gånger mera aktuella än en kamrats avrättning? I gruvor, på banor och fält avrättas oupphörliga människor med samma varma blod och känslor. Bör vi inte tänka på dem?


 Ha vi inte militärvansinnet att bekämpa och tala och skriva om? Står ej ännu privatkapitalismen utmanande blodtörstig och stark?


 Vi kan göra mycket mot dessa drakar. Joe Hill kunde ej göra mer än vi, än hans dikter göra i dag. Utrustade med dem äro vi lika starka, lika väckande som han. De voro ej hans mer än de äro våra. title: Διεθνείς ημέρες δράσης ενάντια στον πόλεμο και τον μιλιταρισμό 20-22/11
content:
FIGHT FOR OUR FUTURE, NOT THEIR WARS!


20 Νοέμβρη 2026: πανευρωπαϊκή φοιτητική απεργία ενάντια στη στρατιωτικοποίηση.


20-22 Νοέμβρη: διεθνείς ημέρες δράσης ενάντια στον μιλιταρισμό και τον πόλεμο.


Από τις 20 ως τις 22 Νοεμβρίου 2026 διοργανώνονται συντονισμένες αντιμιλιταριστικές διαμαρτυρίες και πορείες σε περισσότερες από 20 ευρωπαϊκές χώρες.


Η αρχική πρωτοβουλία προήλθε από τη

Διεθνή Απεργία Νεολαίας

 (

International Youth Strike

 – “Fight for Our Future, Not Their Wars” = «Στη Μάχη για το Μέλλον μας, Όχι για τους Πολέμους τους») και σύντομα υιοθετήθηκε από τον συνασπισμό

Stop ReArm Europe

 (

Stop ReArm Europe

 coalition – “Welfare, not Warfare”).


Δημοσιεύουμε το αρχικό κάλεσμα του International Youth Strike:


ΣΤΗ ΜΑΧΗ ΓΙΑ ΤΟ ΜΕΛΛΟΝ ΜΑΣ, ΟΧΙ ΓΙΑ ΤΟΥΣ ΠΟΛΕΜΟΥΣ ΤΟΥΣ!


Ο κόσμος φλέγεται


Ο κόσμος στον οποίο μεγαλώνουμε διαμορφώνεται από ένα σύστημα που αδιαφορεί για τις ανάγκες των ανθρώπων. Η εκμετάλλευση των εργαζομένων, η κλιματική αλλαγή και ο πόλεμος δεν είναι αστοχίες του συστήματος, αλλά η ουσία του καπιταλισμού. Η αύξηση της στρατιωτικοποίησης, ο αυταρχισμός και η διάλυση του κράτους πρόνοιας δεν είναι ξεχωριστά προβλήματα, αλλά συναποτελούν συμπτώματα της κρίσης του παγκόσμιου καπιταλισμού.


Οι στρατιωτικές δαπάνες φτάνουν σε ιστορικά υψηλά, ενώ η εκπαίδευση, η υγειονομική περίθαλψη, η στέγαση και οι δημόσιες υπηρεσίες θυσιάζονται για τη χρηματοδότηση των επανεξοπλισμών. Προγράμματα όπως το ReArm Europe (το οποίο στοχεύει να επενδύσει 800 δισεκατομμύρια ευρώ), η επέκταση στρατιωτικών συμμαχιών όπως το ΝΑΤΟ και οι αυξανόμενες εκκλήσεις για υποχρεωτική στρατιωτική θητεία προετοιμάζουν τη γενιά μας για πόλεμο αντί να εγγυώνται το μέλλον μας. Το ΝΑΤΟ δεν υπερασπίζεται την ειρήνη. Έχει επανειλημμένα προωθήσει τα ιμπεριαλιστικά συμφέροντα μέσω στρατιωτικών επεμβάσεων, κλιμάκωσης και προστασίας της γεωπολιτικής και οικονομικής ισχύος – και γι’ αυτό πρέπει να διαλυθεί.


Ο δυτικός ιμπεριαλισμός, με επικεφαλής την κυβέρνηση Τραμπ στις ΗΠΑ, επιβάλλει σχέδια επανεξοπλισμών που επικροτούνται φανατικά από την ευρωπαϊκή άρχουσα τάξη και υποστηρίζονται από συντηρητικές και ακροδεξιές κυβερνήσεις στην Ευρώπη και σε όλο τον κόσμο.


Αλλά δεν υποστηρίζονται μόνο από αντιδραστικές πολιτικές δυνάμεις. Η δίνη του μιλιταρισμού έχει επίσης συναντήσει ενθουσιώδη υποστήριξη από διάφορες σοσιαλδημοκρατικές κυβερνήσεις που έχουν εγκρίνει στρατιωτικούς προϋπολογισμούς ρεκόρ.


Από την Παλαιστίνη μέχρι το Σουδάν, από τον Λίβανο μέχρι το Ιράν, από τη Βενεζουέλα μέχρι την Κούβα, λαοί σε όλο τον κόσμο συνεχίζουν να υποφέρουν από ιμπεριαλιστικές επιθέσεις – κατοχές, στρατιωτικές επεμβάσεις, κυρώσεις, αποικιακή κυριαρχία και γενοκτονία που διαπράττονται στο όνομα γεωπολιτικών και οικονομικών συμφερόντων.


 

Η νεολαία και η εργατική τάξη πληρώνουν το τίμημα


Είμαστε οι άνθρωποι που θα αναγκαστούν να πεθάνουν και να σκοτώσουν στους πολέμους τους για τα συμφέροντά τους. Η στρατιωτικοποίηση εισέρχεται στα σχολεία και τα πανεπιστήμιά μας μέσω της εργασίας για τον στρατό και της στρατολόγησης, μέσω ερευνών που χρηματοδοτούνται από βιομηχανίες όπλων και συνεργασιών με ιδρύματα που συνεργάζονται σε πολέμους και γενοκτονίες. Η στρατιωτικοποίηση κανονικοποιεί τη βία, ενισχύει τις πατριαρχικές δομές και ενδυναμώνει την ακροδεξιά, ενώ οι κυβερνήσεις επιμένουν ότι δεν υπάρχει εναλλακτική και μας πουλάνε ως δικαιολογία το παραμύθι της «άμυνας». Αλλά ξέρουμε καλά ότι ο επανεξοπλισμός δεν αποτρέπει, αλλά αντιθέτως κλιμακώνει τις συγκρούσεις.


Απορρίπτουμε αυτό το μέλλον.


Αγωνιζόμαστε για εκπαίδευση απαλλαγμένη από στρατιωτικά συμφέροντα. Αγωνιζόμαστε για την κατάργηση τόσο της εθελοντικής όσο και της υποχρεωτικής στρατιωτικής θητείας.


Αγωνιζόμαστε για δημόσιες επενδύσεις σε σχολεία, υγειονομική περίθαλψη, στέγαση και κλιματική δικαιοσύνη αντί για όπλα και πόλεμο. Αγωνιζόμαστε για μια γρήγορη και δίκαιη [οικολογική] μετάβαση πέρα από τα ορυκτά καύσιμα, με γνώμονα τις ανάγκες των εργαζομένων, όπου καμία, κανείς, κανένα δεν θα μείνει πίσω· για διεθνή αλληλεγγύη αντί για ιμπεριαλιστική κυριαρχία, και για το δικαίωμα κάθε λαού να καθορίζει το μέλλον του απαλλαγμένο από την κατοχή και την αποικιοκρατία.


Ο αγώνας κατά της στρατιωτικοποίησης είναι άρρηκτα συνδεδεμένος με τον αγώνα κατά του οικονομικού συστήματος που τη συντηρεί. title: Families of seriously ill prisoners launch vigil in Ankara
content:
Families of seriously ill political prisoners began an indefinite sit-in outside the Turkish Ministry of Justice in Ankara on Tuesday. Together with members of parliament from the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) and human rights organizations, they are demanding the release of ill prisoners and access to adequate medical treatment. The participants announced that they would continue their protest until concrete steps are taken.


The vigil was organized at the call of DEM Party MPs, the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD), and the Human Rights Association (IHD). Among the participants are relatives of Newroz Bozkurt, who was transferred from Sincan Women’s Prison to Etlik City Hospital, and Evin Zapsu, who is imprisoned in Kayseri Bünyan Women’s Prison with stage four cancer.


The demonstrators unfurled a banner bearing the names of seriously ill prisoners and the words: “We stand at the gates of justice. Through resistance, we will open the prison gates – Freedom for sick prisoners.” Slogans demanding the release of political prisoners were repeatedly chanted.


“People must no longer die in prisons”


Şirin Altay, the Ankara representative of the Federation of Solidarity Associations for Prisoners’ Families (TUHAD-FED), stated that the situation of seriously ill prisoners had not changed despite numerous protests and public appeals outside the Ministry of Justice. For this reason, the families have decided to launch an indefinite protest, Altay said and called on the authorities to facilitate the immediate release of prisoners and thereby strengthen public confidence in the ongoing peace process.


“People must no longer die in prisons. They must be able to receive medical treatment under appropriate conditions. The Ministry of Justice must hear our voices,” Altay said. She questioned the authorities’ responsibility for the deaths of political prisoners and demanded an answer as to how a peace process could move forward while people continued to die in detention. She stressed that the families would remain outside the ministry to fight for the lives of their loved ones.


“We cannot bear any more news of deaths”


DEM Party MP Ali Bozan recalled political prisoner Tuncer Sağlam, who recently died. He remarked that the continued refusal to release prisoners and provide adequate medical care was not only a human rights issue but also placed a burden on the social peace process. “We cannot bear any more news of deaths from prisons,” Bozan stated. Pointing out that the public was right to question how peace could be discussed while seriously ill people continued to be held in prison, he stated: "The vigil is therefore also intended to contribute to the peace process by drawing attention to the urgently needed humanitarian measures. Where rights violations continue indefinitely, protests will also continue indefinitely."


Mother of Newroz Bozkurt demands treatment outside prison


Sultan Bozkurt gave a particularly moving account of her daughter Newroz’s situation. She said her daughter had been seriously ill for a year. "Although she is now in hospital, she remains under prison conditions. When this process began two years ago, we hoped that we might be able to embrace our children again in good health,” she stated.


Sultan Bozkurt said she had traveled from Istanbul to Ankara and had been allowed to see her daughter for only ten minutes over the course of two days. "My daughter's health has deteriorated significantly. She is in a terrible condition. Her blood levels have dropped to zero,” Bozkurt said. She demanded that her daughter be transferred to a regular hospital ward and receive treatment under appropriate conditions.


She emphasized that no new law was needed to ensure medical care and the release of seriously ill prisoners. "Those affected must be given the opportunity to continue their treatment outside prison and in a family environment. We said that mothers would no longer have to cry when there is peace. We will do everything in our power to ensure that mothers no longer cry. Tears have no color. Now, concrete steps must finally be taken.”


Evin Zapsu can barely manage her daily life


Mecit Zapsu, the husband of seriously ill prisoner Evin Zapsu, also appealed to the Ministry of Justice. He criticized the apparent treatment of medical care for prisoners as a concession, even though it was a fundamental right. He said his wife is suffering from stage four cancer in …

title: Numerous politicians detained in operation against Kurdish party alliance Hevbendî in Turkey
content:
Numerous Kurdish politicians have been detained in Turkey as part of a large-scale operation targeting the newly formed party alliance Hevbendî. Among those detained is Bayram Bozyel, chairman of the Socialist Party of Kurdistan (PSK). The public prosecutor’s office in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır) accuses members of the alliance of endangering the unity of the state and Turkey’s territorial integrity. According to Hevbendî, the investigation covers all 51 members of the alliance’s council.


Hevbendî was founded on November 7 in Amed as the “National Alliance of Kurdistan.” Its members include the PSK, the Kurdistan Democratic Party/North (PDK-Bakur), the Patriotic Party of Kurdistan (PWK), Pêlkurd, Vejîn, and the Kurdistan National Initiative. The alliance aims to strengthen cooperation among Kurdish parties and political movements.


House raids in five cities


Police raided homes in Amed, Ankara, Mardin, Batman, and Istanbul in the early hours of November 17. According to Hevbendî, those detained included Bayram Bozyel, PSK deputy chairman and lawyer Hasan Dağtekin, Pêlkurd spokesperson Fuat Önen, PWK deputy chairman Mehmet Can Azbay, as well as Sevgi Çelik, Aryan Serhed, Ali Öncü, Rojbin Bükün, Ali Çeven, and Ali Aydın.


The home of PWK chairman Mustafa Özçelik was also raided and searched. According to the alliance, an arrest warrant has also been issued for him. Those targeted are accused under Article 302 of the Turkish Penal Code of “disrupting the unity of the state and the territorial integrity of the country.” The offense carries a sentence of aggravated life imprisonment. According to the alliance, the investigation files have been placed under a confidentiality order, and those detained have been denied access to their lawyers for 24 hours.


PSK: “This repression will not intimidate us”


The PSK condemned the detentions and announced that it would continue its political activities. “These and similar repressive measures, as well as the detention of our officials, will not intimidate us. We will continue to struggle alongside all patriotic forces until the Kurdish people achieve their national and democratic rights,” the party stated. It also called on democratic organizations and the public to oppose the measures and show solidarity with Hevbendî. “We will not be intimidated and will continue to stand up for Hevbendî.”


Solidarity appeal criticizes criminalization of peaceful political activity


In a joint appeal titled “Shoulder to Shoulder: Solidarity with the Hevbendî Detainees,” intellectuals, writers, academics, and artists condemned the operation. They pointed out that the accusations concerned a political conference, a joint program, and a press conference, none of which had involved acts of violence or calls for violence.


The signatories described the detentions as a violation of freedom of expression and association under the Turkish Constitution and the European Convention on Human Rights. They also referred to the case law of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR), according to which peaceful advocacy for the right to self-determination was not in itself a criminal offense.


‘Those who expected division have strengthened unity’


The signatories stated that the repression had fostered solidarity among different Kurdish political movements, some of which had previously had significant differences. “The national unity that the Kurdish people were unable to achieve through their own efforts over the years has now emerged on its own as a result of a single arrest warrant. People of different views and traditions who long kept their distance from one another are now signing the same declaration.”


They emphasized, however, that their previous objections to the establishment, working methods, and structures of Hevbendî remained unchanged. In light of the detentions, however, solidarity with those affected took precedence. “We will conduct our discussions on procedural matters among ourselves and on our own terms, just as a family discusses its affairs within the family. We will not allow these debates to become material for prosecutors’ investigation files or indictments.”


Alliance for national rights and political self-determination


Hevbendî emerged from a prolonged process of political rapprochement. The starting point was a conference on Kurdistan’s national unity held in Amed on March 14, 2026. At another conference on November 7, a joint program was adopted, before the alliance …

title: Ecuadorian Fishermen Sue US Over Boat Strike, Alleged Subsequent Torture
content:
The fishermen’s boat was targeted despite being cleared of wrongdoing, the lawsuit points out.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

A group of Ecuadorian fishermen who say their boat was targeted in a drone strike by the Trump administration earlier this year is suing the U.S. government.

The group had previously announced their intention to sue the administration, and formally filed their lawsuit on Monday.

While the U.S. has acknowledged several boat strikes on the South American coasts (ostensibly targeting so-called “narcoterrorists”), the administration has not claimed responsibility for this specific attack. However, a report in August suggested that several vessels, including this one, were targets of a secret CIA mission.

All fishermen aboard the boat survived the strike, but many reported experiencing serious injuries. They faced additional injuries after the strike, both physical and legal, they said.

According to the federal lawsuit, filed in the Western District of Pennsylvania, the men were “kidnapped” and held “against their will” for about a day by U.S. officials, then sent to a detention center in El Salvador for several additional days.

“While in U.S. custody and control, these fishermen were treated by the U.S. in cruel and inhumane ways amounting to torture,” the lawsuit states, noting that the White House “has not conducted these strikes pursuant to any congressional authorization.”

“These premeditated and intentional attacks against defenseless people lack any plausible legal justification,” the suit adds.

Crew members of the La Negra Francisca Duarte II, the boat named in the lawsuit as the one that was attacked, are demanding $5 million to pay for damages, as well as any additional relief as determined by the court. They are also asking that the administration be barred from launching similar attacks in the future.

The fishermen point out that their boat was targeted despite evidence demonstrating they had nothing to do with “narcoterrorism,” as the Ecuadorian Navy had inspected the vessel just before the attack occurred, determining no wrongdoing or presence of narcotics.

“Even if that weren’t the case … the US has no right to be bombing boats in the Caribbean and the Pacific on the claim the people are narco-traffickers,” said Dan Kovalik, the U.S.-based attorney representing the crew. “If they believe someone is a narco-trafficker, they need to go get a warrant for their arrest.”

The lawsuit was filed just days after an effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth was introduced and voted on in the House of Representatives. One of the eight articles of impeachment that Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Kentucky) brought forward charged Hegseth with “unauthorized lethal military targeting” of boats near South America that has resulted “in at least 243 deaths.”

That impeachment vote failed to advance after several Democratic lawmakers neglected to appear in time to vote alongside their conference and Massie.

title: PKK prisoners: Seriously ill prisoners must be released immediately
content:
Political prisoners convicted in PKK-related trials expressed their support for the indefinite vigil outside the Turkish Ministry of Justice in Ankara. The protest was launched on Tuesday by relatives of seriously ill political prisoners, who are demanding their immediate release and adequate medical care outside prison. In a statement issued by Deniz Kaya on behalf of the prisoners, the situation in prisons is described as one of the crucial tests for the Peace and Democratic Society Process.


“We demand the immediate and unconditional release of all prisoners, particularly those who are seriously ill,” the statement said. The prisoners stressed that the continued exposure of political prisoners to life-threatening illnesses, denial of medical care, and violations of their right to life was incompatible with the pursuit of a democratic solution. “Peace cannot be achieved through political declarations alone but must be reflected in respect for human dignity, the protection of life, and the removal of restrictions on freedom,” they said.


Serious illnesses and denied releases


The prisoners criticized the continued human rights violations, isolation measures, and life-threatening prison conditions despite the ongoing peace process. They called on the state to abandon its policy of delaying action and take concrete, confidence-building steps toward democratization. According to the statement, hundreds of seriously ill prisoners remain behind bars despite severe health problems. Medical treatment is being obstructed, while releases are being denied for political or arbitrary reasons.


The statement cited several recent cases as examples: Tuncer Sağlam died without receiving the necessary medical treatment. Newroz Bozkurt, who has leukemia, is fighting for her life in an intensive care unit. Political prisoner Evin Zapsu has been diagnosed with stage four cancer. “Human life and the right to health must never be subordinated to political, administrative, or security considerations. Medical care and freedom are not privileges but fundamental human rights. Likewise, people who have already served their prison sentences must not continue to be detained on the basis of arbitrary decisions. The practice of forcing prisoners to express remorse, the isolation of political prisoners, and the systematic delay of releases must also come to an end. Without such changes, there can be no genuine progress toward social peace,” the prisoners emphasized.


Call for support for the vigil


The prisoners welcomed the indefinite vigil launched in Ankara and called on women, young people, workers, democratic organizations, and human rights initiatives to show solidarity with the protesting relatives. “What happens in prisons is not merely a problem for prisoners and their families. It is a shared responsibility of all those who seek justice, freedom, and a democratic society,” the statement noted. It stressed that action must be taken before more prisoners lose their lives as a result of being denied medical treatment.


The prisoners called on the Turkish government to stop delaying the necessary steps in the peace process: “Seriously ill prisoners must be released unconditionally, their medical treatment must be ensured, and prisoners who have served their sentences must be released immediately. End the unlawful practices in prisons and remove, without exception, all obstacles to the freedom of prisoners,” they demanded.


The prisoners also pledged to continue supporting the vigil and the struggle of the prisoners’ relatives: “We will not remain silent in the face of violations of our comrades’ right to life and freedom.”

author: Unknown
title: Ekrem İmamoğlu sentenced to prison and banned from politics
content:
The verdict has been announced in the trial of 12 people, including Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality (İBB) Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu, over allegations that “delegates’ free will was compromised in exchange for financial benefits and the voting process was manipulated” at the 38th Ordinary Congress of the Republican People’s Party (CHP), held on November 4–5, 2023.


The lawsuit was filed following an investigation launched by the Ankara Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office into allegations concerning the CHP’s 38th Ordinary Congress. The indictment alleged that during the congress, where Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality (İBB) Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu served as the Chair of the Congress Presidium, some delegates were given money, promised candidacies and jobs, provided with supermarket gift cards, and asked to submit photographs of their ballot papers. It further alleged that the second round of voting was delayed and misleading information was provided, thereby influencing the delegates’ decisions to secure Özgür Özel’s victory. The prosecution sought prison sentences of up to three years for each defendant on charges of violating the Election Law.


The trial continued at Ankara’s 26th Criminal Court of First Instance on Wednesday.


During the hearing, the public prosecutor reiterated the final opinion on the merits of the case, seeking the conviction of nine defendants, including Ekrem İmamoğlu. The prosecutor requested the acquittal of three defendants, including Cemil Tugay.


The court also delivered its verdict in line with the prosecution’s opinion.


Imprisoned Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu, former Beşiktaş Mayor Rıza Akpolat, Osmangazi Mayor Erkan Aydın, New Party Istanbul Provincial Chair Özgür Çelik, New Party Bursa Provincial Chair Nihat Yeşiltaş, Baki Aydöner, Mehmet Kılınçarslan, Metin Güzelkaya, and Serhat Can Eş were each sentenced to two years and one month in prison for “electoral fraud.” They were also banned from politics.


However, the appeals process must be completed and the verdict upheld before the sentences can be enforced. The ruling will become final following appellate review.


On the other hand, the court acquitted Izmir Metropolitan Municipality Mayor Cemil Tugay, who has joined the AKP, Hüseyin Yaşar, and Özgen Nama on the grounds that there was insufficient evidence beyond reasonable doubt to establish their involvement in the alleged offense.

title: PACE President visits detainees: Turkey is bound to implement the ECtHR judgments
content:
Petra Bayr, the President of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) made a statement following visits to a number of people in detention in Turkey this weekend.


Bayr said she met Osman Kavala, Selahattin Demirtaş, Figen Yüksekdağ Şenoğlu, Ekrem İmamoğlu and Müzeyyen Doğan, a member of HEVİ LGBTI+ Association, arrested in connection with nationwide operations targeting LGBTI+ organisations and activists on 12 September 2026.


“Most of them have been deprived of their liberty for far too long. Four of these five cases are before the European Court of Human Rights. In three, the Court ruled and ordered release. In the fourth, a priority application is pending. Turkey, like every Council of Europe member state, is bound to implement the Court's judgments. Court judgements are not suggestions. They are obligations. Obligations that have been taken on by all of us. A judgment that is not implemented weakens all of us. A judgment that is implemented strengthens all of us.”


Bayr continued: “One thing is clearer to me after these meetings than ever before. We need the member states of the Council of Europe to speak with one voice, in Strasbourg, in the Committee of Ministers and in every bilateral meeting, to insist that the Court's judgments are implemented. At every opportunity, without exception.”


Bayr expressed her hope that this visit will help them continue a constructive dialogue with the Turkish authorities and pave the way for the full and coherent implementation of the Court’s judgments.


“This is not simply about fulfilling legal obligations. It is about strengthening the trust of the Turkish people in their institutions and demonstrating that Turkey remains genuinely committed to building a truly democratic and pluralistic society, a commitment made more than a century ago, when the modern Turkish Republic was founded. Also, the peace process with the Kurdish people will only be successful if it is grounded in the rule of law, democracy and human rights,” the PACE President concluded.

title: EuroLeague'de Beşiktaş, Real Madrid'i 83-79 yendi
content:
Erkekler EuroLeague'in 12. haftasında Beşiktaş, sahasında İspanya ekibi Real Madrid'i 83-79 mağlup etti. Bu sonuçla siyah-beyazlı takım, organizasyonda 6. galibiyetini aldı. Real Madrid ise 5. yenilgisini yaşadı.

Karşılaşmaya sert savunma yaparak başlayan Beşiktaş Fuzul, Gabriel ve Wilbekin'ın kazandırdığı sayılarla 7. dakikada 14 farklı üstünlük yakaladı: 16-2. Çabuk toparlanan Real Madrid, hücumda üretkenliğini kaybeden siyah-beyazlı takım karşısında üst üste bulduğu basketlerle farkı 3'e kadar indirdi. Beşiktaş, ilk periyodu 18-15 önde tamamladı.

İkinci çeyreğin başında dış atışlardan üst üste 3 isabet sağlayan siyah-beyazlılar, 12. dakikada farkı yeniden çift hanelere çıkardı: 27-17. Kalan bölümde de skor üretmeye devam eden ve bu periyotta 3 sayı çizgisinin gerisinden 7 basket kaydeden Beşiktaş Fuzul, soyunma odasına 45-37 üstün gitti.

Üçüncü periyodun ilk 6 dakikasında iki takım da skor üretmekte zorlandı. Karşılıklı basketlere sahne olan son 4 dakikada dış atışlardan kritik basketler bularak üstünlüğünü sürdüren siyah-beyazlı ekip, son bölüme 64-54 önde girdi.

Dördüncü ve son çeyrek büyük bir heyecana sahne oldu. Real Madrid, Smith'in dış atışıyla 37. dakikanın başlarında farkı 4'e düşürdü: 71-67. Eflatun-beyazlılara Jeffries'in kritik basketleriyle yanıt veren Beşiktaş, sahadan 83-79 galip ayrıldı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: 7 Members-Elect Vote Against Jeffries for Speaker, Citing Medicare for All, Gaza
content:
The members said that their “constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate” on progressive issues.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

A group of seven Democratic House representatives-elect cited a voter mandate for action on Gaza and Medicare for All in their opposition to House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries after the caucus selected him for speaker-elect on Wednesday, marking a break from the leader even as the vast majority of other Democrats voted “yes.”

On Wednesday morning, Democrats overwhelmingly nominated Jeffries for speaker in the new Congress in January, in a 251 to 11 yes or no vote, with two absences. The vote was done in a closed-door meeting, with a secret ballot, though Jeffries did call for a recorded vote rather than a simple voice vote. If elected on the House floor in January, he will become the first Black person to ever be the speaker of the House.

Several members spoke in favor of Jeffries ahead of the vote, reports say, including Representatives Teresa Leger Fernández (D-New Mexico) and Jim Clyburn (D-South Carolina), and Rep.-elect Rebecca Bennett (D-Wisconsin). He was also nominated by Representatives Derek Tran (D-California) and Mark Pocan (D-Wisconsin).

Current Democratic Whip Rep. Katherine Clark (D-Massachusetts) was elected as majority leader, the number two position in the caucus. Rep. Pete Aguilar (D-California) was elected as majority whip, and Rep. Ted Lieu (D-California) was chosen as caucus chairman, the third and fourth positions, respectively.

Among the dissenters to Jeffries were seven representatives-elect who said that they are still not assured that Jeffries and his leadership team would help them deliver on key progressive issues.

“Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these issues,” they wrote in a joint statement released after the vote.

“We have worked to secure commitments from Leader Jeffries in good-faith conversations. While we have seen meaningful progress, there is still work to be done to ensure that the direction our party takes this coming Congress reflects what our constituents are demanding of leadership. Those conversations are ongoing. As such, our vote in caucus today was no,” they continued.

The statement was signed by Reps.-elect Darializa Avila Chevalier (D-New York), Adam Hamawy (D-New Jersey), Frederick Haynes (D-Texas), Melat Kiros (D-Colorado), Donavan McKinney (D-Michigan), Chris Rabb (D-Pennsylvania), and Claire Valdez (D-New York). Haynes, who is replacing Rep. Jasmine Crockett (D-Texas), said that he narrowly missed the vote after waking up with an illness, but intended to vote no.

Rep.-elect Angela Gonzales-Torres (D-California) also released a statement explaining her “no” vote, citing a need for leaders to advocate for affordable housing, Medicare for All, the abolition of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and accountability for “the corrupt elite.”

“Since day one, I have been telling leadership that Angelenos have not been satisfied with the status quo and are demanding transformative change. I voted NO today, keeping my community and the trust they instilled in me in mind,” she wrote.

The statements stop short of a full rebuke of Jeffries and his leadership style, but acknowledge many of progressives’ criticisms of the centrist lawmaker, like his vehemently pro-Israel stances and soft hand toward ICE.

Other progressives voted “yes” on Jeffries, however, including figures like Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minnesota), according to Axios.

In a social media post after the vote, Omar did not acknowledge the ballot, but called for progressive priorities to be passed. She listed a set of policies that Democrats passed with their recent trifecta in Minnesota, including universal school meals, paid sick leave, and legal marijuana.

“That’s how you use a majority,” she said. “Now it’s Congress’s turn.”

Donations are down for Truthout at a time when media is under immense pressure. Google’s AI search has driven our traffic down by 15 percent, Trump is arresting journalists, and many independent media organizations face heartbreaking cutbacks and closures.

At the same time, movement media is vital in the fight against Trump’s authoritarian reign. Our mandate to tell the truth, share …

author: Jenny Brown
title: ‘Delay, Deny, Discipline’ Is Amazon’s Real Pregnancy Policy, Workers Say
content:
Willamina Barclay was working as a picker at Amazon’s fulfillment center in Rochester, New York, when she felt lightheaded again. “She pleaded with a manager for a seat… He refused: ‘No, because you don’t have a [pregnancy] accommodation. If I give you a chair, I have to give everybody else a chair,’” he said, according to a recent lawsuit.


But Barclay, who learned she was pregnant in March 2025, had already asked managers many times for accommodations—a seat, extra breaks to drink, eat, pee (or throw up) in the bathroom, no ladder-climbing or squatting, and no heavy lifting.


Amazon—a company known for fast delivery—had failed to answer for weeks, demanding medical documentation. Even after Barclay provided it, Amazon still refused most accommodations, permitting her four breaks a day, but no chair. She was moved to a different position, but still required to lift heavy packages.


Amazon counted her new breaks against her unpaid time off (UPT), a leave bank that workers accumulate at five minutes per hour and that maxes out at 80 hours. She went to Human Resources several times to try to rectify the situation, but stopped because they were also counting those visits as UPT, the lawsuit says.


The heavy lifting led to sharp pains. At one point she left the warehouse in a wheelchair headed for the hospital. Amazon also counted that time against her unpaid leave bank. On another occasion, she had to leave due to uncontrolled vomiting. Despite a doctor’s note, that was also counted against her. Her UPT thus used up, Amazon fired her.


Under the law, workers cannot be penalized for taking pregnancy-related leave

(see box at end of article)

.


Barclay’s ordeal is detailed in a lawsuit filed September 8 by

A Better Balance

, a nonprofit focused on work policies affecting families. It’s a proposed class action on behalf of all U.S. workers whose rights under the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act (PWFA) have been violated by Amazon.


SYSTEMATIC VIOLATIONS


Barclay’s harrowing experience is common, said Sultana Hossain, recording secretary of the Amazon Labor Union (ALU) on Staten Island: Under the law “pregnant workers don’t have to give in paperwork,” she said. “They only have to verbally say, ‘I’m pregnant and I need to be accommodated.’ But we’re seeing Amazon systemically violate that.


“Even if workers get an accommodation eventually, it can take several weeks,” said Hossain. “So people really don’t have any choice but to keep working in their regular role, which is really dangerous if they actually need an accommodation.”


Key’Asia, a worker at Amazon’s fulfillment center near Wilmington, Delaware, said that Amazon management twice rejected a note from her doctor, once because it had an e-signature, and then again when she got an ink signature. (For privacy to discuss medical matters, some workers asked that last names not be used.)


Managers said the signature looked fraudulent and still refused to accommodate her pregnancy, Key’Asia said. “They are making you do the things that your doctor told you that you’re not supposed to be doing,” she told attendees at an online Jobs With Justice event in October. “They’re making you do things that are putting yourself and your baby at risk.” She said Amazon fired her twice, both times when she was pregnant.


PATTERN OF ILLEGALITY


Workers have noticed a pattern: When they request accommodations, Amazon managers ask if they are “safe to work.” If they say “yes,” they are forced to continue to work without accommodations. If they say “no,” Amazon puts them on

unpaid leave

, which rapidly runs out.


Marissa, who worked at Amazon’s fulfillment center in Rossford, Ohio, said that after her accommodations were denied, she was forced out on unpaid leave, and she ended up losing her apartment. “I was out $1,700… I couldn’t pay for my vehicle. I couldn’t afford to eat.


“Amazon doesn’t care about whether or not you’re in pain,” she said. “They care about whether or not you can get their packages out on time.”


Hossain said it was typical for workers to get fired for “job abandonment” because “they ran out of time-off options because they were just not given the accommodation.” (A Better Balance

has also sued

 Amazon for this practice on behalf of a disabled worker.)


TRAGIC RESULTS


Hayat Bzezi was working at Amazon’s Staten Island JFK8 warehouse during the busy holiday season of 2024, when all workers were required to take an additional weekly 10-hour shift …
