title: Clara Mattei: Capitalism deliberately produces poverty
content:
Historically, how have governments used austerity policies as an economic instrument to protect capitalism, suppress wages, dismantle social protections and prevent democratic oversight? Economist Clara Mattei, who examines these issues in her book

The Capital Order: How Economists Invented Austerity and Paved the Way to Fascism

, answered our questions.


With Mattei, one of the most prominent researchers working on the history and critique of austerity policies, we discussed the rise of right-wing governments around the world, wars in the Middle East and the rapidly accelerating militarisation of Europe from a political economy perspective. We also explored how an effective strategy of resistance against these developments could be built.


According to Oxfam, the twelve richest people in the world — all men — now own more money than the poorest half of the world's population, which is more than four billion people. How is this exploitative “capital order” created? 


Inequality is not an accidental or corruptive element of our economy. Inequality is deeply rooted in the very formation of economic growth and what can be called “accumulation of wealth”.  


There wouldn't be any wealth without the creation of market dependence and the precarity to compel workers to work for a wage — for someone else. This is a crucial point about the capital order — capital money is really based on this political relation of exploitation that is never mentioned by economists but is fundamental to understanding any dynamic of capitalism, including impoverishment, inequality, and structural violence. 


Many people find economics incomprehensible — yet politicians make far-reaching decisions. Is "complexity" a real problem or also a political tool to depoliticize decisions? Who wins when the public merely watches instead of participating in decision-making? 


This is crucial, and it is the reason why we founded the Forum for Real Economic  Emancipation (freefreeforum.org): to create a space where economic ideas can actually  become empowering to people, a space to explain the problems people feel in their own skin. 


The fact is, economics is a discipline meant to be kept in the hands of very few, who protect that knowledge as something absolutely inaccessible to the undereducated majority. Yes, complexification, mathematization, and technical language are wonderful ways to maintain explanatory power, and thus retain political power. 


And so, the reason people have not fully rebelled against the system is that they are told they don’t understand how it works, and have to listen to the experts. But these experts are merely hiding all of their extremely classist assumptions beneath formulas, mathematics. These assumptions oblige people to accept a system based on structural exploitation and violence. One important example of this that I give in my book is the harsh rejection of the labor theory of value – that explains profit as the product of unpaid labor – in favor of a theory of abstinence by which value is not coming from exploitation of one class over the other, but rather it is the outcome of the virtuous capacity to save of the rational savers-investors. 


You criticize the Western-dominated academic world: to what extent is modern economics/economic science historically and politically influenced by the West? What does this obscure, and what models of thinking and politics are exported globally as a result? 


I show in my first book how mainstream economics — the economics that is still taught in schools and still informs public debate — was championed at a moment of extreme and widespread criticism and challenges to capitalism as a way of organizing our society. This is because economics was meant to protect society from any upheaval and from any challenge.


And so, what you find is that a lot of its theories, for example, the idea that exploitation does not exist, that everything is just and fair because people get exactly what they deserve from their market transactions, and the idea that the entrepreneur counts much more than the worker, or that harmony is the consequence of self-interested behavior — are ideas that really help propel a sense of the impossibility of escaping capitalism. They deeply naturalize capitalism and the hierarchy that it produces. 


So economic ideas emerged especially to tell workers that they could not participate in  changing the world. And this is still the case today. Clearly, these …

author: CNT Villaverde Alto - Comarcal Sur de Madrid
title: Crónica: la Huelga General del 11N desde CNT Comarcal Sur
content:
Con algo menos de un mes de trabajo a las espaldas, la noche del pasado 10 de noviembre, CNT Comarcal Sur desplegó toda su preparación en la jornada de Huelga General con una premisa clara:

subir los salarios, bajar los alquileres

. Fueron algo más de tres semanas de presencia en la mesa sindical, en asambleas de barrios y municipios, en los centros de trabajo y en el seno del propio Sindicato, traducidas en

24 horas que bien pudieron durar décadas

.


Arrancamos la jornada acompañando a

nuestra Sección Sindical en EMT

 durante los piquetes desarrollados en las cocheras de Carabanchel. Como con cada día de Huelga General, el despliegue de la acción sindical sobre el transporte —sea de la condición que sea— es indispensable para asegurar el éxito de la jornada; así como para garantizar el cumplimiento de los servicios mínimos e informar a las y los compañeros no obligados a trabajar este día de su derecho a secundar la jornada de paro.


Dada la importancia del sector del transporte rodado, no solo respaldamos el trabajo de las compañeras de la Sección de EMT, sino que, también, acompañando a los Comités Unitarios tanto de Getafe como de Leganés, acudimos a las cocheras de autobuses de ambas ciudades.


En esta misma línea y, siguiendo el trabajo desarrollado en las semanas previas, marcado por la militancia de base, desde el territorio y en sentido unitario,

la presencia del Sindicato junto a los Comités Unitarios fue fundamental en la jornada

. Si bien de por sí la aparición de estos comités territoriales marcaba un rasgo diferencial con respecto a anteriores convocatorias de Huelga General;

la apuesta de este Sindicato por la organización unitaria de la Huelga

, así como su naturaleza de Comarcal Sur, facultó que tanto las afiliadas a título individual pudiesen participar en sus comités más cercanos, así como que la organización apoyase con fuerza logística y militante las acciones de distintos comités.


A las acciones en cocheras, tanto en Getafe como en Leganés, se sumó la presencia de

piquetes tanto en zonas industriales como comerciales

, así como durante las reclamas nocturnas que, en algunos casos, se convirtieron en marchas que iniciaron la actividad informativa por los establecimientos que, ya de madrugada, se encontraban abiertos y fueron notificados del arranque de la Huelga General. Así, se consiguió

con éxito tanto la distribución de información entre trabajadoras como el cierre de negocios secundando la convocatoria

; con especial hincapié en el piquete comercial desplegado por Villaverde junto a su comité de huelga, dada la vinculación de este Sindicato con el barrio por su raigambre a través del Ateneo Libertario de Villaverde.


Comida popular en el Ateneo Libertario


Este espacio, nuestro local, fue epicentro para la actividad del Sindicato desde la misma madrugada, sirviendo como punto de encuentro para huelguistas, afiliadas o no; espacio de descanso y reposo, así como de avituallamiento para reponer fuerzas comiendo y bebiendo lo necesario o secando la ropa en una jornada pasada por agua. Porque nuestro objetivo siempre ha sido prefigurar el mundo nuevo que queremos en cada uno de los pasos que damos, un día de Huelga General es el espacio para llevar hasta su extremo este principio. Así, al apoyo mutuo en los piquetes, a los cuidados entre compañeras y a nuestro local como lugar de refugio y descanso, se sumó

una gran comida popular preparada por las militantes y para las militantes

, con las puertas abiertas a todo el barrio en huelga; porque las que comen juntas conspiran juntas.


Simultáneamente, como en el caso de la EMT, mientras se desplegaban piquetes por los municipios del sur,

las compañeras organizadas en Secciones Sindicales extendieron a sus centros de trabajo la convocatoria de Huelga General

, compartiendo la labor con compañeras de otros sindicatos y con el apoyo de la propia afiliación de este Sindicato que, solidariamente, pudo reforzar cada convocatoria.


Piquete del Sector Social en Madrid


Así, tras un descanso fraternal, pusimos rumbo hacia el centro de Madrid, donde nos esperaba una convocatoria que desbordó cualquier expectativa. Allí,

junto a las compañeras de las CNT de la Comunidad y de los anarcosindicatos Solidaridad Obrera y CGT

, conformamos un bloque sindicalista, anarquista y de base, que diese cuerpo y voz a los principios y objetivos que nos venían guiando, no desde el arranque de la jornada, sino desde su preparación semanas atrás …

title: Hürmüz Boğazı'nda BAE petrol şirketinin gemisine saldırı
content:
Temsili görsel | Fotoğraf: Eric Seddon/Pexels

BAE resmi haber ajansı WAM'ın ADNOC açıklamasına dayandırdığı habere göre saldırı, 17 Kasım akşamı meydana geldi. Yaralanan 11 mürettebatın tedavisi sürerken kayıp kişi için arama kurtarma çalışmaları devam ediyor.

Şirket, saldırının nasıl gerçekleştirildiği ve gemide meydana gelen hasar hakkında ayrıntı paylaşmadı.

ABD ile İran arasındaki tırmanan gerilim, küresel enerji taşımacılığının en önemli geçiş noktalarından Hürmüz Boğazı'nda güvenlik kaygılarını artırıyor. Boğazdaki sevkiyat aksamaları petrol ve doğalgaz piyasalarını da etkiliyor. ADNOC gemisine yönelik saldırının ardından bölgedeki deniz trafiğine ilişkin endişeler yeniden gündeme geldi.

author: Unknown
title: AKP'de fon vurgunu krizi: "Cami cemaatinin tepkisi bizi korkuttu"
content:
Fon vurgununun ardından AKP içinde tepkilerin büyüdüğü, partinin kendi tabanından gelen eleştiriler karşısında zorlandığı öne sürüldü. Nefes yazarı Nuray Babacan, bugünkü köşesinde fon krizinin AKP içinde yarattığı rahatsızlığı ve iktidar partisinin tabanından gelen tepkileri ele aldı. Babacan, iktidar partisinde özellikle “cami cemaatinin tepkisi”nden çekinildiğine ilişkin kulis bilgilerini aktardı. Babacan'ın aktardığına göre, AKP'li bir kurmay, partinin kendi tabanından gelen eleştirilerin önceki sorunlardan farklı olduğunu belirterek şunları söyledi;

“Vatandaş cebinden parasının çalındığı ve zenginlere verildiği hissinde. Hiçbir sorun, tabanda bu kadar yankı bulmamıştı. Kemik taban sorunu yaşanıyor. Beraber siyaset yaptığımız, bize oy verdiğini bildiğimiz isimlerin eleştirisi çok sert. Haklı olduklarını, sonuna kadar hesap soracağımızı söylüyoruz. Aynı düşünceleri paylaştığımızı söylemek bile onları yatıştırmıyor.”

Babacan, fon vurgununun kamuoyuna yansımasından üç hafta sonra yapılan nabız yoklamalarında tepkilerin arttığının görüldüğünü yazdı. İlk anket sonuçlarının ardından “Vatandaş hâlâ bunu konuşuyor mu ya…” diye şaşıranlar olduğunu aktaran Babacan, anketlerin her seferinde daha kötü sonuç vermesi üzerine parti içinde harekete geçme kararı alındığını belirtti.

Babacan'ın aktardığı kulis bilgilerine göre, seçimlere kadar krizin yarattığı tepki giderilemezse AKP'nin oy oranının yüzde 25'lerde kalabileceği değerlendiriliyor. Fon vurgunuyla ilgili kamuoyuna yansıyan “Listede 60 milletvekili var” iddiasının da tepki gördüğünü belirten Babacan, Ankara Ulus Hali'nde bir pazarcının bir siyasetçiye “O vekillerin koluna kelepçeyi takmadan buraya gelmeyin” diye bağırdığı olayın da konuşulduğunu yazdı.

Babacan, yazısına şöyle devam etti; “Yurt dışına kaçan 40-50 ismin iktidardaki operasyon hareketliliğini fark eder etmez, 1-15 Eylül tarihleri arasında çıkış yaptığı saptanıyor. Yani, konunun kapatılamayacak kadar büyük olduğuna karar verilmesinden hemen sonra, 17 Eylül’de başlayan gözaltı dalgasından hemen önce… Zamanlama manidar!

Bir yandan TMSF, bu fonlara 10 milyon liranın üzerinde para yatıran herkesi tek tek görüşmeye çağırıp, kazandıkları parayı geri yatırmalarını istiyor. Aylar öncesinden fonla vedalaşmış olan kişiler durumu şaşkınlıkla karşılarken, ‘Yatırmazsak ne olur?’ sorusuna görevlilerin, ‘Bilmiyoruz, biz sadece takip ve uyarı ile sorumluyuz’ dediği anlatılıyor. Soruşturma ve tutuklanma korkusu hızla yayılıyor.

Diğer yandan Borsa İstanbul Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı ve Türkiye Varlık Fonu Yönetim Kurulu Başkan Vekili Erişah Arıcan’ın görevden alınacağı, hatta geç kalındığı konuşuluyor. Beştepe’de düzenlenen her ekonomi toplantısına katılan ve ekonomi yönetiminin tezlerinin tam tersini savunan Arıcan’la ilgili partide aylar öncesinden oluşmuş bir tepki zaten var. Toplantılarda, yurt dışına kaçan paralar konusunda uluslararası alanda devreye girildiği, kaçan isimlerle ilgili de kırmızı bülten hazırlandığı bilgisi paylaşılıyor."

author: Unknown
title: Yılın kelimesi "insan" oldu
content:
Fotoğraf: Mehmet Turgut Kirkgoz/Pexels

İngiltere merkezli Cambridge Sözlüğü, yapay zekanın hızla gelişmesiyle insan ve makine arasındaki sınırların giderek daha fazla tartışılmaya başlanması ve insanların teknolojiye bağımlılıklarına ilişkin endişelerin artması nedeniyle 2026 yılının kelimesini "insan" (human) olarak belirledi.

Sözlük tarafından yapılan açıklamada, yılın kelimesinin insanların, hayvanlardan veya makinelerden farklı olarak sahip olduğu nitelikleri, kusurları ve duyguları ifade ettiği belirtildi.

Cambridge Sözlüğü Baş Editörü Colin McIntosh, yapay zekanın insanların insan olma biçimine ilişkin konuşmalarını değiştirdiğini belirtti. İnsanların düşünme süreçlerini yapay zekaya devretmeleri halinde neleri kaybedebileceklerine yönelik endişelerin, teknolojiye ne ölçüde güvenmeleri gerektiğini yeniden değerlendirmelerine yol açtığını ifade eden McIntosh, yapay zekanın matematikten küçük yaştaki çocukların eğitimine kadar pek çok alanda kullanılmasının, insanların kendi düşünme becerilerini teknolojiye bırakmalarına ilişkin tartışmaları artırdığına dikkati çekti.

McIntosh, "insan" kelimesinin bu tartışmaların merkezine yerleştiğini kaydetti.

Cambridge Sözlüğü'nün 2026 için değerlendirdiği diğer kelimeler arasında, insan kontrolü olmadan karmaşık işlemleri gerçekleştirebilen yapay zeka sistemlerini tanımlayan "agent" (ajan), fiziksel, ahlaki veya duygusal açıdan kişinin hayatını iyileştiren şeyleri ifade eden "wholesome" ve internet ya da dijital teknoloji içermeyen faaliyetleri tanımlayan "analogue" (analog) yer aldı.

Sözlüğün 2025 yılı kelimesi ise kişinin hiç tanımadığı bir ünlüye veya kurgusal karaktere karşı geliştirdiği tek taraflı duygusal bağı ifade eden "parasosyal" olmuştu.

author: Rafael Oliveira
title: “Pelo menos o banco fez dinheiro”: vazamento expõe bastidores do Deutsche Bank no Brasil
content:
Vazamento mostra escândalos de um dos maiores bancos do mundo. A

 Pública

 é o único parceiro no Brasil. Leia o especial

Inside Deutsche Bank


aqui.


Vazamento mostra escândalos de um dos maiores bancos do mundo. A

 Pública

 é o único parceiro no Brasil. Leia o especial

Inside Deutsche Bank


aqui.


O que a mineradora Vale, o banco Safra, a petroquímica Braskem e a construtora Andrade Gutierrez têm em comum? Além da origem brasileira, de negócios bilionários e da atuação que transcende os limites do território nacional,

as quatro empresas foram clientes de um banco que teve funcionários relativizando acusações ou tentando contornar mecanismos internos em prol do lucro.


Isso é o que apontam documentos sigilosos acessados pela

Agência Pública

, que incluem e-mails, relatórios e planilhas internas do Deutsche Bank (DB), um dos maiores bancos do mundo, presente no Brasil há mais de um século.


O material é parte do

Inside Deutsche Bank

, investigação transnacional da qual a

Pública

 faz parte, baseada no vazamento de mais de 15 milhões de documentos do banco, obtido pelos jornalistas sul-africanos Josy Joseph e Khadija Sharife. O projeto tem coordenação global da Barracuda Media e do Centro Latinoamericano de Periodismo de Investigación (CLIP) na região.


Os documentos do projeto mostram, entre outras coisas, como o banco descumpriu suas próprias regras para clientes poderosos e repetidamente ignorou sinais de alerta, inclusive no Brasil.

 As questões não se limitaram às quatro empresas citadas nesta reportagem. A primeira

reportagem

 da série detalhou uma grande controvérsia em torno do BTG Pactual, de André Esteves. Nos próximos dias, reportagens mostrarão a conduta do Deutsche Bank frente a acusações contra as gigantes da proteína animal BRF e JBS e também contra a Cutrale, uma das campeãs globais na produção de suco de laranja.


Vale: Executiva do Deutsche Bank ressaltou “compromisso com sustentabilidade”


Em 25 de janeiro de 2019, a cidade de Brumadinho (MG) virou lama. O rompimento da barragem da mina de ferro Córrego do Feijão matou 272 pessoas e lançou milhões de toneladas de rejeitos na bacia do rio Paraopeba. A tragédia foi o maior acidente de trabalho da história do Brasil em vidas humanas perdidas e um dos maiores desastres ambientais já registrados no país.


Na época, Minas Gerais ainda se recuperava do

rompimento de uma barragem

 da mineradora Samarco, na cidade de Mariana, em 2015. O que ambas tinham em comum? A Vale. No primeiro desastre, a empresa responsável pela barragem era uma

joint venture

 entre a Vale e a australiana BHP (o conselho de administração era formado por representantes de ambas, com 50% do controle cada). No caso do segundo, a Vale era a única operadora da mina.


 Mariana (MG) devastada pela lama, em tragédia ocorrida em 2015


De acordo com os emails analisados pela

Pública

, três dias depois da tragédia de Brumadinho, a funcionária responsável pela chefia da cobertura de Corporate Banking (voltada ao atendimento de empresas) do Deutsche Bank no Brasil enviou um email para colegas estrangeiros, com as primeiras informações sobre a situação. Na mensagem, Luciana Novaes informava que a equipe brasileira vinha acompanhando as notícias, faria uma reunião sobre o assunto naquele mesmo dia e estava em contato com o Grupo Global de Sustentabilidade do DB.


O que chama a atenção, porém, é

o email que Novaes envia horas depois, para compartilhar o posicionamento da equipe brasileira sobre o episódio após a reunião.


“Nossa opinião é que a situação ainda é muito instável e é prematuro chegar a qualquer conclusão sobre as causas do rompimento da barragem”, afirma a funcionária do banco. Ela também recomenda que o Deutsche Bank continuasse a monitorar a situação de perto e mantivesse contato próximo com a Vale para obter informações sobre relatórios técnicos, além de acompanhar as contas da mineradora e conversar com outros bancos para saber suas visões quanto ao episódio.


Depois das atualizações iniciais,

o resto do email é ocupado por uma exaltação das qualidades da Vale.


“A Vale é uma empresa reconhecida pelo seu compromisso com a sustentabilidade”, disse a funcionária do banco. Para fundamentar seu ponto de vista, em seguida, ela apontou no email a presença da mineradora em rankings de respeito aos direitos humanos e sustentabilidade, como o World Corporate Human Rights Benchmark, o Global Compact LEAD da ONU e o Índice de Sustentabilidade Empresarial …

author: Unknown
title: Alev alev IDFA
content:
Heybeli’nin tam karşımızdaki mıntıkasında orman cayır cayır yanıyordu. Rüzgarlı havadan dolayı ilk dumanı fark ettiğimiz andan çok kısa süre sonra koca koca çamların aniden tutuşup alevlerin hızla yanlarındakine geçmesine, ben ve arkadaşlarım Burgaz’dan çaresizce şahit oluyorduk.


Havadan müdahalenin gecikmeden başlaması yüreklerimize su serpmiş, ben gene de yerimde duramadığım gibi gözyaşlarıma hâlâ mani olamıyordum. Bunda annemin çocukluğundaki bir yangının onda bıraktığı travmanın tesiri var mıydı bilemiyorum, lakin ikimizin de bu hususta epeyce hassas olduğu kesindi.


Ergenliğimde bizim adanın Hristos tepesinde sahilden gördüğümüz duman beni anında tetiklemiş; müdahalede asgari zarar görmemi sağlayacak kıyafetlerimi hızla kuşanıp tepeye itfaiye araçlarından önce varmıştım. Romantik bir oğlan olduğumdan, normalde sırtımı yaslayarak gurubu izlediğim ağaçlardan bilhassa bir tanesini kurtarmak için büyükçe bir çam dalıyla alevlere var gücümle vurmuş, canımı resmen dişime katmıştım. Vücüdumun açıkta kalan alanlarında kıllarım alev aldığı gibi yüksek ısıdan ve dumandan neredeyse bayılacak hâle gelmiştim. İmdadıma annem ve arkadaşı

Helga

 yetişmiş, yanlarında getirdikleri suyu, içim kurumuşçasına kana kana içmiştim.


Yıllar içinde yangınlar birbirini takip etmiş, lakin 2003’te Burgaz adasının neredeyse tüm ormanının kül olmasına yol açan büyük yangınında bile birileri hayatını tehlikeye atmaya devam ederken belirli bir grubun felakete medyatik bir sansasyona bakar gibi soğukça yaklaşması insanlık adına kabul edilir bir durum değildi.


İstikbalimiz ne olacak?


>1,5°C: Pyropolitics and the New World

 adlı belgesel yangının sadece tabii bir afet olmakla kalmayıp küresel ısınmayla bağlantılı olarak siyasi bir dinamik hâline gelmesini de kurcalıyor. Uluslararası Amsterdam Belgesel Film Festivali’nin (IDFA) dünya çapındaki festivallerde ses getirmiş belgesellerden oluşan Best of fests klasmanında Amsterdam seyircisiyle buluşan çarpıcı film 230 kilometre karelik alanın yanmasına, 16 binden fazla binanın yok olmasına yol açan 2025 California felaketine odaklanıyor.


Haftalar boyunca söndürülemeyen yangını gayet uzun sekanslar sayesinde de tenimizde hissediyor, alevlerle mücadele edenlere birer kahramana bakarcasına hayran kalıyoruz. Zor durumda kalanlara yönelik yardım faaliyetlerine şahit oluyor, adeta cehenneme dönmüş coğrafyayı siren seslerinin kuşatmışlığına biz de maruz kalıyoruz.


Yönetmen, prodüktör ve montaj hanelerinde adını tek başına, sinematografide

Carson Davis


Brown

’la gördüğümüz

Lukas Marxt

 bizi adeta hipnotize ediyor. Televizyon haberlerinde hızla üzerinden geçtiğimiz yıkımı bize uzun uzun göstererek bu hususta derin düşüncelere dalmamıza imkân tanıyor.


2026 Almanya, Avusturya ortak yapımı 73 dakikalık film, gezegenin karanlık istikbali hususunda bizi bir kez daha uyarırken, bazılarının inkâr etmeye meyilli olduğu korkutucu vaziyetin artık fazlasıyla içinde olduğumuzu da gözümüze sokuyor; Bank of America binasının yandığını gösteren sekans da cabası!


Festival gözdeleri ve dahası…


2026 IDFA’da büyük alakayla karşılanan belgesellerden 

Musk

 ve

Naza

 seyircinin güncel mevzulara olan açlığını ispatladı.


Festivalde yer alan fimlerden Ürdün’de Filistinli göçebelerle alakalı

Beton Diyar

,

Che

’nin yoldaşlarının izinden gitmemize imkân tanıyan

Che Guevara: Son Yoldaşlar

, İran’ın dirayetle süren kadın ayaklanmarına bizi zarafetle dahil eden

Devrim Provaları

 görülmeye değer eserlerden.


Belarus’ta adeta unutulmuş insanları tekrar hatırlatıp dayanışmaya çağıran

Susturulmuş Diyardan Mektuplar

, güvenlik kuvvetlerinin üniforma yüzünden yetkilerini aşmaya meyilli olmasına dair 

Mahpusluk

, göçmenlik siyasetine bir halk hareketiyle direnmenin ve zafere ulaşmanın adeta manifestosu

Herkes Kenmure Sokağına

 IDFA’nın enteresan katılımcılarından bir diğer üçü.


Filistin kökenli bir anne ve Yahudi bir babaya sahip olmanın ne demek olduğunu

Az Zeeb

 bize layıkıyla aktarırken yanıbaşımızdaki coğrafyada bitmek bilmeyen savaşların acısını

Savaş Kuşları

 belgeselinde tenimizde hissediyoruz.


Bir Zamanlar Harlem’de

 bizi ABD’de siyahların gerçekleştirmiş olduğu Rönesansa dahil ederken

Gabin

 bizi Fransa’nın kırsal kesimine zarafetle dahil ediyor.


Pembe ve Mavi Binada Altı Ay

 otobiyografik özellikleri sayesinde IDFA’da yer alan (çok sevimli ve neşeli) kurmacalardan biri.


Dağı Tepesindeki Orman

 sayesinde Latin Amerika’da işgalciler yüzünden kıyıma uğramış kadim halkları …

author: Unknown
title: Di lêpirsînên fonê de 40,4 mîlyar lîre hat bidestxistin
content:
Wezîrê Dadê Akın Gurlek, daneyên dawî yên derbarê lêpirsînên fonê de ku ji aliyê Serdozgeriya Komarê ya Stenbolê ve tên meşandin, parve kirin. Gurlek ragihand ku di çarçoveya van lêpirsînan de, bi rêya vegerandina bi dilxwazî û bidestxistinê, ji 75 kesan bi qasî 40,4 mîlyar lîre hatiye berhevkirin.


Gurlek li ser hesabê xwe yê medyaya civakî daxuyaniyek belav kir û diyar kir ku lêpirsîn li gorî delîlên nû hatiye kûrkirin. Her weha destnîşan kir ku tevgerên pereyan, veguhestina mal û milkan û hesabên pêwendîdar bi hûrgilî tên lêkolînkirin.


498 gumanbar, 129 girtî


Gurlek derbarê rewşa dawî ya lêpirsînan de agahî dan û aşkere kir ku bi giştî 498 gumanbar hene.


Li gorî daneyên ku Gurlek parve kirine, 129 gumanbar girtî ne û ji bo 289 kesan jî biryara kontrola edlî hatiye dayîn. Xebatên ji bo girtina 54 gumanbarên ku biryara zeftkirinê li ser wan heye didomin û karûbarên edlî yên 22 kesên desteserkirî jî berdewam in.


Hat diyarkirin ku di çarçoveya lêpirsînan de, ji bo pêşîgirtina li revandina dahatên ku tê nirxandin ji sûc hatine bidestxistin, li ser mal û milkên 417 kesan û 149 saziyan biryara destdanîn û rawestandinê hatiye bicihanîn.


Îdiayên derbarê karmendên dewletê de


Gurlek diyar kir ku ji bilî rêveberên fonan û aktorên bazarê, îdiayên li ser pêvajoyên çavdêriyê jî di çarçoveya lêpirsînê de ne.


Gurlek destnîşan kir ku hemû mijarên ku dikarin berpirsiyariya hiqûqî biafirînin karmendên dewletê jî di nav de ji aliyê rayedarên edlî yên peywendîdar ve tên nirxandin û di daxuyaniya xwe de wiha got:


"Ji bo me ne dezgeh, unvan ango têkiliyên kesan, delîlên şênber û berpirsiyariya hiqûqî diyarker in. Tu îdia wê pêşwext rast neyê qebûlkirin û tu delîlên şênber jî wê neyên paşguhkirin."


Vegerandina bi dilxwazî berpirsiyariyê ji holê ranake


Gurlek aşkere kir ku di çarçoveya vegerandina bi dilxwazî û bidestxistinê de ji 75 kesan bi qasî 40,4 mîlyar lîre hatiye standin û tekez kir ku vegerandina pereyan wê berpirsiyariya hiqûqî ji holê raneke.


Gurlek got, "Vegerandina bi dilxwazî, bi tena serê xwe berpirsiyariya hiqûqî ji holê ranake."


Ji aliyê din ve Gurlek diyar kir ku bi serokatiya Alîkarê Serokkomar Cevdet Yilmaz, 10emîn Civîna Lijneya Koordînasyona Fonan hatiye lidarxistin û di civînê de rewşa lêpirsînan, lêkolînên darayî, tedbîrên hatine wergirtin û xebatên ji bo parastina mafên veberhêneran hatine nirxandin.


(FY/AY)

author: Kodao Productions
title: Pax Silica signing failure a temporary victory for Trump Out campaign – activists
content:
Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) welcomed as a “temporary victory” the failure of the US and Philippine governments to sign a Pax Silica agreement during Donald Trump’s visit to the country.


At the conclusion of their series of protest actions nationwide on Wednesday, Bayan said the Ferdinand Marcos  Jr. government suffered a “[m]ajor public relations failure and embarrassing diplomatic blunder.”


“[T]he failure of the Trump and Marcos regimes to sign the scheduled agreement is a temporary victory for the Trump Out  campaign since one of its key objectives was to prevent such signing from taking place,” Bayan secretary general Raymond Palatino said.


Palatino said the massive protests against Pax Silica in the last two weeks made it difficult for the Marcos regime to ink a one-sided agreement.


(Photo by Nuel M. Bacarra/Kodao)


Brutal suppression


Bayan said Marcos’s brutal and underhanded tactics against protests only managed to show the world the widespread opposition against Pax Silica and Trump’s visit to the Philippines.


With hundreds of violent arrests since Sunday and attempts to block rallies from reaching spots where Trump was expected, Bayan said Marcos showed the broad range of resistance against Pax Silica and the US leader.


“We condemn the barbed wires, container vans, and barricades placed by the police to block the march from reaching Mendiola. This is overkill and pathetic groveling to secure the unwelcome war criminal and plunderer Donald Trump,” Bayan secretary general Raymond Palatino said.


National and international news, however, highlighted the mass arrests and violent police dispersals of rallies in Metro Manila, Central Luzon, Southern Tagalog and Cebu.


Tens of thousands of students held protest rallies as far south as Davao City and as far north as Cagayan Valley since last week.


Thousands of protesters concluded their week-long series of protests against Trump’s visit along Recto Avenue in Manila as Trump and Marcos held bilateral talks on Wednesday. #

(Raymund B. Villanueva)

title: Prisoner Newroz Bozkurt brought to hospital
content:
Newroz Bozkurt, who suffers from Chronic Lymphocytic Leukaemia (CLL), was transferred to Etlik City Hospital on Saturday, 14 November, after becoming unwell.

author: Isaac Nellist
title: Community picket shuts down Bisalloy Steel for 36-hours over ties to Israel’s genocide
content:
A community picket has shut down operations the Bisalloy Steel factor in Unanderra, in Tharawal/Wollongong, for the 11th time, over November 15–17, for its role in arming Israel’s genocide in Gaza.

Bisalloy Steel supplies armoured steel to Israel that is used for armoured vehicles, tanks and other military technology used in its genocide of Palestinian’s in Gaza and occupation of the West Bank.

The picket was organised by Wollongong Friends of Palestine (WFoP) and supported by many Palestine solidarity and anti-militarism groups.

“We had amazing community support,” Safaa Rayan, social worker and WFoP spokesperson, told Green Left. “It was cold and rainy but we still managed to have hundreds of people not just turn up, but camp out. The street was lined with tents, each full with people.

“Parents turned up with their children, we had three DJ performances each day … we even had people join in who have never been to a protest or picket before.”

At the previous picket in June, NSW Police attempted to break up the picket, arresting at least one person and pushing others to the ground. One woman was concussed after police allegedly pushed her head into the pavement.

“The police violence at the last picket really shows how Bisalloy and the cops are working together to protect the genocide supply chain,” Rayan said. “It's clear the NSW government values business as usual for genocide suppliers far more than the rights of citizens, let alone the lives of Palestinians.”

Rayan said the police presence was minimal this time. “They sent out a car every three hours, would drive past and leave.

“Our pickets are extraordinarily peaceful, and people are very respectful of the area and the environment.”

Local campaigner and Jewish woman Kim Sattler said the deepening militarisation of Wollongong and the appointment of Bisalloy into the AUKUS supply chain was concerning. “This endangers our local community and leads us into war.”

Rayan said “AUKUS is a threat to not only Australia's sovereignty, but also to our environment bringing nuclear submarines at our shores, particularly as they want to build a base here at Port Kembla”.

Climate organiser and youth worker Jayne Hoschke said Bisalloy should make things that the community needs to address the climate crisis. “Instead, they’re determined to help make things that make the world worse … our community won’t let that happen.”

“It's all interconnected,” Rayyan told GL. “We will continue to picket at Bisalloy until they divest from the military industrial complex.”

She also called on the federal and state government to take action. “It is their obligation under the United Nations statue to not supply weapons or weapons parts to a country committing a genocide.

“Because of their inaction, we as the citizens are having to do the work.”

Wollongong Friends of Palestine

author: Cas Smith
title: Hazelmere locals reject plans for mega AI data centre
content:
About 200 people rallied outside Midland Town Hall on November 11 to oppose plans for a hyperscale artificial intelligence data centre in Hazelmere, in Perth’s eastern suburbs.

Gwenaël (Gwen) Velge, a Research Associate at Murdoch University’s Mineral Policy Institute; Kate Herron from Trillion Trees; and former Labor MLA Matthew Hughes addressed the rally and highlighted the disruptive nature of CDC Data Centres’ planned project, which is expected to cause significant noise pollution and energy usage.

At a consultation meeting last month, a CDC technician said the data centre would have an energy allotment of 192 megawatts (MW) with 96 generators.

This would make it significantly larger than the 120 MW, 88 generator data centre previously proposed by Greensquare, which was rejected earlier this year by the City of Swan, following community backlash and concerns about noise pollution.

Velge noted the significance of this decision in the Mining Monitor on October 29. “Earlier this year, the City recommended refusing the GreenSquare proposal over the potential noise of its 88 generators.

“CDC proposes 96 generators, [which] come within 1dB (decibels) of the limit modelled at 75% load, and approach ‘the limits of compliance’; whereas Greensquare was asked to model at 100% load.”

He said the “sheer scale” of the energy demand of hyperscale data centres makes it harder to achieve a renewable energy transition.

“Renewable energy capacity meant to replace coal and gas is directly absorbed by this new demand. In the best-case scenario, this added demand slows down the transition, in the worst-case scenario the narrative and promises of ‘transition’ justifies and legitimates actual energy addition.

“Of course, some grid growth is to be expected as we electrify. But data centres are a clear case of addition: that demand did not exist before and it competes directly with the electrification part of the transition.”

The Australian Energy Market Operator (AEMO) expects consumption on the region’s electrical grid to increase by 57% in the next decade, from 20.4 to 32.1 terrawatt-hours (TWh).

However, this excludes the energy demands from data centre projects already in the pipeline, which are expected to be excessive, based on the ‘cooling’ requirement for servers.

Two planned projects in WA, the Hazelmere data centre and a project in Maddington — both proposed by CDC — are expected to consume 4.3TWh a year in total (or on a single hot day, up to 550–590MW).

Velge said this would be “more than five times AEMO’s forecast for the entire sector, and nearly 40% of the total projected growth for the next decade”.

“With huge amounts of heat comes huge amounts of emissions, and heat which must be displaced with either water or with fans.

“So, the choice is between huge water usage or noise. Adding this much extra demand on the grid is bound to push the price of electricity much higher than it already is.”

Another concern is the lack of transparency around the Hazelmere project, with many questions remaining about how it might develop. CDC’s application, for example, refers to the planned building as “HA1”, which raises the question: should people be expecting a HA2?

Local residents have discovered that CDC has acquired the adjoining lots at 170 Bushmead Road and 40 and 50 Hazelmere Crescent, making a larger project down the track a real possibility, even if the acquisitions had not been included in the current application.

This meant that CDC could be using a “salami-slicing” approach, splitting the project into smaller units, so that its cumulative impacts can’t be assessed as a whole.

In any case, Gwen argued that data centre projects should be approached like mining ones.

“Treating data centres like mining projects means applying our Mining Policy Principles: the right of affected communities to veto, assessment of cumulative impacts not just project by project assessments and a meaningful test of whether the project serves communities and the transition or if it serves private profits....

“We shouldn’t let ourselves be priced out of our own public utilities to release more carbon emissions and more heat into our globally warming atmosphere.

“As we know from the US, data centres are also an opportunity to rally people from all walks of life and all political stripes around something everyone opposes — a genuinely positive sight in the polarising times we live in.

“The numbers don’t add up. People and ecosystems …

author: Sarah Raymundo
title: No red carpet for empire: State repression and the fight against Pax Silica
content:
Kampuhan Kontra Pax Silica, a UP Diliman-based formation, together with progressive groups, students, faculty members, and rights advocates hold an indignation protest along Katipunan Avenue in Quezon City on November 15, 2026. Photo by Carlo Manalansan/Bulatlat

At the center of this escalation is Pax Silica, Washington’s emerging high-tech, resource-intensive war infrastructure. If NATO is the military apparatus built to fight U.S.-led wars, Pax Silica is the pre-war supply chain alliance designed to sustain them.

6,000-strong at Liwasang Bonifacio alone—and the numbers continue to surge as protesters march toward the PICC as U.S. President Donald Trump sets foot on Philippine soil. For over a century, U.S. imperialism has plundered this territory and oppressed its people, dating back to how it usurped the Katipunan’s hard-won 1896 triumph over Spanish colonialism. This is not the first time the Filipino people have fiercely rejected a Trump visit; they rose in protest during the ASEAN Summit in November 2017, and they are rising again.

The Filipino public’s refusal to welcome Trump—standing in sharp contrast to the Marcos Jr. administration’s eagerness to accommodate Washington—cannot justify the sweeping crackdown on activists exercising their fundamental rights to assembly, expression, and association. International observers have been alarmed by the scale and intensity of police brutality under Marcos Jr., which echoes the state terror unleashed over half a century ago under the U.S.-backed Martial Law dictatorship of Ferdinand Marcos Sr.—a regime only toppled in 1986 after a protracted, heroic struggle against U.S. imperialism and its client-dictator.

Yet this violence is not merely a nostalgic return to his father’s Martial Law era; it is the continuation of an unbroken war against the poor. In the Philippine countryside, landless peasants live in a state of perpetual siege, battered by recurring tiempo muerto (dead seasons), massacres, and state-backed counterinsurgency campaigns that target cooperative leaders and their families. In the cities, whenever public anger boils over—such as during last year’s mass anti-corruption demonstrations—state repression falls hardest on patriotic youth—students and urban poor—the very demographics with the greatest stake in systemic change.

At the center of this escalation is Pax Silica, Washington’s emerging high-tech, resource-intensive war infrastructure. If NATO is the military apparatus built to fight U.S.-led wars, Pax Silica is the pre-war supply chain alliance designed to sustain them. Before a single bomb is dropped, it secures the physical pillars of modern warfare and artificial intelligence—water, energy grids, land, and semiconductor supply chains—within allied borders. Designated as the United States’ key strategic ally in Asia, the Philippines is being positioned as a primary resource frontline.

The lethal purpose of Pax Silica’s weaponry and intelligence apparatus is already on full display in Palestine—one of its primary targets, and the sharpest expression of a settler colonialism that never stops settling. As this colonial project expands, so too does the global infrastructure required to endlessly reproduce the war machine. That relentless reproduction of war stands in stark, irreconcilable opposition to the social reproduction of human life and labor. This is precisely why the Filipino working poor and youth are determined to junk Pax Silica and reject the presence of a war criminal like Trump. For us Filipinos, defiance against this weaponized interdependence is an imperative of national self-defense.

In oppressed nations like the Philippines, where the people are actively working to resolve their primary contradiction against U.S. imperialism, defending the social reproduction of life and labor inevitably requires taking to the streets. When protesters march despite knowing they will face state violence and police brutality, it is not because they invite harm or court repression; rather, it is how the peoples of oppressed nations shed the illusions of safety and docility under U.S. imperialist diktat. Only by confronting that violence do we reclaim our dignity—a dignity rooted in land, national patrimony, solidarity, and the camaraderie in struggle that Filipinos have always been proud of and known for.

This collective resolve has deep historical roots. From the basic masses and Indigenous Peoples to professionals, students, cultural …

author: Pip Hinman
title: NSW Labor goes full tilt to support coal
content:
As Yasmin Catley, police minister and NSW Labor MP for Swansea, in the Hunter, continues to rail about a climate protest she had wanted to ban, NSW Labor is rushing through a pro-coal bill which critics say undermines a recent federal High Court ruling.

The Paddle for the Planet, organised by Rising Tide, drew around 1000 people to Horseshoe Beach in Muloobinba/Newcastle on November 14. The protest was designed to highlight Australia’s lack of leadership at the COP31 climate summit in Türkiye.

Its attendance was boosted by NSW Labor’s last-ditch undemocratic attempts to prevent it from going ahead. This included Premier Chris Minns’ direct intervention into Newcastle City Council, demanding it ban Rising Tide and, shockingly, “associates, subsidiaries, other groups and individuals” from holding events or protests on council land.

The motion only passed with the casting vote of independent Mayor Gavin Morris, after Labor councillor Declan Clausen crossed the floor to support the ban.

But the NSW Supreme Court’s decision to favour individuals’ right to peacefully express themselves knocked NSW Police’s efforts to ban the protest on its head.

At least 800 people took to the water in canoes and kayaks on a calm and sunny day. There was not one NSW Police officer in sight — nor any coal ships.

Climate activists occupied the channel for an hour to make their views known about Labor’s pretense over its commitment to the climate while approving new coal and gas projects.

Even after the peaceful event, Catley continued to rail against the climate activists for being “reckless” and “dangerous for everybody”.

Meanwhile, Cately and Minns are pushing a new pro-coal bill, favouring MACH Energy, which aims to circumvent a High Court decision on that company’s mine in the Hunter Valley.

The Environmental Defenders’ Office (EDO) described the Mount Pleasant Mine Bill 2026 bill, which went to parliament on November 10, as “eroding the rule of law, the separation of powers and public trust in independent decision-making”.

The bill, which Labor wants to push through this week, authorises MACH Energy to continue mining thermal coal at Mount Pleasant until 2032 (up to 16.5 million tonnes).

The EDO said not only does it override the pending process and decision of the Land and Environment Court of NSW, following the High Court decision, it contains a dangerously broad clause which allows the Planning Minister to be the consent authority for the approval, not the Independent Planning Commission. It would circumvent parliamentary scrutiny.

Jacqui Mumford, Nature Conservation Council NSW (NCC) CEO, said this “would give the Resources Minister unfettered power to override all other laws in relation to the Mount Pleasant coal mine” adding, “this kind of power is a major corruption risk”. She said such a law “would take NSW back to the days of [disgraced Labor MP] Eddie Obeid by bypassing independent assessments and public consultation”.

Labor’s talking points about “protecting jobs” at the Mount Pleasant mine are also being challenged.

While the bill contains a “jobs guarantee”, to which mining corporations must agree, the Denman Aberdeen Muswellbrook Scone Healthy Environment Group (DAMSHEG) pointed out that Labor has not shown a commitment to coal workers at Mount Pleasant, as most are on insecure labour hire contracts.

Labor signed off on a transition authority and investment fund which are supposed to support workers wanting to leave the fossil fuel industry. But with no dedicated funding figure in the Future Jobs and Investment Fund, it remains abstract.

Retired Supreme Court judge Anthony Whealy and barrister and anti-corruption campaigner Geoffrey Watson have publicly criticised NSW Labor over its new coal bill. “I think it’s disgraceful,” Watson, a director at the Centre for Public Integrity and former senior counsel assisting the NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption, told The Guardian on October 21.

“This is, in effect, to overturn a decision of the high court of Australia after a fair hearing. In my book it’s contrary to the separation of powers which acknowledges that each branch of government has its own area or domain.”

Whealy told the ABC on October 20 that the government’s bill is “reprehensible” because it “obliterates” the legal process.

“With an election early in 2027, such matters do not seem to phase NSW Labor, which seems more singularly concerned about winning votes back from One Nation in coal …

title: Feds, Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami set to announce Inuit child initiative
content:
The federal government is set to make an announcement regarding Inuit children Wednesday in Ottawa.


According to a notification sent Tuesday, Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty will be joined by Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami President Natan Obed.


No details about the announcement were shared in the notification.


A recent report on food security in Nunavut said that

70 per cent of children in the territory

 live in a household where parents or caregivers are “skipping meals, eating less, and/or eating lower quality food to make ends meet.”


Authors of the report characterized the situation as a “food security crisis.”


According to the report, Inuit children aged two to five have been found to have lower hemoglobin levels and are likelier to have anemia since the federal government cancelled the Hamlet Food Voucher program.


In its pre-budget request, the ITK, which represents approximately 70,000 Inuit in Canada, sought a permanent $120-million annual replacement for the Inuit Child First Initiative, a program that ensures “Inuit children have access to the essential health, social and educational products, services and supports they need, when they need them.”


The budget did offer the Inuit Child First Initiative / Piratsiagutiit program $575 million over five years.


APTN News will carry the news conference live at 10:45 a.m. ET.

author: Keelan Jacobs
title: First Nations are passing laws to protect their communities, but who will enforce them?
content:
First Nations leaders and legal experts are pressing the federal government to address a longstanding gap in Canada’s justice system. They say while First Nations have the authority to make their own laws, enforcing and prosecuting violations of those laws remains a significant challenge.


The issue took centre stage Tuesday at the 2026

National Conference on the Future of Enforcement of First Nations Laws

 in Gatineau, Que., where discussions focused on the responsibilities of federal and provincial governments, including the RCMP, to recognize and enforce First Nations laws.


At the centre of the discussions are two pieces of federal legislation sponsored by Sen. Mary Jane McCallum. Bill S-223 is proposing amendments to the Royal Canadian Mounted Police Act, and Bill S-224, which is proposing amendments to the Director of Public Prosecutions Act.


For Chief Robert Louie of Westbank First Nation, who moderated Tuesday’s conference discussions, the proposed legislation represents a straightforward but significant step toward recognizing First Nations jurisdiction.


“These are very straightforward things and the federal government can easily do that very simply,” Louie said.


He said the proposed amendments would clarify the RCMP’s responsibilities in enforcing First Nations laws while establishing mechanisms to ensure those laws can be prosecuted.


As of Tuesday, Bill S-223 had been reported back from Senate committee without amendments and was awaiting third reading. Bill S-224 remained before the Senate Standing Committee on Legal and Constitutional Affairs.


The enforcement gap


The ability to create laws does not necessarily mean First Nations have access to the police, prosecutors and courts required to enforce them.


First Nations may rely on the RCMP or provincial police services to investigate alleged violations. However, inconsistent enforcement, limited resources and difficulties accessing prosecution services can leave communities facing significant barriers.


The result is a fragmented system in which First Nations may have the authority to establish laws but lack the institutional support to ensure they are respected.


Meko Nicholas, executive director of the First Nations Lands Management Resource Centre, said the consequences can be particularly costly when communities attempt to enforce housing and tenancy laws.


“As an example, just to evict someone who stopped paying their rent, usually non-band members,” Nicholas said. “If there is somebody who didn’t pay their rent, you’re out right? But that doesn’t happen on reserves.”


Nicholas was describing the additional legal and financial barriers First Nations can encounter when trying to enforce laws that would ordinarily be addressed through established provincial or municipal legal processes.


Louie said private prosecutions can become prohibitively expensive, placing an unfair financial burden on First Nations.


“It should be fair and reasonable, just like it is everywhere else in the country,” he said.


Manitoba Senator Mary Jane McCallum, seen here speaking with a reporter from The Canadian Press at her East Block office on Parliament Hill in 2023, tabled Bill S-223 in the Senate. Photo: Spencer Colby/The Canadian Press.


Two bills, one unresolved question


Bill S-223 seeks to clarify RCMP responsibilities concerning the enforcement of First Nations laws, including preventing offences and executing warrants lawfully issued under those laws.


Bill S-224 addresses prosecution, proposing a mechanism for the federal Director of Public Prosecutions to prosecute summary conviction offences under First Nations laws on behalf of the First Nation that enacted them, subject to the bill’s provisions.


The distinction is important. Police enforcement and prosecution are separate functions. Without the ability to investigate, lay charges where appropriate and prosecute alleged violations, First Nations laws can be difficult to enforce in practice.


Louie said federal, provincial and territorial governments must recognize their responsibility to support First Nations jurisdiction.


“The federal, provincial and territorial governments need to understand and back up with clarity that enforcement is a necessity and they must stand behind First Nations and enforce the law,” he said.


Nicholas acknowledged some progress through federal funding, particularly from Indigenous Services Canada and Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs …

author: Charlotte Morritt-Jacobs
title: While addiction treatment ends, recovery doesn’t, so N.W.T. residents want continuation of care
content:
Maria Hajcik spent roughly 20 years struggling with her addiction in Yellowknife. When she returned home after receiving treatment in Calgary, she had nowhere to go.


“I couldn’t go to my mom’s house and I couldn’t go somewhere that I knew because I was so vulnerable and so scared,” Hajcik said. “I was frightened that I’d get back into the same old things.”


Hajcik has now been clean and sober for 13 years. She is the community and wellness supervisor at the Tree of Peace Friendship Centre in Yellowknife, where she supports people dealing with active addiction and those in recovery.


Her lived experience shapes how she approaches the work. For Hajcik, getting someone into a treatment facility is only one part of recovery. What happens when they return home is equally important.


“If there’s no aftercare, there’s nothing,” Hajcik said. “If people go to treatment and they come back and there’s nothing to do afterwards, they’ll get back into the same old routine, the same old people, the same old lifestyle that they know.”


A central part of activities for National Addictions Awareness Week include conversations on how substance use does not happen in isolation, and recovery can involve addressing the experiences and circumstances that contribute to it. Photo: Charlotte Morritt-Jacobs/APTN.


Hajcik was among those taking part in a wellness walk hosted by the Tree of Peace for

National Addictions Awareness Week

. The event brought together people in recovery, friends and community members to share messages of support and raise awareness about addiction in the North.


For Hajcik, there is no single approach to recovery. She said treatment must be individualized.


“Every person is different when they’re coming off whatever substance you’re using because of their trauma, because of the way that they were raised, because of who they hung around,” she said. “Even if they’re on the same drug, in my experience, every person that walks into my office is different.”


To access territorially funded treatment facilities in southern Canada, such as Aventa, Fresh Start, Sunrise Healing Lodge, Renasant and Cedars Recovery, residents must complete an application package with an authorized referral provider, such as the Tree of Peace.


Hajcik helps clients evaluate their options and connect with appropriate services. She says the Tree of Peace takes a harm-reduction approach, meaning people are supported at different stages of recovery rather than being expected to make every change at once.


“Abstinence is part of the harm reduction,” she said. “If people need to just move slowly and gradually into abstinence-based, that’s fine.”


Hajcik says the approach means supporting people without imposing expectations on what their recovery should look like.


“That’s what harm reduction is, is actually being there for the person as a whole and not telling them what I think they should be doing,” she said.


The Tree of Peace also offers a 21-day on-the-land program at an established wellness camp in a forested area of Yellowknife. Hajcik says participants can receive three months of aftercare following the program, with continued support available through the community wellness team.


“Treatment is for discovery and afterwards is for recovery,” she said. “Recovery doesn’t end. Neither does addiction.”


Participants of a wellness walk in Yellowknife carry a National Addictions Awareness Week banner and hand-made signs put the emphasis on support, belonging and the role community can play in recovery. Photo: Charlotte Morritt-Jacobs/APTN.


Stigma can keep people from seeking help


Darlene Lebrun has been sober for three years. She says her drinking brought her close to death and led to hospitalization.


She credits her family as her biggest source of support, but says she also had to reach a point where she was ready to ask for help herself.


For Lebrun, asking for help was one of the hardest steps.


“What an addict can do is look in yourself to actually seek help and ask for it,” she said. “That’s the toughest thing that anybody can actually do for themselves is ask for help.”


Lebrun says she chose not to attend a treatment centre that operated in the N.W.T. because she knew the people running it and worried others in the community would find out about her addiction.


“It’s such a stigma to be an addict and I always thought people would look down at me or belittle me because of my addiction,” she said. “What I’ve learned …

author: Sara Connors
title: Chief in Yukon raises alarm over looming Parks Canada job cuts
content:
The chief of a First Nation in Yukon is raising concerns about potential staffing cuts at Parks Canada and how they could impact the First Nation’s co-management agreement with the federal agency.


“We are concerned about it, but we don’t know what the implications of this are because we haven’t had that kind of discussion yet,” said Kluane First Nation Chief Bob Dickson.


The First Nation co-manages

Kluane National Park and Reserve

 — one of three national parks in the territory — along with Parks Canada and the Champagne and Aishihik First Nations as part of its final agreement.


Dickson said he learned of the cuts one day before letters were sent to almost 3,000 Parks Canada staff across the country.


The cuts come amid federal belt-tightening, with plans to scrap the equivalent of 500 full-time jobs at the agency to save $145 million in spending over the next three years.


In the North, potential job cuts could sting especially hard.


In Yukon, 58 of 137 Parks Canada jobs are affected — about 42 per cent of its total workforce in the territory, according to the agency.


Dickson said it’s not yet clear how staffing cuts would impact the park’s co-management agreement and employment opportunities for the handful of Kluane citizens who mainly work there seasonally.


He also noted that the First Nation has worked to open a region of the park to citizens for commercial trapping, and that it’s unknown whether workforce reductions could disrupt those efforts.


“We’re still in the process of trying to figure out what does this really mean for us, because we have the management plan, right? And also, we have citizens who are employed there, right? So, we haven’t got all the answers yet,” he said.


Kluane First Nation Chief Bob Dickson says he has concerns over potential Parks Canada job cuts and how they might impact the Kluane National Park and Reserve, which the First Nation helps co-manage. Photo: Jordan Haslbeck/APTN News


Warden detachment to be scrapped


Kluane park’s warden detachment is also on the chopping block.


Responsible for the park’s law enforcement, including protecting species at risk, patrolling and helping educate visitors, the detachment is one of 13 across the country slated for closure.


Instead, services will be centralized in Yellowknife.


Dickson fears losing on-the-ground enforcement could jeopardize park management, including monitoring illegal hunting and safeguarding wildlife like sheep, which he said are vulnerable to vehicle collisions.


“We do have concerns over who’s going to be patrolling the park and how do you manage all of the travellers in the park if we don’t have a warden on site that can do that, right?” he said. “How is that going to be controlled?”


Thechàl Dhâl, or Sheep Mountain, which is located within the Kluane National Park and Reserve in southwest Yukon. Photo: Jordan Haslbeck/APTN News


Parks Canada promises to uphold agreements


According to Parks Canada, it will continue to uphold its cooperative management agreements with Indigenous governments as organizational changes take effect.


Spokesperson Charlotte Bordeleau said in a statement to APTN News that “cooperative management and shared governance arrangements will continue to shape how Parks Canada operates going forward.”


“Our commitment to a network of national heritage places that recognizes and honours the stewardship, histories, cultures, and contributions of Indigenous Peoples remains strong. Strengthening relationships with Indigenous Peoples continues to be central to our reconciliation efforts,” she said.


The issue has also raised concerns among government officials and concerned citizens.


Yukon MLAs passed a unanimous motion earlier this month

urging the federal government to maintain current staffing levels.


St. Elias Chamber of Commerce president Michael Pealow is similarly leading a

petition

 against the cuts, which has garnered nearly 8,700 signatures.


Dickson said his First Nation will be meeting with Parks Canada and hopes to provide input before final decisions are made.


He said it’s important that his people have a voice at the table.


“The last thing we want is others to be telling the story of Kluane First Nation when they are in the park or accessing the park,” he said.


Parks Canada said it will finalize decisions on all positions being assessed in the coming weeks.

Chief in Yukon raises alarm over looming Parks Canada job cuts

title: Μαζικές διαδηλώσεις για την επέτειο του Πολυτεχνείου σε Αθήνα και Θεσσαλονίκη (φωτορεπορτάζ & video)
content:
Μαζικές διαδηλώσεις για την επέτειο του Πολυτεχνείου σε Αθήνα και Θεσσαλονίκη (φωτορεπορτάζ & video).


Αθήνα


Δεκάδες χιλιάδες άνθρωποι έδωσαν και φέτος το παρόν στους δρόμους της πρωτεύουσας τιμώντας τη μνήμη της εξέγερσης του Πολυτεχνείου. 53 χρόνια μετά από εκείνον τον Νοέμβρη του 1973, η εξέγερση συνεχίζει να εμπνέει και να αποτελεί σημείο αναφοράς στους σημερινούς αγώνες. Ο λαός της Αθήνας κατέκλυσε το κέντρο της Αθήνας στην καθιερωμένη πορεία προς την αμερικάνικη πρεσβεία. Τις προηγούμενες μέρες είχε σπάσει ντε φάκτο η απαγόρευση του πρύτανη του ΕΜΠ με την

κατάληψη του κτηρίου Γκίνη και το άνοιγμα της πύλης στη Στουρνάρη

.


Πιστή στο ραντεβού της κι η ΕΛ.ΑΣ. Για ακόμη μια φορά έδωσε ρεσιτάλ αποκτήνωσης και χυδαιότητας. Στο τέλος της πορείας τα κορδόνια των ΜΑΤ απαγόρευσαν στον κόσμο που συμμετείχε στα αναρχικά/αντιεξουσιαστικά μπλοκ να διαλυθεί προς την πλατεία Μαβίλη και τον ωθούσαν προς τη λεωφόρο Αλεξάνδρας. Εκεί τα ΜΑΤ επιτέθηκαν αναίτια, τραυματίζοντας σοβαρά 4 γυναίκες στο κεφάλι. Τουλάχιστον μια κοπέλα χτυπήθηκε με γκλοπ στο πίσω μέρος του κεφαλιού της.


https://www.alerta.gr/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/v-e-l-o-c-i-t-y-antireport-17-11-2026-Tonight：-the-moment-a-riot-cop—from-the-larges.mp4


Τα ΜΑΤ επιτέθηκαν επίσης μέσα στον σταθμό μετρό Αμπελοκήπων και έκαναν προσαγωγές στον σωρό μαζεύοντας κυρίως ανήλικους που φορούσαν μαύρα ρούχα.


Συνολικά έγιναν 15 προσαγωγές εκ των οποίων 2 μετατράπηκαν σε συλλήψεις. Αργά το βράδυ εκδόθηκε

κάλεσμα αλληλεγγύης στη ΓΑΔΑ

 για τους προσαχθέντες και συλληφθέντες της πορείας.


Θεσσαλονίκη


Πάνω από 10 χιλιάδες άτομα ανταποκρίθηκαν στα

καλέσματα

 φοιτητικών συλλόγων και σχημάτων, εργατικών σωματείων, κομμάτων και οργανώσεων της Αριστεράς και οργανώσεων και συλλογικοτήτων του αναρχικού/αντιεξουσιαστικού χώρου. Η πορεία, ξεκινώντας από την Πολυτεχνική Σχολή ΑΠΘ, διέσχισε όλο το κέντρο της Θεσσαλονίκης μέσω των οδών Εθνικής Αμύνης, Τσιμισκή, Βενιζέλου και Εγνατία ενώ κατέληξε στο άγαλμα Βενιζέλου. Καθ’ όλη τη διάρκεια τα αναρχικά/αντιεξουσιαστικά μπλοκ ήταν περικυκλωμένα από ισχυρές δυνάμεις των ΜΑΤ αλλά και από δεκάδες μαυροφορεμένους και κουκουλοφόρους ασφαλίτες που έφεραν σακίδια. Ένα φαινόμενο που επαναλαμβάνεται σε κάθε μεγάλη πορεία. Μετά το τέλος της πορείας μικροεπεισόδια ξέσπασαν στη Ρωμαϊκή Αγορά με δυνάμεις της ΕΛ.ΑΣ. να περικυκλώνουν και να αποκλείουν την περιοχή για παραπάνω από μια ώρα.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: As Congress Debates Ending Iran War, Trump Sends a Third Aircraft Carrier
content:
CENTCOM announced on Tuesday that it had carried out more strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

A third U.S. aircraft carrier with thousands of U.S. troops has arrived in the Middle East to support the Iran war, U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) announced on Monday, adding to the U.S.’s arsenal in the area as President Donald Trump keeps his options open for escalating the war.

The USS Theodore Roosevelt arrived in the area on Sunday, joining two other aircraft carriers, each with roughly 5,000 soldiers and dozens of fighter jets aboard, and about 20 other warships.

The carrier’s arrival comes as the U.S. continues its war on Iran with a naval blockade of Iranian ports, a sanctions campaign, and strikes. Reuters reported that the U.S. carried out a new round of airstrikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island on Tuesday. Iran began firing back on U.S. assets in the region in recent days after reports found earlier this month that the U.S. has been secretly attacking Qeshm for weeks, despite President Donald Trump saying at the time that “we haven’t been doing any fighting for months.”

Since then, Trump has said that the war is “militarily effectively over” and that he’s aiming to maintain “the status quo.” The status quo does still include U.S. military activity, and analysts have warned that inaction by Congress to force a withdrawal is stretching the conflict into a forever war.

Further, the arrival of the new aircraft carrier, which left its base in San Diego in September, gives Trump access to a massive amount of military might in the region that he could use at any time.

Reuters reported on Sunday that Trump has been telling allies that he may hold off on attacks if the U.S. doesn’t face new attacks from Iran or Houthi, or Ansar Allah, militants in Yemen. In public comments, he has indeed preferred to say that the war is winding down or is over.

However, Reuters, citing current and former U.S. officials, also noted that “Trump has alternated between threats of escalating the war with new strikes and winding down hostilities, and current and former officials say he does not appear ‌to have made up his mind about how to resolve the unpopular conflict.”

Trump has reportedly been calling around to regional allies, like Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Tayyip ​Erdogan, apparently telling bin Salman in October that he was planning to resume intense attacks after the midterm elections. Both allies apparently asked him not to intensify strikes again.

Though the temperamental commander-in-chief may conduct a devastating campaign in Iran any time, Democrats in Congress who have pledged to end the war are dragging their feet on actually doing so. Though some progressives and Democrats have said that they plan to try to force a defunding of the war through the next government spending package, which is due December 11, others have said that they don’t want to risk a shutdown in order to end the war that killed roughly 3,500 Iranians as of July.

At the same time, lengthy deployments for U.S. soldiers on the aircraft carriers in the Middle East are overstretching the Navy, as reports have found that sailors have faced extreme hardship while on board, including a lack of food and a spike in suicidal ideation and attempts.

However, Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao downplayed these concerns during his Senate confirmation hearing on Tuesday. Cao said that sailors who reported losing weight while deployed were just picky, “like my kids.” He said that the reported eight suicide attempts from the USS Abraham Lincoln earlier this year were not suicide attempts, but “eight suicide mitigations.”

Cao also displayed a complete disregard for basic facts about the costs of the war. Cao said he doesn’t know what the U.S.’s naval blockade on Iranian ports is costing daily in another line of questioning, and that Pentagon inspectors have still yet to fully assess damage to naval bases in the Middle East that were struck by Iran earlier in the war.

title: Six lawyers detained in raids in Izmir
content:
Six lawyers were detained during a police operation in the western Turkish city of Izmir on Tuesday morning. Five of them are members of the Contemporary Lawyers’ Association (ÇHD). According to the organization, the lawyers were taken into custody during searches of their homes in the early morning hours.


Those detained include Veysi Çetin, secretary of the ÇHD’s Izmir branch, as well as association members Yemen Cankan, Emrah Kanbay, Göksel Akbaba and Erdoğan Akdoğdu. Lawyer Bahattin Özdemir was also detained.


According to the ÇHD, police seized electronic devices and data storage media during the house searches. Access to the investigation file has also been restricted. The detained lawyers have reportedly been unable to exercise their right to consult with legal counsel.


The ÇHD views the detentions as part of a systematic policy of repression against social opposition movements. The authorities are attempting to criminalize the practice of law and intimidate independent defense lawyers, the association’s Izmir branch stated. “This attack on the right to legal defense is nothing more than an attempt by the government to cover up the violations of the law, arbitrary practices and human rights abuses it perpetrates through the judiciary,” the statement said.


The ÇHD announced that it would provide legal support throughout the proceedings against the six detainees and continue to resist restrictions on the right to legal defense.

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Says Nationwide Outages Are “Fine” as More Systems Go Down
content:
Two additional outages occurred after Trump’s comments, affecting the NSA and Apple products.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

President Donald Trump appeared to downplay the nationwide outages that have affected millions of Americans over the past week, suggesting they aren’t anything to worry about.

In remarks to reporters in the Philippines on Tuesday, Trump indicated that he had spoken to Chase executives about one of the latest outages, which affected banking services for Chase, U.S. Bank, and Wells Fargo. When reporters asked Trump whether he was concerned about the outages, the president said he wasn’t worried.

“It’s life. When you’re big and powerful, and you have all of the money, things like that happen. It’s fine,” he said.

Q: Have you spoken tothe banks regarding the outage at Chase?TRUMP: I haveQ: What are they saying?T: It's going to be very much under controlQ: Are you concerned about these outages?T: No. It's life. When you're big & powerful & have all the money, things like this happen. It's fine

Trump’s response is unlikely to calm the fears of millions of Americans, some of whom may be wondering if the outages are connected in some way. So far, there is nothing to indicate that, or that any of the outages are the result of cyberattacks.

Shortly after Trump’s comments, another outage was reported, this time affecting the National Security Agency (NSA). According to sources speaking to CNN, the agency’s internal communications system used to transmit classified information, called NSA Net, had gone down. The sources added that there was no reason to believe the outage had been caused by a cyberattack, and that it did not affect the NSA’s ability to continue informing Trump about national security matters.

Another source told The New York Times that NSA Net has been unstable for weeks.

Beyond the banks and the NSA, other outages have included problems with Microsoft products reported by users worldwide, which occurred on Thursday. Perhaps most notably, on Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) grounded all domestic flights for several hours, citing communications and radar errors that were later revealed to have been caused by the replacement of a copper-wired router connection at a facility in Arkansas. Flights have yet to resume at normal operating speeds at airports across the country, with some delays and cancellations still occurring.

Later on Tuesday, thousands of users worldwide reported problems accessing Apple services, including iCloud, Apple Pay, the App Store, and Apple Support. The issue with those products was ongoing as of 2 pm Eastern Time, according to reporting from DownDetector.

title: Sebahat Tuncel: Silencing the guns is not enough; rights must be guaranteed
content:
The relationship between militarism, the climate crisis and ecological destruction was discussed during a session titled “Combating Militarism from a Climate Justice Perspective” at the Peoples’ Climate Summit in Antalya. The session addressed the environmental impact of military spending and armed conflicts, as well as opportunities for cooperation between the climate justice movement and antimilitarist movements.


Speaking at the session, Free Women’s Movement (TJA) activist Sebahat Tuncel highlighted the links between the climate crisis and the capitalist system, policies of exploitation, wars and repressive practices.


Tuncel stated that while government representatives at COP31 were discussing ways to maintain capitalism and the system of exploitation, the Peoples’ Climate Summit was exploring how to build an alternative way of life in opposition to these policies.


Sebahat Tuncel stated that the situation in Palestine could not be considered separately from the policies of repression and violence faced by peoples in other parts of the world. “The injustice, climate crisis, policies of war and policies of genocide we are witnessing in Palestine actually affect all peoples. Replace Palestine with Kurdistan. Similar policies are being pursued in Kurdistan as well. Think of the Alawites in Syria, or all the peoples in the Middle East who face repression because of their identity, faith or culture. Therefore, the struggle for climate justice is a struggle that concerns us all,” she said.


Emphasizing that wars cause not only loss of life but also ecological destruction, Tuncel stated that the situation in Palestine, Kurdistan and Lebanon concerned all of humanity. She said that policies of war and conflict devastated living environments and that the effects of the ecological crisis were not limited to those living in conflict zones.


‘Solidarity alone is not enough’


Sebahat Tuncel stated that policies of war erected barriers between societies and alienated peoples from one another, calling for a united struggle against these policies.


“The policy imposed on us by states is one of divide and rule. What we must do in response is unite and struggle together. Solidarity alone is not enough. We need to go beyond solidarity and build a common internationalist struggle to change and transform the male-dominated capitalist system. Only an organized society can achieve this,” Tuncel said.


Referring to the LGBTI+ movement’s slogan, “We exist, and we will continue to exist,” Tuncel stated that Kurds, women and people of different identities would also continue their struggle for existence. Describing the denial of peoples, identities and beliefs as fascism, she said that it brought with it repression, oppression, exploitation and marginalization.


‘Turkey has been turned into a giant prison’


Addressing prison policies in Turkey, Sebahat Tuncel stated that there were 16 prisons of various types in Antalya. She criticized the government for presenting the construction of new prisons as good news, describing it as a continuation of policies of repression and punishment.


Recalling the arrest of Kurdish politicians in 2009 as part of the KCK investigations, Tuncel said that those demanding rights, freedom, democracy and peace faced the threat of prosecution. Arguing that the law had been turned into a political instrument, Tuncel said, “They have turned Turkey into a giant prison.”


Tuncel argued that the isolation imposed on Abdullah Öcalan in İmralı had spread throughout Turkey and its prisons. “In fact, it has spread across the whole of Turkey and into every prison. There are not only prisons being built physically, but also prisons being constructed in our minds. We cannot achieve freedom without dismantling all these policies of isolation,” she said.


Tuncel emphasized that freedom could not be achieved without overcoming the policies of isolation, stating that freedom required a social order in which people could express their thoughts, organize and live with dignity.


Time to build positive peace


Addressing the Peace and Democratic Society Process, Sebahat Tuncel said that a struggle had been waged for many years to resolve the Kurdish question through democratic means rather than war and conflict.

title: Oil exports begin through Kirkuk–Ceyhan pipeline
content:
Iraq’s Ministry of Oil issued a statement announcing the resumption of oil exports through the Kirkuk–Ceyhan pipeline.


The statement confirmed that crude oil would be exported through the old pipeline between Iraq and Turkey, with an initial export volume of 120,000 barrels per day.


Export capacity is expected to increase gradually in the coming period, with plans to reach 500,000 barrels per day.


The ministry described the reactivation of the pipeline and the resumption of exports as a “strategic step,” stating that it would strengthen Iraq’s oil export capacity and help diversify the country’s oil export routes.


The statement emphasized that reopening this export route would provide an important source of additional revenue and support the Iraqi economy.

title: Women’s Justice and Memory Vigil in Amed: Stories of seven women shared
content:
At the “Women’s Justice and Memory Vigil” organized by the Network Against Violence outside the courthouse in Amed (tr: Diyarbakır), participants carried photographs of women who had been killed. Representatives of numerous political parties and civil society organizations attended the demonstration, chanting slogans including “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” (Woman, Life, Freedom), “Femicide is political” and “Stop protecting and exonerating perpetrators, prosecute them.”


Reading the statement on behalf of the organizers, Nermin Unat, a member of the Rosa Women’s Association, said that the stories of seven women who lost their lives in different cities between November 9 and 15 had been added to the collective memory. Unat emphasized that women who had been killed despite filing complaints and requesting protection, as well as those whose families were still seeking justice, would not be forgotten.


The women whose stories were shared this week included Pelin Pınar and Nuran Tay, who died after falling from balconies in Istanbul, Rukiye Demirel, who lost her life in Niğde, and Sema Gündüz, who died in Uşak. The stories of Aysel Sakaldaş, who was stabbed to death by her former husband in the Bayramiç district of Çanakkale; Ayşen Güneş, who was found dead in her home in the Elbistan district of Maraş; and Hanife K., who was shot dead by her husband in the Suluova district of Amasya, were also read aloud.


Speaking at the vigil, Amed Metropolitan Municipality Co-Mayor Serra Bucak said that activities organized as part of the November 25 International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women aimed to prevent further femicides.


Calling on the government to review its policies and take into account the efforts of local administrations to prevent violence against women, Bucak stated that 16 femicides had been officially recorded in Amed in 2026. She also drew attention to suspicious deaths of women, emphasizing the need to investigate these cases and hold those responsible accountable. “We will never give up demanding accountability,” Bucak said.


The vigil concluded with chants following a silent protest.
